vocab.exampleEn: It's hard to put a stop to the spread of misinformation.

vocab.note: Also one's own wife in some dialects and casual talk ({嫁|よめ}さん). Some people avoid the word because it suggests the wife joins the husband's family.
vocab.example: しゅうとめと{嫁|よめ}の{関係|かんけい}は、ドラマの{定番|ていばん}だ。
vocab.exampleEn: The relationship between mother-in-law and daughter-in-law is a staple of TV dramas.

meanings: to marry into (a family, said of the bride)
vocab.note: Group 1. ます form: {嫁|とつ}ぎます; て form: {嫁|とつ}いで. 〜に{嫁|とつ}ぐ / 〜へ{嫁|とつ}ぐ. A little old-fashioned; neutral: {結婚|けっこん}する.
vocab.example: {娘|むすめ}が{嫁|とつ}いでから、{家|いえ}の{中|なか}が{静|しず}かになった。
vocab.exampleEn: Since our daughter married and left, the house has become quiet.

meanings: shifting (blame or costs onto someone else)
vocab.note: Also 〜する. {責任|せきにん}{転嫁|てんか}: passing the buck. {価格|かかく}に{転嫁|てんか}する: to pass costs on to prices.
vocab.example: {失敗|しっぱい}を{部下|ぶか}に{転嫁|てんか}するような{上司|じょうし}は{信頼|しんらい}されない。
vocab.exampleEn: A boss who shifts the blame for failures onto subordinates won't be trusted.

meanings: a bride's entry (into her husband's family)
vocab.note: Also 〜する. {嫁入|よめい}り{道具|どうぐ}: the household goods a bride used to bring.
vocab.example: {祖母|そぼ}の{嫁入|よめい}りの{日|ひ}は、{雪|ゆき}が{降|ふ}っていたそうだ。
vocab.exampleEn: It's said that it was snowing on the day my grandmother married into the family.

vocab.note: A younger brother's wife is {弟|おとうと}の{妻|つま} or {義理|ぎり}の{妹|いもうと}.
vocab.example: {兄嫁|あによめ}とは{年|とし}が{近|ちか}いので、{姉妹|しまい}のように{仲|なか}がいい。
vocab.exampleEn: My sister-in-law and I are close in age, so we get on like sisters.

vocab.note: Also 〜する. Law and official forms; in speech {結婚|けっこん}.
vocab.example: {婚姻届|こんいんとどけ}が{受理|じゅり}されて{初|はじ}めて、{法律|ほうりつ}{上|じょう}の{婚姻|こんいん}が{成立|せいりつ}する。
vocab.exampleEn: A marriage is legally established only once the registration form has been accepted.

vocab.note: {婚姻届|こんいんとどけ}を{出|だ}す: to register a marriage at the town office.
vocab.example: {二人|ふたり}は{記念日|きねんび}に{婚姻届|こんいんとどけ}を{出|だ}した。
vocab.exampleEn: The two of them submitted their marriage registration on their anniversary.

meanings: bond of fate (a tie that brings people together)
vocab.note: ご{縁|えん}, {縁|えん}がある, {縁|えん}を{切|き}る (to cut ties). Same kanji: {縁|ふち} (rim). Sounds like {円|えん} (yen).
vocab.example: これも{何|なに}かのご{縁|えん}ですから、どうぞよろしくお{願|ねが}いします。
vocab.exampleEn: This must be fate, so I look forward to working with you.

meanings: match (an offer of marriage made through others)
vocab.note: {縁談|えんだん}がまとまる: a match is agreed.
vocab.example: {親戚|しんせき}が{持|も}ってきた{縁談|えんだん}を、{姉|あね}はあっさり{断|ことわ}った。
vocab.exampleEn: My sister turned down the match a relative had brought without a second thought.

vocab.note: The narrow wooden floor outside the rooms, facing the garden.
vocab.example: {夏|なつ}の{夕方|ゆうがた}は、{縁側|えんがわ}でスイカを{食|た}べたものだ。
vocab.exampleEn: On summer evenings we used to eat watermelon on the veranda.

vocab.note: Also 〜する. Today {離婚|りこん} for a couple; {離縁|りえん} is also ending an adoption.
vocab.example: {昔|むかし}の{小説|しょうせつ}では、{離縁|りえん}された{女性|じょせい}が{実家|じっか}に{戻|もど}る{場面|ばめん}がよく{描|えが}かれる。
vocab.exampleEn: Old novels often show a woman who has been divorced returning to her parents' home.

vocab.note: {血縁|けつえん}{関係|かんけい}: blood relation.
vocab.example: {血縁|けつえん}がなくても、{家族|かぞく}は{家族|かぞく}だ。
vocab.exampleEn: Even without a blood tie, family is family.

meanings: matchmaking (bringing a couple together, as a shrine's blessing)
vocab.note: {縁結|えんむす}びの{神様|かみさま}: a god of love and marriage.
vocab.example: この{神社|じんじゃ}は{縁結|えんむす}びで{有名|ゆうめい}だ。
vocab.exampleEn: This shrine is famous for bringing couples together.

vocab.note: 〜とは{無縁|むえん}だ: has nothing to do with. Also {無縁|むえん}{墓地|ぼち}: graves no one tends.
vocab.example: {都会|とかい}の{暮|く}らしは、{近所|きんじょ}{付|づ}き{合|あ}いとは{無縁|むえん}だった。
vocab.exampleEn: City life had nothing to do with getting to know the neighbours.

vocab.note: {因縁|いんねん}の{対決|たいけつ}: a grudge match. {因縁|いんねん}をつける: to pick a quarrel. いん + えん → いんねん.
vocab.example: {両家|りょうけ}には、{古|ふる}くからの{因縁|いんねん}があるらしい。
vocab.exampleEn: There seems to be an old history between the two families.

vocab.note: 縁 read ふち becomes ぶち: がく + ふち → がくぶち.
vocab.example: {祖父|そふ}の{写真|しゃしん}を{額縁|がくぶち}に{入|い}れて{飾|かざ}った。
vocab.exampleEn: We put Grandfather's photo in a frame and displayed it.

meanings: to adore (look up to someone with affection)
vocab.note: Group 1. ます form: {慕|した}います; て form: {慕|した}って. Of students, juniors and children towards someone they love and respect. Passive {慕|した}われる (to be loved) is common.
vocab.example: {先生|せんせい}は{多|おお}くの{教|おし}え{子|ご}に{慕|した}われていた。
vocab.exampleEn: The teacher was loved by many former pupils.

meanings: yearning (deep, tender longing for someone, literary)
vocab.note: Also 〜する. Written: {亡|な}き{母|はは}への{思慕|しぼ}.
vocab.example: その{詩|し}には、{故郷|こきょう}への{思慕|しぼ}がにじんでいる。
vocab.exampleEn: That poem is suffused with longing for home.

meanings: fellowship (getting to know each other, at social events)
vocab.note: {親睦会|しんぼくかい}: a social gathering; {親睦|しんぼく}を{深|ふか}める.
vocab.example: {新入|しんにゅう}{社員|しゃいん}の{親睦|しんぼく}を{深|ふか}めるため、{食事会|しょくじかい}が{開|ひら}かれた。
vocab.exampleEn: A dinner was held to help the new employees get to know each other.

meanings: debt of gratitude (a kindness one owes)
vocab.note: {恩|おん}を{返|かえ}す, {恩|おん}に{着|き}る (to feel indebted), {恩|おん}をあだで{返|かえ}す (to bite the hand that feeds you; the kanji of あだ is outside the course list).
vocab.example: {育|そだ}ててもらった{恩|おん}は、{一生|いっしょう}{忘|わす}れない。
vocab.exampleEn: I'll never forget the debt I owe for being brought up.

vocab.note: Also 〜する. {鶴|つる}の{恩返|おんがえ}し: the folk tale "The Crane's Gratitude".
vocab.example: いつか{故郷|こきょう}に{恩返|おんがえ}しがしたい。
vocab.exampleEn: Someday I want to give something back to my hometown.

meanings: respected former teacher (to whom one owes much)
vocab.note: Said of one's own teacher, with gratitude.
vocab.example: {結婚式|けっこんしき}には{高校|こうこう}{時代|じだい}の{恩師|おんし}も{来|き}てくださった。
vocab.exampleEn: My old high-school teacher kindly came to the wedding too.

meanings: benefactor (someone to whom one owes a great deal)
vocab.note: {命|いのち}の{恩人|おんじん}: the person who saved one's life.
vocab.example: {倒|たお}れたとき{救急車|きゅうきゅうしゃ}を{呼|よ}んでくれた{人|ひと}は、{命|いのち}の{恩人|おんじん}だ。
vocab.exampleEn: The person who called an ambulance when I collapsed saved my life.

vocab.note: Held by graduating students and their parents.
vocab.example: {卒業式|そつぎょうしき}の{後|あと}、ホテルで{謝恩会|しゃおんかい}が{開|ひら}かれた。
vocab.exampleEn: After the graduation ceremony, a thank-you party for the teachers was held at a hotel.

vocab.note: Also as a な-adjective-like noun: {恩知|おんし}らずな{人|ひと}.
vocab.example: {世話|せわ}になった{人|ひと}を{悪|わる}く{言|い}うなんて、{恩知|おんし}らずにもほどがある。
vocab.exampleEn: Speaking ill of someone who helped you is the height of ingratitude.

meanings: being a good son or daughter (devotion to one's parents)
vocab.note: Also 〜する and as an adjective: {親孝行|おやこうこう}な{息子|むすこ}. Opposite: {親不孝|おやふこう}.
vocab.example: {親孝行|おやこうこう}したいときには{親|おや}はなし、とよく{言|い}われる。
vocab.exampleEn: People often say that by the time you want to repay your parents, they're gone.

meanings: filial piety (devotion to one's parents, formal)
vocab.note: Also 〜する. Sounds like N5's {高校|こうこう} (high school). Usually {親孝行|おやこうこう}.
vocab.example: {祖父|そふ}は{孝行|こうこう}を{何|なに}より{大切|たいせつ}にした{人|ひと}だった。
vocab.exampleEn: My grandfather was someone who valued devotion to his parents above all.

meanings: being a bad son or daughter (causing one's parents grief)
vocab.note: Also 〜する. {親|おや}より{先|さき}に{死|し}ぬのは{一番|いちばん}の{親不孝|おやふこう}だ.
vocab.example: {心配|しんぱい}ばかりかけて、{親不孝|おやふこう}な{息子|むすこ}だった。
vocab.exampleEn: I was a son who caused nothing but worry.

vocab.note: {姻戚|いんせき}{関係|かんけい}. In speech {親戚|しんせき}.
vocab.example: {両家|りょうけ}は{姻戚|いんせき}{関係|かんけい}にある。
vocab.exampleEn: The two families are related by marriage.

vocab.note: Medical and formal.
vocab.example: {妊娠中|にんしんちゅう}は、{胎児|たいじ}への{影響|えいきょう}を{考|かんが}えて{薬|くすり}を{選|えら}ぶ。
vocab.exampleEn: During pregnancy, medicines are chosen with the effect on the unborn baby in mind.

vocab.note: {紳士|しんし}{淑女|しゅくじょ}の{皆様|みなさま} (ladies and gentlemen); {紳士|しんし}{服|ふく} (menswear); {紳士的|しんしてき} (gentlemanly).
vocab.example: {祖父|そふ}は{誰|だれ}に{対|たい}しても{礼儀正|れいぎただ}しい{紳士|しんし}だった。
vocab.exampleEn: My grandfather was a gentleman, courteous to everyone.

vocab.note: Mostly in {紳士|しんし}{淑女|しゅくじょ}.
vocab.example: {舞踏会|ぶとうかい}には、{着飾|きかざ}った{紳士|しんし}{淑女|しゅくじょ}が{集|あつ}まった。
vocab.exampleEn: Ladies and gentlemen in their finest gathered at the ball.

meanings: master of the house (also husband, old-fashioned)
vocab.note: {亭主|ていしゅ}{関白|かんぱく}: a domineering husband. In the tea ceremony, the host.
vocab.example: うちの{亭主|ていしゅ}は、{休|やす}みの{日|ひ}も{朝早|あさはや}くから{庭|にわ}いじりをしている。
vocab.exampleEn: My husband potters about in the garden from early morning even on his days off.

vocab.note: Private rooms, traditional multi-course meals; used for business and family occasions.
vocab.example: {両家|りょうけ}の{顔合|かおあ}わせは、{老舗|しにせ}の{料亭|りょうてい}で{行|おこな}われた。
vocab.exampleEn: The first meeting of the two families was held at a long-established traditional restaurant.

vocab.note: Also as an adjective: {亭主関白|ていしゅかんぱく}な{夫|おっと}. Now mostly said critically or as a joke.
vocab.example: {父|ちち}は{亭主関白|ていしゅかんぱく}に{見|み}えて、{実|じつ}は{母|はは}に{頭|あたま}が{上|あ}がらない。
vocab.exampleEn: Father looks like the lord of the house, but in fact he's no match for Mother.

vocab.note: Group 1. ます form: {誓|ちか}います; て form: {誓|ちか}って. {愛|あい}を{誓|ちか}う, {神|かみ}に{誓|ちか}って (I swear to God).
vocab.example: {二人|ふたり}は{家族|かぞく}の{前|まえ}で、{永遠|えいえん}の{愛|あい}を{誓|ちか}った。
vocab.exampleEn: The two vowed eternal love in front of their families.

vocab.note: {誓|ちか}いを{立|た}てる (to make a vow), {誓|ちか}いを{破|やぶ}る. Sounds like N5's ちかい (near).
vocab.example: {二度|にど}と{遅刻|ちこく}しないという{誓|ちか}いは、{三日|みっか}で{破|やぶ}られた。
vocab.exampleEn: The vow never to be late again was broken within three days.

meanings: oath (sworn in public, as at a ceremony or in court)
vocab.note: Also 〜する. {選手|せんしゅ}{宣誓|せんせい}: the athletes' oath at a sports meeting. Sounds like {先生|せんせい} (teacher).
vocab.example: {大会|たいかい}は、{選手|せんしゅ}{代表|だいひょう}の{宣誓|せんせい}で{始|はじ}まった。
vocab.exampleEn: The tournament began with the athletes' representative taking the oath.

vocab.note: Also 〜する. {扶養|ふよう}{家族|かぞく}: dependants. Sounds like N3's {不要|ふよう} (unnecessary).
vocab.example: {両親|りょうしん}を{扶養|ふよう}しているので、{税金|ぜいきん}が{少|すこ}し{安|やす}くなる。
vocab.exampleEn: I support my parents, so my taxes are slightly lower.

meanings: relief (formal support for those in need)
vocab.note: Also 〜する. {相互|そうご}{扶助|ふじょ}: mutual aid.
vocab.example: {昔|むかし}の{村|むら}では、{相互|そうご}{扶助|ふじょ}が{暮|く}らしを{支|ささ}えていた。
vocab.exampleEn: In the villages of the past, mutual aid supported daily life.

meanings: to take over (a job or duties from someone)
vocab.note: Group 1. ます form: {引|ひ}き{継|つ}ぎます; て form: {引|ひ}き{継|つ}いで. {仕事|しごと}を{引|ひ}き{継|つ}ぐ. Noun: {引|ひ}き{継|つ}ぎ (a handover).
vocab.example: {父|ちち}が{始|はじ}めた{店|みせ}を、{今|いま}は{長女|ちょうじょ}が{引|ひ}き{継|つ}いでいる。
vocab.exampleEn: The eldest daughter now runs the shop her father started.

meanings: heir (to a family business or household)
vocab.note: Also spelled {跡継|あとつ}ぎ. {後継|あとつ}ぎがいない: there's no one to take over.
vocab.example: {後継|あとつ}ぎがいないため、{百年|ひゃくねん}{続|つづ}いた{旅館|りょかん}が{閉|と}じることになった。
vocab.exampleEn: With no one to take it over, the inn that had run for a hundred years is to close.

vocab.note: Usually printed 継母, but まま isn't a jōyō reading of 継, so the course writes it in kana. Formal written word: {継母|けいぼ}.
vocab.example: {昔話|むかしばなし}では、ままははは{意地悪|いじわる}な{役|やく}が{多|おお}い。
vocab.exampleEn: In folk tales, the stepmother is often the cruel one.

meanings: succession (to a title, tradition or throne)
vocab.note: Also 〜する: {伝統|でんとう}を{継承|けいしょう}する. Sounds like N2's {軽傷|けいしょう} (minor injury).
vocab.example: {伝統|でんとう}{工芸|こうげい}の{継承|けいしょう}が{危|あや}ぶまれている。
vocab.exampleEn: There are fears for the passing on of traditional crafts.

vocab.note: Also 〜する. {継続|けいぞく}は{力|ちから}なり: keeping at it is what makes you strong.
vocab.example: {契約|けいやく}を{継続|けいぞく}するかどうか、{来月|らいげつ}までに{決|き}めてください。
vocab.exampleEn: Please decide by next month whether to continue the contract.

vocab.note: {後継者|こうけいしゃ}{不足|ぶそく}: a shortage of successors.
vocab.example: {農家|のうか}の{後継者|こうけいしゃ}{不足|ぶそく}は{深刻|しんこく}だ。
vocab.exampleEn: The shortage of successors on farms is serious.

meanings: to inherit (a trait, tradition or property)
vocab.note: Group 1. ます form: {受|う}け{継|つ}ぎます; て form: {受|う}け{継|つ}いで. {親|おや}から{受|う}け{継|つ}いだ{性格|せいかく}.
vocab.example: {祖母|そぼ}から{受|う}け{継|つ}いだ{着物|きもの}を、{娘|むすめ}の{成人式|せいじんしき}で{着|き}せた。
vocab.exampleEn: I had my daughter wear the kimono I inherited from my grandmother for her coming-of-age ceremony.

meanings: to succeed to (a family business or name)
vocab.note: Group 1. ます form: {継|つ}ぎます; て form: {継|つ}いで. {家業|かぎょう}を{継|つ}ぐ, {父|ちち}の{跡|あと}を{継|つ}ぐ.
vocab.example: {兄|あに}が{家|いえ}を{継|つ}ぐと{思|おも}いきや、{継|つ}いだのは{末|すえ}っ{子|こ}の{私|わたし}だった。
vocab.exampleEn: Everyone thought my brother would take over the family, but it was me, the youngest, who did.

vocab.note: {宴会場|えんかいじょう}: a banquet hall.
vocab.example: {忘年会|ぼうねんかい}の{宴会|えんかい}は、{夜|よる}{遅|おそ}くまで{続|つづ}いた。
vocab.exampleEn: The year-end party went on until late at night.

vocab.note: Written; {祝|いわ}いの{席|せき} in speech.
vocab.example: {優勝|ゆうしょう}を{祝|いわ}う{祝宴|しゅくえん}が{盛大|せいだい}に{開|ひら}かれた。
vocab.exampleEn: A grand banquet was held to celebrate the victory.

vocab.note: {祝賀会|しゅくがかい}, {祝賀|しゅくが}{行事|ぎょうじ}.
vocab.example: {創立|そうりつ}{百周年|ひゃくしゅうねん}の{祝賀会|しゅくがかい}に{招待|しょうたい}された。
vocab.exampleEn: I was invited to the celebration of the hundredth anniversary of the founding.

meanings: happy event (a wedding or birth, formal)
vocab.note: Opposite: ちょうじ (a funeral or other sad occasion; its first kanji is outside the course list). Sounds like N3's けいじ (detective).
vocab.example: {慶事|けいじ}のお{祝|いわ}いには、{新|あたら}しいお{札|さつ}を{用意|ようい}するのが{礼儀|れいぎ}だ。
vocab.exampleEn: For gifts of money at happy occasions, it's good manners to prepare new banknotes.

meanings: to separate (by distance, time or a barrier)
vocab.note: Group 2. ます form: {隔|へだ}てます; て form: {隔|へだ}てて. {道|みち}を{隔|へだ}てて (across the road), {十年|じゅうねん}の{時|とき}を{隔|へだ}てて.
vocab.example: {川|かわ}を{隔|へだ}てて、{二|ふた}つの{村|むら}が{向|む}かい{合|あ}っている。
vocab.exampleEn: The two villages face each other across the river.

vocab.note: {間隔|かんかく}を{空|あ}ける. Sounds like N3's {感覚|かんかく} (sense).
vocab.example: {電車|でんしゃ}は{五分|ごふん}{間隔|かんかく}で{運転|うんてん}されている。
vocab.exampleEn: The trains run at five-minute intervals.

vocab.note: {隔週|かくしゅう}で, {隔週|かくしゅう}{土曜日|どようび}.
vocab.example: {実家|じっか}には{隔週|かくしゅう}で{顔|かお}を{出|だ}している。
vocab.exampleEn: I visit my parents' home every other week.

meanings: gap (difference in opinion, age or distance)
vocab.note: {意見|いけん}の{隔|へだ}たり, {世代|せだい}の{隔|へだ}たり.
vocab.example: {親子|おやこ}の{間|あいだ}には、{考|かんが}え{方|かた}に{大|おお}きな{隔|へだ}たりがあった。
vocab.exampleEn: There was a wide gap in outlook between parent and child.

vocab.note: な-adjective. {幼稚|ようち}な{考|かんが}え, {幼稚|ようち}な{言|い}い{訳|わけ}. Critical.
vocab.example: そんな{幼稚|ようち}な{言|い}い{訳|わけ}が{通|とお}ると{思|おも}っているのか。
vocab.exampleEn: Do you think such a childish excuse will work?

meanings: festival child (a child in a temple or festival procession)
vocab.note: Special reading. Children in costume walk in temple processions ({稚児|ちご}{行列|ぎょうれつ}).
vocab.example: お{寺|てら}の{祭|まつ}りで、{娘|むすめ}が{稚児|ちご}{行列|ぎょうれつ}に{参加|さんか}した。
vocab.exampleEn: My daughter walked in the children's procession at the temple festival.

vocab.note: For ages three to six; {保育園|ほいくえん} is a day nursery.
vocab.example: {幼稚園|ようちえん}の{送|おく}り{迎|むか}えは、{祖父|そふ}の{役目|やくめ}だ。
vocab.exampleEn: Taking the child to and from kindergarten is Grandfather's job.

vocab.note: {旧姓|きゅうせい}で{働|はたら}く: to keep using one's old name at work. Sounds like N2's {急性|きゅうせい} (acute).
vocab.example: {職場|しょくば}では、{結婚後|けっこんご}も{旧姓|きゅうせい}を{使|つか}っている。
vocab.exampleEn: At work I still use my maiden name after marriage.

vocab.note: Forms: {姓|せい} and {名|めい}. In speech {名字|みょうじ}. Sounds like N3's せい (fault).
vocab.example: {書類|しょるい}には、{姓|せい}と{名|めい}を{分|わ}けて{書|か}いてください。
vocab.exampleEn: Please write your surname and given name separately on the form.

vocab.note: Whether married couples should be allowed to keep separate surnames has long been debated in Japan.
vocab.example: {夫婦別姓|ふうふべっせい}をめぐっては、さまざまな{意見|いけん}がある。
vocab.exampleEn: There are many views on separate surnames for married couples.

vocab.note: {双子|ふたご}の{姉妹|しまい}. 双 read ふた.
vocab.example: {双子|ふたご}といえども、{性格|せいかく}はまったく{違|ちが}う。
vocab.exampleEn: They may be twins, but their personalities are completely different.

vocab.note: {双方|そうほう}の{意見|いけん}を{聞|き}く. In speech {両方|りょうほう}.
vocab.example: {話|はな}し{合|あ}いは、{双方|そうほう}が{譲|ゆず}らず{平行線|へいこうせん}に{終|お}わった。
vocab.exampleEn: Neither side gave way, and the talks ended with no meeting of minds.

vocab.note: {帯|おび}を{締|し}める. A paper band on a book with a blurb is also an {帯|おび}.
vocab.example: {着物|きもの}の{帯|おび}を{一人|ひとり}で{結|むす}ぶのは{難|むずか}しい。
vocab.exampleEn: Tying a kimono sash on your own is difficult.

meanings: household (as a unit in statistics and forms)
vocab.note: {単身|たんしん}{世帯|せたい} (one-person households), 〜{世帯|せたい} (counter). Older everyday word: {所帯|しょたい}.
vocab.example: {一人暮|ひとりぐ}らしの{高齢者|こうれいしゃ}{世帯|せたい}が{増|ふ}えている。
vocab.exampleEn: The number of elderly people living alone is rising.

vocab.note: この{一帯|いったい}, {関東|かんとう}{一帯|いったい}. Sounds like N3's いったい (what on earth).
vocab.example: {昔|むかし}はこの{一帯|いったい}が{田|た}んぼだった。
vocab.exampleEn: This whole area used to be rice paddies.

meanings: to take on (a tinge or quality)
vocab.note: Group 2. ます form: {帯|お}びます; て form: {帯|お}びて. {赤|あか}みを{帯|お}びる, {現実味|げんじつみ}を{帯|お}びる (to become real). Written.
vocab.example: {二人|ふたり}の{結婚|けっこん}の{話|はなし}が、{急|きゅう}に{現実味|げんじつみ}を{帯|お}びてきた。
vocab.exampleEn: Talk of the two getting married suddenly started to feel real.

vocab.note: {人生|じんせい}の{伴侶|はんりょ}. Written and in speeches.
vocab.example: {人生|じんせい}の{伴侶|はんりょ}に{出会|であ}えたことに{感謝|かんしゃ}している。
vocab.exampleEn: I'm grateful to have met my partner for life.

vocab.note: Also 〜する. {保護者|ほごしゃ}{同伴|どうはん}: accompanied by a parent or guardian.
vocab.example: {中学生|ちゅうがくせい}{以下|いか}は、{保護者|ほごしゃ}の{同伴|どうはん}が{必要|ひつよう}です。
vocab.exampleEn: Children of junior high school age and younger must be accompanied by a parent or guardian.

meanings: to accompany (go with, be a consequence of)
vocab.note: Group 1. ます form: {伴|ともな}います; て form: {伴|ともな}って. 〜を{伴|ともな}う: {危険|きけん}を{伴|ともな}う. N2's 〜にともなって is now 〜に{伴|ともな}って.
vocab.example: {結婚|けっこん}には、{喜|よろこ}びだけでなく{責任|せきにん}も{伴|ともな}う。
vocab.exampleEn: Marriage brings not only joy but responsibility.

vocab.note: Also 〜する: {土地|とち}を{譲渡|じょうと}する.
vocab.example: {父|ちち}は{生前|せいぜん}に、{土地|とち}の{一部|いちぶ}を{長男|ちょうなん}に{譲渡|じょうと}した。
vocab.exampleEn: While alive, Father transferred part of the land to his eldest son.

meanings: inherited from one's parents (a trait or possession)
vocab.note: {親譲|おやゆず}りの{頑固|がんこ}さ.
vocab.example: {負|ま}けず{嫌|ぎら}いなところは{父|ちち}{親譲|おやゆず}りだ。
vocab.exampleEn: My competitiveness comes from my father.

vocab.note: Also 〜する. The grammar term "concession" is {譲歩|じょうほ} in Japanese grammar books too.
vocab.example: {双方|そうほう}が{少|すこ}しずつ{譲歩|じょうほ}して、ようやく{合意|ごうい}した。
vocab.exampleEn: Both sides gave a little, and they finally reached agreement.

vocab.note: Also 〜する: {恋人|こいびと}を{束縛|そくばく}する (to be controlling).
vocab.example: {束縛|そくばく}の{強|つよ}い{相手|あいて}とは、{長|なが}く{付|つ}き{合|あ}えない。
vocab.exampleEn: I can't stay long with a partner who's very controlling.

meanings: to bind (tie with rope or string)
to tie up (with rope or string)
vocab.note: Group 1. ます form: {縛|しば}ります; て form: {縛|しば}って. {規則|きそく}に{縛|しば}られる: to be bound by rules.
vocab.example: {古新聞|ふるしんぶん}をひもで{縛|しば}って{出|だ}した。
vocab.exampleEn: I tied up the old newspapers with string and put them out.

vocab.note: Group 2. ます form: {慰|なぐさ}めます; て form: {慰|なぐさ}めて. Noun: {慰|なぐさ}め.
vocab.example: {泣|な}いている{妹|いもうと}を、{母|はは}は{黙|だま}って{抱|だ}きしめて{慰|なぐさ}めた。
vocab.exampleEn: Mother silently hugged my crying little sister to comfort her.

vocab.note: After a divorce, an accident or defamation. Sounds like {医者|いしゃ} + 料, but 慰 is comfort.
vocab.example: {離婚|りこん}の{際|さい}、{慰謝料|いしゃりょう}をめぐって{争|あらそ}いになった。
vocab.exampleEn: On their divorce, they fell into a dispute over compensation.

vocab.note: {慰|なぐさ}めの{言葉|ことば}, {何|なん}の{慰|なぐさ}めにもならない.
vocab.example: {祖母|そぼ}にとって、{孫|まご}の{手紙|てがみ}が{何|なに}よりの{慰|なぐさ}めだった。
vocab.exampleEn: For my grandmother, letters from her grandchildren were the greatest comfort.

meanings: birth (of a person or of something new)
vocab.note: Also 〜する: {新|あたら}しい{町|まち}が{誕生|たんじょう}した. {誕生日|たんじょうび} (carried).
vocab.example: {初孫|はつまご}の{誕生|たんじょう}を、{家族|かぞく}{全員|ぜんいん}で{祝|いわ}った。
vocab.exampleEn: The whole family celebrated the birth of the first grandchild.

vocab.note: Also read ふるさと (N3's word, also written {古里|ふるさと}).
vocab.example: {彼|かれ}は{四十年|よんじゅうねん}ぶりに{故郷|こきょう}の{土|つち}を{踏|ふ}んだ。
vocab.exampleEn: He set foot in his home town for the first time in forty years.

vocab.note: {郷里|きょうり}に{帰|かえ}る. Written.
vocab.example: {定年後|ていねんご}は{郷里|きょうり}に{戻|もど}って{畑|はたけ}を{耕|たがや}すつもりだ。
vocab.exampleEn: After retiring I plan to go back to my home region and work the fields.

meanings: local region (one's native area, its culture)
vocab.note: {郷土|きょうど}{料理|りょうり} (local dishes), {郷土|きょうど}{史|し} (local history).
vocab.example: {祭|まつ}りでは、{各地|かくち}の{郷土|きょうど}{料理|りょうり}が{並|なら}んだ。
vocab.exampleEn: At the festival, local dishes from all over were laid out.

vocab.note: Also 〜する. N2's {帰省|きせい} is a visit home for the holidays; {帰郷|ききょう} can be for good.
vocab.example: {十年|じゅうねん}ぶりの{帰郷|ききょう}だったが、{駅前|えきまえ}は{昔|むかし}のままだった。
vocab.exampleEn: It was my first homecoming in ten years, but the area in front of the station was just as it used to be.

vocab.note: {同郷|どうきょう}の{友人|ゆうじん}: a friend from back home.
vocab.example: {上京|じょうきょう}して{最初|さいしょ}に{仲良|なかよ}くなったのは、{同郷|どうきょう}の{先輩|せんぱい}だった。
vocab.exampleEn: The first person I made friends with after moving to Tokyo was an older student from my home town.

meanings: visit to one's parents' home (after marriage, or for a birth)
vocab.note: Also 〜する. {里帰|さとがえ}り{出産|しゅっさん}: giving birth while staying with one's parents.
vocab.example: {正月|しょうがつ}は{妻|つま}の{里帰|さとがえ}りに{合|あ}わせて{北海道|ほっかいどう}へ{行|い}く。
vocab.exampleEn: At New Year we go to Hokkaido for my wife's visit to her family.

meanings: rural village (literary; also one's parents' home)
vocab.note: {山里|やまざと}, {里山|さとやま} (the wooded hills near villages). Old distance unit: {一里|いちり} (about 4 km).
vocab.example: {春|はる}になると、{里|さと}のあちこちで{桜|さくら}が{咲|さ}く。
vocab.exampleEn: When spring comes, cherry trees bloom all over the village.

vocab.note: {里親|さとおや}{制度|せいど}: the foster care system. Also someone who adopts a rescued animal.
vocab.example: {保護|ほご}された{子猫|こねこ}の{里親|さとおや}を{探|さが}している。
vocab.exampleEn: We're looking for someone to adopt a rescued kitten.

vocab.note: Formal; in speech ひいおじいさん.
vocab.example: {曽祖父|そうそふ}は、{明治|めいじ}の{終|お}わりに{生|う}まれたそうだ。
vocab.exampleEn: I'm told my great-grandfather was born at the end of the Meiji era.

vocab.note: Formal; in speech ひいおばあさん.
vocab.example: {曽祖母|そうそぼ}の{代|だい}から{受|う}け{継|つ}がれてきた{着物|きもの}だ。
vocab.exampleEn: This kimono has been handed down since my great-grandmother's time.

vocab.note: Also 〜する: {遺産|いさん}を{相続|そうぞく}する. N2's {遺産|いさん} is what is left.
vocab.example: {相続|そうぞく}をめぐって、{兄弟|きょうだい}の{仲|なか}が{悪|わる}くなる{例|れい}は{少|すく}なくない。
vocab.exampleEn: It's not unusual for brothers and sisters to fall out over an inheritance.

meanings: will (last wishes, also written as a document)
vocab.note: {遺言|ゆいごん}を{残|のこ}す, {遺言書|ゆいごんしょ}. Lawyers also say いごん.
vocab.example: {遺言|ゆいごん}を{残|のこ}しておいてくれればよかったものを、{父|ちち}は{何|なに}も{書|か}かなかった。
vocab.exampleEn: If only Father had left a will, but he didn't write anything.

vocab.note: {法定|ほうてい}{相続人|そうぞくにん}: the legal heirs.
vocab.example: {相続人|そうぞくにん}{全員|ぜんいん}の{同意|どうい}がなければ、{家|いえ}は{売|う}れない。
vocab.exampleEn: The house can't be sold without the agreement of all the heirs.

vocab.note: 〜{税|ぜい}: {消費税|しょうひぜい}, {所得税|しょとくぜい}.
vocab.example: {土地|とち}を{相続|そうぞく}したが、{相続税|そうぞくぜい}が{払|はら}えずに{手放|てばな}した。
vocab.exampleEn: I inherited the land but couldn't pay the inheritance tax, so I let it go.

meanings: indebtedness (a moral obligation for kindness received)
vocab.note: {恩義|おんぎ}を{感|かん}じる. Written, a little old-fashioned.
vocab.example: {若|わか}いころ{世話|せわ}になった{社長|しゃちょう}に、{今|いま}も{恩義|おんぎ}を{感|かん}じている。
vocab.exampleEn: I still feel indebted to the company president who looked after me when I was young.

vocab.note: In kana: its kanji is outside the jōyō list. {家族|かぞく}のきずな.
vocab.example: {災害|さいがい}を{経|へ}て、{町|まち}の{人々|ひとびと}のきずなは{深|ふか}まった。
vocab.exampleEn: Having gone through the disaster, the bonds among the townspeople grew stronger.

meanings: betrothal gifts (exchanged between families at an engagement)
vocab.note: {結納|ゆいのう}を{交|か}わす. Many couples now hold a meal ({顔合|かおあ}わせ) instead.
vocab.example: {最近|さいきん}は{結納|ゆいのう}を{省略|しょうりゃく}する{家庭|かてい}も{多|おお}い。
vocab.exampleEn: These days many families skip the formal exchange of engagement gifts.

vocab.note: In kana: its kanji is outside the course list. {花|はな}むこ (bridegroom), むこ{養子|ようし} (a son-in-law adopted into the wife's family).
vocab.example: {娘|むすめ}のむこは、{料理|りょうり}が{得意|とくい}な{優|やさ}しい{青年|せいねん}だ。
vocab.exampleEn: My daughter's husband is a kind young man who's good at cooking.

vocab.note: Also a stepfather. In speech: {義理|ぎり}のお{父|とう}さん, {夫|おっと}の{父|ちち}.
vocab.example: {義父|ぎふ}は{口数|くちかず}は{少|すく}ないが、{優|やさ}しい{人|ひと}だ。
vocab.exampleEn: My father-in-law doesn't say much, but he's a kind man.

vocab.note: Also a stepmother. A husband's mother is traditionally also しゅうとめ.
vocab.example: {義母|ぎぼ}に{料理|りょうり}を{教|おし}わるのが{楽|たの}しみだ。
vocab.exampleEn: I look forward to learning to cook from my mother-in-law.

vocab.note: {親族|しんぞく}{一同|いちどう}: all the relatives (in formal notices). In speech {親戚|しんせき}.
vocab.example: {葬儀|そうぎ}は{親族|しんぞく}だけで{行|おこな}われた。
vocab.exampleEn: The funeral was held with family members only.

vocab.note: Also "one of us" in a group: {身内|みうち}の{恥|はじ}.
vocab.example: {身内|みうち}だからこそ、{言|い}いにくいこともある。
vocab.exampleEn: Precisely because they're family, some things are hard to say.

meanings: parents' home (the house one grew up in)
vocab.note: {実家|じっか}に{帰|かえ}る. For a married person, their own parents' house.
vocab.example: {週末|しゅうまつ}は{実家|じっか}に{帰|かえ}って、{両親|りょうしん}の{様子|ようす}を{見|み}てくる。
vocab.exampleEn: At the weekend I'll go home and see how my parents are.

meanings: marriage hunting (actively looking for a spouse)
vocab.note: Also 〜する. Coined from {結婚|けっこん}{活動|かつどう}, after {就活|しゅうかつ} (job hunting).
vocab.example: {友人|ゆうじん}は{婚活|こんかつ}アプリで{知|し}り{合|あ}った{人|ひと}と{結婚|けっこん}した。
vocab.exampleEn: My friend married someone they met on a marriage-hunting app.

vocab.note: {晩婚化|ばんこんか}: the trend towards marrying later.
vocab.example: {晩婚化|ばんこんか}が{進|すす}み、{初婚|しょこん}の{年齢|ねんれい}が{上|あ}がっている。
vocab.exampleEn: With the trend towards later marriage, the age of first marriage is rising.

vocab.note: {未婚|みこん}{率|りつ}: the proportion of people who have never married.
vocab.example: {調査|ちょうさ}では、{未婚|みこん}の{若者|わかもの}の{多|おお}くが{結婚|けっこん}を{希望|きぼう}していた。
vocab.exampleEn: In the survey, many unmarried young people said they wanted to marry.

vocab.note: {既婚|きこん}{者|しゃ}: a married person. 既 is lesson 27's kanji.
vocab.example: {申込書|もうしこみしょ}の{既婚|きこん}・{未婚|みこん}の{欄|らん}は、{記入|きにゅう}しなくても{構|かま}わない。
vocab.exampleEn: You don't have to fill in the married/unmarried box on the application form.

vocab.note: Also 〜する.
vocab.example: {母|はは}が{再婚|さいこん}すると{聞|き}いて、{娘|むすめ}は{心|こころ}から{喜|よろこ}んだ。
vocab.exampleEn: Hearing that her mother was remarrying, the daughter was truly glad.

meanings: registering a marriage (entering the family register)
vocab.note: Also 〜する. Strictly, entering someone into a family register ({戸籍|こせき}); in everyday use, getting legally married.
vocab.example: {式|しき}は{来年|らいねん}だが、{入籍|にゅうせき}は{先月|せんげつ}{済|す}ませた。
vocab.exampleEn: The ceremony is next year, but we registered our marriage last month.

vocab.note: Also 〜する. Formal; {結婚式|けっこんしき} in speech.
vocab.example: {二人|ふたり}は{海外|かいがい}で{挙式|きょしき}することにした。
vocab.exampleEn: The two decided to hold their wedding abroad.

meanings: both families (of the bride and groom)
vocab.note: {両家|りょうけ}の{顔合|かおあ}わせ: the first meeting of the two families.
vocab.example: {両家|りょうけ}の{親|おや}が{初|はじ}めて{顔|かお}を{合|あ}わせた。
vocab.exampleEn: The parents of both families met for the first time.

vocab.note: {一族|いちぞく}の{墓|はか}, {一族|いちぞく}{経営|けいえい}.
vocab.example: {正月|しょうがつ}には、{一族|いちぞく}が{本家|ほんけ}に{集|あつ}まる。
vocab.exampleEn: At New Year, the whole clan gathers at the main family's house.

vocab.note: {家系図|かけいず}: a family tree. Sounds like N3's {家計|かけい} (household budget).
vocab.example: うちは{代々|だいだい}{医者|いしゃ}の{家系|かけい}だ。
vocab.exampleEn: Ours is a family of doctors going back generations.

vocab.note: In kana: its kanji is outside the course list. Formal neutral word: {義母|ぎぼ}.
vocab.example: {料理|りょうり}の{味付|あじつ}けは、しゅうとめに{教|おそ}わった。
vocab.exampleEn: I learned how to season dishes from my mother-in-law.

vocab.note: {恩着|おんき}せがましい{言|い}い{方|かた}. From {恩|おん}に{着|き}せる (to make someone feel indebted).
vocab.example: {手伝|てつだ}ってくれたのはありがたいが、{恩着|おんき}せがましいのは{困|こま}る。
vocab.exampleEn: It's kind of them to help, but I wish they wouldn't keep reminding me of it.

meanings: to stay close by (someone's side, in support)
vocab.note: Group 1. ます form: {寄|よ}り{添|そ}います; て form: {寄|よ}り{添|そ}って. {相手|あいて}の{気持|きも}ちに{寄|よ}り{添|そ}う: to be there for someone.
vocab.example: {看護師|かんごし}は、{患者|かんじゃ}の{家族|かぞく}にも{寄|よ}り{添|そ}う{存在|そんざい}だ。
vocab.exampleEn: Nurses are there for patients' families too.

meanings: home with one's parents (under their roof)
vocab.note: {親元|おやもと}を{離|はな}れる: to leave home.
vocab.example: {大学|だいがく}{進学|しんがく}を{機|き}に、{親元|おやもと}を{離|はな}れた。
vocab.exampleEn: I left home when I went to university.

vocab.note: Also 〜する. Sounds like N2's {状況|じょうきょう} (situation).
vocab.example: {夢|ゆめ}を{追|お}って{上京|じょうきょう}してから、もう{十年|じゅうねん}になる。
vocab.exampleEn: It's already been ten years since I came to Tokyo chasing my dream.

meanings: living apart (of a married couple or family)
vocab.note: Also 〜する.
vocab.example: {仕事|しごと}の{都合|つごう}で、{夫婦|ふうふ}はしばらく{別居|べっきょ}している。
vocab.exampleEn: Because of work, the couple are living apart for a while.

vocab.note: 核 is lesson 14's kanji. {核家族化|かくかぞくか}: the shift to nuclear families.
vocab.example: {核家族|かくかぞく}が{増|ふ}え、{祖父母|そふぼ}と{暮|く}らす{子供|こども}は{少|すく}なくなった。
vocab.exampleEn: With more nuclear families, fewer children live with their grandparents.

vocab.note: Three or more generations under one roof.
vocab.example: {大家族|だいかぞく}で{育|そだ}ったので、{一人|ひとり}の{食事|しょくじ}は{寂|さび}しい。
vocab.exampleEn: I grew up in a big family, so eating alone feels lonely.

vocab.note: な-adjective. {夫婦|ふうふ}{円満|えんまん}, {円満|えんまん}に{解決|かいけつ}する, {円満|えんまん}{退社|たいしゃ}.
vocab.example: {話|はな}し{合|あ}いの{結果|けっか}、{問題|もんだい}は{円満|えんまん}に{解決|かいけつ}した。
vocab.exampleEn: As a result of the talks, the problem was settled amicably.

vocab.note: な-adjective. {和|なご}やかな{雰囲気|ふんいき}, {和|なご}やかに{話|はな}す.
vocab.example: {両家|りょうけ}の{食事会|しょくじかい}は、{和|なご}やかな{雰囲気|ふんいき}で{進|すす}んだ。
vocab.exampleEn: The dinner for the two families went on in a warm, relaxed atmosphere.

meanings: by ourselves (just the family, with no outsiders)
vocab.note: {親子|おやこ}{水入|みずい}らず, {家族|かぞく}{水入|みずい}らずで{過|す}ごす.
vocab.example: {久|ひさ}しぶりに{夫婦|ふうふ}{水入|みずい}らずで{旅行|りょこう}した。
vocab.exampleEn: For the first time in ages, the couple went on a trip just the two of them.

vocab.note: Newspaper mixed spelling: the second kanji is outside the jōyō list. {一家|いっか}{団|だん}らん.
vocab.example: {夕食|ゆうしょく}は、{家族|かぞく}の{団|だん}らんの{時間|じかん}だ。
vocab.exampleEn: Dinner is the family's time together.

vocab.note: {契|ちぎ}りを{結|むす}ぶ (to pledge oneself). Literary.
vocab.example: {二人|ふたり}は{生涯|しょうがい}の{契|ちぎ}りを{結|むす}んだ。
vocab.exampleEn: The two pledged themselves to each other for life.

meanings: relationship one can't shake off (said wryly)
vocab.note: Half joking: {彼|かれ}とは{腐|くさ}れ{縁|えん}だ (we're stuck with each other).
vocab.example: {小学校|しょうがっこう}からの{腐|くさ}れ{縁|えん}で、{今|いま}でも{毎週|まいしゅう}{会|あ}っている。
vocab.exampleEn: We've been stuck with each other since primary school and still meet every week.

vocab.note: Also 〜する: {親|おや}と{絶縁|ぜつえん}する.
vocab.example: {兄|あに}とは{十年|じゅうねん}{前|まえ}に{絶縁|ぜつえん}したきりだ。
vocab.exampleEn: I broke off with my brother ten years ago and haven't spoken since.

vocab.note: Mostly {涙|なみだ}ながらに + verb: {涙|なみだ}ながらに{語|かた}る.
vocab.example: {選手|せんしゅ}は{涙|なみだ}ながらに{引退|いんたい}を{発表|はっぴょう}した。
vocab.exampleEn: The athlete announced their retirement in tears.

vocab.note: {生|う}まれながらの{才能|さいのう}, {生|う}まれながらにして.
vocab.example: {人|ひと}は{生|う}まれながらにして{平等|びょうどう}である。
vocab.exampleEn: People are born equal.

meanings: as of old (in the traditional way)
vocab.note: {昔|むかし}ながらの + noun: {昔|むかし}ながらの{製法|せいほう}.
vocab.example: この{店|みせ}では、{昔|むかし}ながらの{方法|ほうほう}でみそを{作|つく}っている。
vocab.exampleEn: This shop makes miso by traditional methods.

vocab.note: At weddings: {新郎新婦|しんろうしんぷ}のご{入場|にゅうじょう}です.
vocab.example: {新郎新婦|しんろうしんぷ}が{入場|にゅうじょう}すると、{会場|かいじょう}は{拍手|はくしゅ}に{包|つつ}まれた。
vocab.exampleEn: When the bride and groom came in, the hall filled with applause.

meanings: parental authority (custody of a child, legal)
vocab.note: {親権|しんけん}を{持|も}つ, {親権|しんけん}{争|あらそ}い.
vocab.example: {離婚|りこん}の{際|さい}、{子供|こども}の{親権|しんけん}は{母親|ははおや}が{持|も}つことになった。
vocab.exampleEn: When they divorced, it was decided that the mother would have custody of the child.

vocab.note: {養子|ようし}を{迎|むか}える, {養子|ようし}{縁組|えんぐみ} (adoption). Sounds like N4's {用紙|ようし} (form).
vocab.example: {子供|こども}のいない{夫婦|ふうふ}が、{親戚|しんせき}の{子|こ}を{養子|ようし}に{迎|むか}えた。
vocab.exampleEn: A childless couple adopted a relative's child.

vocab.note: Short for {産前産後|さんぜんさんご}{休業|きゅうぎょう}. {育休|いくきゅう}: childcare leave.
vocab.example: {来月|らいげつ}から{産休|さんきゅう}に{入|はい}るので、{仕事|しごと}を{引|ひ}き{継|つ}いでおく。
vocab.exampleEn: I'm going on maternity leave next month, so I'll hand over my work.

vocab.note: Short for {育児|いくじ}{休業|きゅうぎょう}. {育休|いくきゅう}を{取|と}る.
vocab.example: {父親|ちちおや}が{育休|いくきゅう}を{取|と}ることも、{珍|めずら}しくなくなってきた。
vocab.exampleEn: It's no longer unusual for fathers to take childcare leave.

vocab.note: {血筋|ちすじ}を{引|ひ}く: to be descended from. Also a talent that runs in the family.
vocab.example: {音楽|おんがく}の{才能|さいのう}は{血筋|ちすじ}かもしれない。
vocab.exampleEn: A gift for music may run in the family.

vocab.note: {生|お}い{立|た}ちを{語|かた}る.
vocab.example: {作家|さっか}は、{自分|じぶん}の{生|お}い{立|た}ちを{小説|しょうせつ}に{書|か}いた。
vocab.exampleEn: The writer wrote about their own upbringing in a novel.

vocab.note: After a name as a title of respect; also used jokingly for a friend's drawing.
vocab.example: {町|まち}の{美術館|びじゅつかん}で、{郷土|きょうど}{出身|しゅっしん}の{画伯|がはく}の{作品|さくひん}が{展示|てんじ}されている。
vocab.exampleEn: The town gallery is showing works by a master painter from the region.

vocab.note: {宗派|しゅうは}によって{作法|さほう}が{違|ちが}う: the rites differ by sect.
vocab.example: {宗派|しゅうは}が{何|なん}であれ、{手|て}を{合|あ}わせる{気持|きも}ちは{同|おな}じだ。
vocab.exampleEn: Whatever the sect, the feeling behind putting your hands together is the same.

vocab.note: Also 〜する. Sounds like N2's {改修|かいしゅう} (renovation).
vocab.example: {結婚|けっこん}を{機|き}に{改宗|かいしゅう}する{人|ひと}もいる。
vocab.exampleEn: Some people convert to another religion when they marry.

vocab.note: Formal; in speech お{坊|ぼう}さん.
vocab.example: {葬儀|そうぎ}では、{僧侶|そうりょ}がお{経|きょう}を{読|よ}んだ。
vocab.exampleEn: At the funeral, a priest chanted a sutra.

vocab.note: Written: {若|わか}い{僧|そう}, {旅|たび}の{僧|そう}. Sounds like N2's {層|そう} (layer).
vocab.example: {旅|たび}の{僧|そう}が、{一夜|いちや}の{宿|やど}を{求|もと}めて{村|むら}を{訪|おとず}れた。
vocab.exampleEn: A travelling monk came to the village asking for a night's lodging.

vocab.note: {尼寺|あまでら}: a convent. Formal: {尼僧|にそう}.
vocab.example: {夫|おっと}を{亡|な}くした{後|あと}、{祖母|そぼ}の{姉|あね}は{尼|あま}になった。
vocab.exampleEn: After losing her husband, my grandmother's older sister became a nun.

meanings: nun (formal: a Buddhist or Christian nun)
vocab.note: Written; in speech {尼|あま}さん.
vocab.example: その{寺|てら}では、{尼僧|にそう}たちが{静|しず}かに{暮|く}らしている。
vocab.exampleEn: At that temple, nuns live a quiet life.

vocab.note: {座禅|ざぜん}を{組|く}む: to sit in Zen meditation.
vocab.example: {週末|しゅうまつ}は{寺|てら}で{座禅|ざぜん}を{組|く}んで、{心|こころ}を{落|お}ち{着|つ}けている。
vocab.exampleEn: At weekends I do sitting meditation at a temple to calm my mind.

vocab.note: {禅|ぜん}の{教|おし}え, {禅寺|ぜんでら}. Sounds like lesson 26's {善|ぜん} (goodness).
vocab.example: {禅|ぜん}の{考|かんが}え{方|かた}は、{茶道|さどう}にも{大|おお}きな{影響|えいきょう}を{与|あた}えた。
vocab.exampleEn: Zen thought had a great influence on the tea ceremony as well.

vocab.note: 寺 becomes でら, as in {山寺|やまでら}.
vocab.example: {京都|きょうと}の{禅寺|ぜんでら}の{庭|にわ}は、{石|いし}と{砂|すな}だけで{作|つく}られている。
vocab.exampleEn: The garden of the Zen temple in Kyoto is made of nothing but stones and sand.

vocab.note: {先祖|せんぞ}の{霊|れい}, {霊|れい}を{慰|なぐさ}める. Sounds like {礼|れい} (bow) and {例|れい} (example).
vocab.example: お{盆|ぼん}には、{先祖|せんぞ}の{霊|れい}が{家|いえ}に{帰|かえ}ってくると{言|い}われる。
vocab.exampleEn: It's said that at Obon the spirits of one's ancestors come back home.

meanings: the soul (as separate from the body, formal)
vocab.note: Written; {魂|たましい} is the everyday word.
vocab.example: {死後|しご}も{霊魂|れいこん}は{残|のこ}ると{信|しん}じる{人|ひと}は{少|すく}なくない。
vocab.exampleEn: Quite a few people believe that the soul remains after death.

meanings: memorial (consoling the souls of the dead)
vocab.note: {慰霊碑|いれいひ}: a memorial to the dead; {慰霊祭|いれいさい}: a memorial service.
vocab.example: {毎年|まいとし}、{事故|じこ}のあった{日|ひ}に{慰霊|いれい}の{式典|しきてん}が{行|おこな}われる。
vocab.exampleEn: Every year, a memorial ceremony is held on the day of the accident.

vocab.note: A modern public or private cemetery; {墓地|ぼち} is any graveyard.
vocab.example: {郊外|こうがい}の{霊園|れいえん}に{墓|はか}を{移|うつ}した。
vocab.exampleEn: We moved the family grave to a cemetery in the suburbs.

vocab.note: {魂|たましい}を{込|こ}める: to put one's heart into; {三|みっ}つ{子|ご}の{魂|たましい}{百|ひゃく}まで (the child is father to the man).
vocab.example: {職人|しょくにん}は、{一|ひと}つひとつの{器|うつわ}に{魂|たましい}を{込|こ}めて{作|つく}る。
vocab.exampleEn: The craftsman puts their soul into each piece they make.

meanings: repose of souls (prayer for the dead)
vocab.note: {鎮魂|ちんこん}{歌|か}: a requiem. 鎮 is lesson 22's kanji.
vocab.example: {夜空|よぞら}に、{鎮魂|ちんこん}の{鐘|かね}が{響|ひび}いた。
vocab.exampleEn: The bell for the repose of the dead rang out into the night sky.

vocab.note: {呪|のろ}いをかける. Sounds like the adjective のろい (slow); context tells them apart.
vocab.example: {古|ふる}い{人形|にんぎょう}には{呪|のろ}いがあるといううわさが{立|た}った。
vocab.exampleEn: A rumour started that the old doll carried a curse.

vocab.note: Group 1. ます form: {呪|のろ}います; て form: {呪|のろ}って. Also {運命|うんめい}を{呪|のろ}う (to curse one's fate).
vocab.example: {彼|かれ}は{自分|じぶん}の{不運|ふうん}を{呪|のろ}った。
vocab.exampleEn: He cursed his bad luck.

vocab.note: {呪文|じゅもん}を{唱|とな}える: to say a spell.
vocab.example: {魔法|まほう}{使|つか}いが{呪文|じゅもん}を{唱|とな}えると、{扉|とびら}が{開|ひら}いた。
vocab.exampleEn: When the wizard chanted a spell, the door opened.

vocab.note: Everyday word; formal: {葬儀|そうぎ}.
vocab.example: {祖父|そふ}の{葬式|そうしき}には、{思|おも}いがけず{大勢|おおぜい}の{人|ひと}が{来|き}た。
vocab.exampleEn: Unexpectedly many people came to Grandfather's funeral.

vocab.note: {葬儀|そうぎ}{社|しゃ}: a funeral company; {葬儀|そうぎ}{場|じょう}: a funeral hall.
vocab.example: {葬儀|そうぎ}は{近親者|きんしんしゃ}のみで{執|と}り{行|おこな}われた。
vocab.exampleEn: The funeral service was held with close relatives only.

vocab.note: Also 〜する. In Japan most people are cremated ({火葬|かそう}) and the ashes are placed in a grave.
vocab.example: {遺骨|いこつ}は{家族|かぞく}の{墓|はか}に{埋葬|まいそう}された。
vocab.exampleEn: The remains were buried in the family grave.

vocab.note: Also 〜する. {火葬場|かそうば}: a crematorium.
vocab.example: {告別式|こくべつしき}の{後|あと}、{火葬場|かそうば}へ{向|む}かった。
vocab.exampleEn: After the farewell ceremony, we went to the crematorium.

meanings: to lay to rest (bury the dead)
vocab.note: Group 1. ます form: {葬|ほうむ}ります; て form: {葬|ほうむ}って. Also figurative: {事件|じけん}を{闇|やみ}に{葬|ほうむ}る (to bury a scandal in darkness).
vocab.example: {不祥事|ふしょうじ}は{闇|やみ}に{葬|ほうむ}られかけたが、{一本|いっぽん}の{記事|きじ}で{明|あき}らかになった。
vocab.exampleEn: The scandal was nearly hushed up, but one article brought it to light.

vocab.note: お{墓|はか} is the everyday polite form.
vocab.example: {彼岸|ひがん}には{家族|かぞく}そろってお{墓|はか}に{行|い}く。
vocab.exampleEn: At the equinox the whole family goes to the grave.

vocab.note: {寺|てら}の{墓地|ぼち}, {共同|きょうどう}{墓地|ぼち}.
vocab.example: {寺|てら}の{裏|うら}には{古|ふる}い{墓地|ぼち}が{広|ひろ}がっている。
vocab.exampleEn: An old graveyard stretches out behind the temple.

meanings: visit to a grave (to pay respects)
vocab.note: Also 〜する. Usually お{墓参|はかまい}り.
vocab.example: お{盆|ぼん}に{帰省|きせい}して、{家族|かぞく}でお{墓参|はかまい}りをした。
vocab.exampleEn: We went home for Obon and visited the family grave together.

vocab.note: Also read ぼせき in formal writing.
vocab.example: {墓石|はかいし}には、{先祖|せんぞ}の{名前|なまえ}が{刻|きざ}まれている。
vocab.exampleEn: The names of the ancestors are carved on the gravestone.

vocab.note: 〜{碑|ひ}: a stone monument ({慰霊碑|いれいひ}, {句碑|くひ}).
vocab.example: {公園|こうえん}には、{町|まち}の{開拓|かいたく}を{記念|きねん}する{記念碑|きねんひ}が{建|た}っている。
vocab.exampleEn: In the park stands a monument commemorating the settling of the town.

vocab.note: A stone with words carved on it.
vocab.example: {道端|みちばた}の{石碑|せきひ}には、{昔|むかし}の{洪水|こうずい}の{記録|きろく}が{刻|きざ}まれていた。
vocab.exampleEn: The stone by the road was carved with a record of a flood long ago.

vocab.note: Built from roughly the 3rd to the 7th century; the period is named after them.
vocab.example: {住宅地|じゅうたくち}の{真|ま}ん{中|なか}に、{古墳|こふん}がそのまま{残|のこ}っている。
vocab.exampleEn: An ancient burial mound has survived just as it was in the middle of a residential area.

vocab.reading: ぜんぽうこうえんふん
vocab.note: Square at the front ({前方|ぜんぽう}), round at the back ({後円|こうえん}).
vocab.example: {空|そら}から{見|み}ると、{前方後円墳|ぜんぽうこうえんふん}の{形|かたち}がよく{分|わ}かる。
vocab.exampleEn: From the air you can clearly see the keyhole shape of the burial mound.

meanings: mourning (in memory of the dead, formal)
vocab.note: Also 〜する. {追悼|ついとう}{式|しき}: a memorial service; {追悼|ついとう}の{意|い}を{表|あらわ}す.
vocab.example: {試合|しあい}の{前|まえ}に、{亡|な}くなった{選手|せんしゅ}を{追悼|ついとう}して{黙|もく}とうが{行|おこな}われた。
vocab.exampleEn: Before the match, a moment's silence was held in memory of the player who had died.

vocab.note: {哀悼|あいとう}の{意|い}を{表|ひょう}する: to express one's condolences. 哀 is lesson 16's kanji.
vocab.example: {首相|しゅしょう}は{遺族|いぞく}に{深|ふか}い{哀悼|あいとう}の{意|い}を{表|ひょう}した。
vocab.exampleEn: The prime minister expressed deep condolences to the bereaved families.

vocab.note: Group 1. ます form: {悼|いた}みます; て form: {悼|いた}んで. {死|し}を{悼|いた}む, {故人|こじん}を{悼|いた}む. Sounds like N3's {痛|いた}む (to hurt).
vocab.example: {町|まち}の{人々|ひとびと}は、{祭|まつ}りを{守|まも}り{続|つづ}けた{老人|ろうじん}の{死|し}を{悼|いた}んだ。
vocab.exampleEn: The townspeople mourned the death of the old man who had kept the festival going.

vocab.note: Also 〜する. Only for others ({会長|かいちょう}のご{逝去|せいきょ}); for one's own family: {死去|しきょ}, {亡|な}くなる.
vocab.example: {恩師|おんし}のご{逝去|せいきょ}の{知|し}らせを{受|う}け、{言葉|ことば}を{失|うしな}った。
vocab.exampleEn: On hearing of my old teacher's passing, I was lost for words.

vocab.note: Also 〜する. Sounds like N2's {急性|きゅうせい} (acute).
vocab.example: {作家|さっか}は{連載|れんさい}の{途中|とちゅう}で{急逝|きゅうせい}した。
vocab.exampleEn: The writer died suddenly in the middle of the serial.

vocab.note: Black for a funeral; for the wake a plain dark suit is usually fine.
vocab.example: {急|きゅう}な{知|し}らせだったので、{喪服|もふく}を{借|か}りて{参列|さんれつ}した。
vocab.exampleEn: The news came suddenly, so I borrowed mourning clothes to attend.

meanings: period of mourning (after a family death)
vocab.note: {喪中|もちゅう}はがき: a postcard telling friends one won't send New Year's cards.
vocab.example: {喪中|もちゅう}のため、{新年|しんねん}のご{挨拶|あいさつ}を{控|ひか}えさせていただきます。
vocab.exampleEn: As we are in mourning, we will refrain from sending New Year greetings.

vocab.note: Usually the spouse or the eldest child.
vocab.example: {父|ちち}の{葬儀|そうぎ}では、{長男|ちょうなん}の{兄|あに}が{喪主|もしゅ}を{務|つと}めた。
vocab.exampleEn: At our father's funeral, my older brother, the eldest son, acted as chief mourner.

meanings: loss (of something one had: confidence, memory, rights)
vocab.note: Also 〜する. {記憶|きおく}{喪失|そうしつ} (amnesia), {自信|じしん}{喪失|そうしつ}.
vocab.example: {大切|たいせつ}な{人|ひと}を{失|うしな}った{喪失|そうしつ}{感|かん}は、すぐには{消|き}えない。
vocab.exampleEn: The sense of loss after losing someone dear doesn't fade quickly.

vocab.note: 〜{発祥|はっしょう}の{地|ち}: the birthplace of. Sounds like N2's {発症|はっしょう} (onset).
vocab.example: この{町|まち}は、ある{有名|ゆうめい}な{祭|まつ}りの{発祥|はっしょう}の{地|ち}だと{言|い}われている。
vocab.exampleEn: This town is said to be the birthplace of a famous festival.

vocab.note: Mostly of Western folklore; Japanese spirits of folklore are {妖怪|ようかい}.
vocab.example: その{森|もり}には{妖精|ようせい}が{住|す}んでいるという{言|い}い{伝|つた}えがある。
vocab.exampleEn: Legend has it that fairies live in that forest.

vocab.note: {悪魔|あくま}のような{人|ひと}. 〜{魔|ま}: a person possessed by something ({睡魔|すいま}, sleepiness).
vocab.example: {物語|ものがたり}の{中|なか}で、{悪魔|あくま}は{男|おとこ}に{三|みっ}つの{願|ねが}いをかなえると{約束|やくそく}した。
vocab.exampleEn: In the story, the devil promised the man to grant him three wishes.

vocab.note: {魔法|まほう}{使|つか}い: a wizard or witch.
vocab.example: {魔法|まほう}でも{使|つか}ったかのように、{部屋|へや}が{一瞬|いっしゅん}で{片付|かたづ}いた。
vocab.exampleEn: The room was tidied in an instant, as if by magic.

meanings: demon (evil spirit that haunts a place)
vocab.note: Also figurative: {甲子園|こうしえん}には{魔物|まもの}が{住|す}む (anything can happen there).
vocab.example: {夜|よる}の{山|やま}には{魔物|まもの}が{出|で}ると、{昔|むかし}の{人|ひと}は{恐|おそ}れた。
vocab.exampleEn: People long ago feared that evil spirits came out in the mountains at night.

vocab.note: A charm or object meant to keep evil away.
vocab.example: {玄関|げんかん}に{魔除|まよ}けのお{札|ふだ}を{貼|は}っている。
vocab.exampleEn: We have a talisman against evil stuck up in the entrance.

vocab.note: Also of places fans visit: アニメの{聖地|せいち}{巡礼|じゅんれい}.
vocab.example: {毎年|まいとし}{多|おお}くの{信者|しんじゃ}が{聖地|せいち}を{訪|おとず}れる。
vocab.exampleEn: Every year many believers visit the holy place.

vocab.note: Sounds like N2's {清書|せいしょ} (fair copy).
vocab.example: {聖書|せいしょ}の{言葉|ことば}は、{多|おお}くの{文学|ぶんがく}{作品|さくひん}に{引用|いんよう}されている。
vocab.exampleEn: Words from the Bible are quoted in many works of literature.

vocab.note: な-adjective. {神聖|しんせい}な{場所|ばしょ}. Sounds like N3's しんせい (application).
vocab.example: {土俵|どひょう}は{神聖|しんせい}な{場所|ばしょ}だとされている。
vocab.exampleEn: The sumo ring is regarded as a sacred place.

meanings: worship (reverence for a god, person or idea)
vocab.note: Also 〜する. {英雄|えいゆう}{崇拝|すうはい}: hero worship.
vocab.example: {山|やま}そのものを{崇拝|すうはい}する{信仰|しんこう}は、{各地|かくち}に{見|み}られる。
vocab.exampleEn: Faiths that worship the mountain itself are found in many places.

meanings: to worship (revere as a god or hero)
vocab.note: Group 2. ます form: あがめます; て form: あがめて. In kana: あが isn't a jōyō reading of 崇 (often printed 崇める). {神|かみ}としてあがめる.
vocab.example: {村人|むらびと}は{古|ふる}い{大木|たいぼく}を{神|かみ}としてあがめてきた。
vocab.exampleEn: The villagers have long revered the old tree as a god.

vocab.note: な-adjective. {崇高|すうこう}な{理想|りそう}, {崇高|すうこう}な{精神|せいしん}.
vocab.example: {人|ひと}の{命|いのち}を{救|すく}うという{崇高|すうこう}な{使命|しめい}.
vocab.exampleEn: The lofty mission of saving people's lives.

meanings: temple or shrine visit (formal, to worship)
vocab.note: Also 〜する. Written; N2's {参拝|さんぱい} is more common.
vocab.example: {江戸|えど}{時代|じだい}には、{庶民|しょみん}の{間|あいだ}でも{遠|とお}くの{寺社|じしゃ}への{参詣|さんけい}が{盛|さか}んだった。
vocab.exampleEn: In the Edo period, pilgrimages to distant temples and shrines were popular even among ordinary people.

meanings: to pay a visit to worship (at a shrine or temple, literary)
vocab.note: Group 2. ます form: {詣|もう}でます; て form: {詣|もう}でて. Noun: {詣|もう}で ({初詣|はつもうで}: the first visit of the New Year).
vocab.example: {元日|がんじつ}の{朝|あさ}、{家族|かぞく}で{近所|きんじょ}の{神社|じんじゃ}に{詣|もう}でた。
vocab.exampleEn: On the morning of New Year's Day, the family went to worship at the local shrine.

vocab.note: Sounds like N5's お{金|かね} (money), which has the same pitch; context tells them apart.
vocab.example: {夕方|ゆうがた}になると、{寺|てら}の{鐘|かね}が{町|まち}に{響|ひび}く。
vocab.exampleEn: In the evening, the temple bell rings out over the town.

meanings: New Year's Eve bell (rung 108 times at temples)
vocab.note: Rung at midnight on New Year's Eve; 108 is said to be the number of worldly desires ({煩悩|ぼんのう}).
vocab.example: {除夜|じょや}の{鐘|かね}を{聞|き}きながら、{一年|いちねん}を{振|ふ}り{返|かえ}った。
vocab.exampleEn: I looked back on the year while listening to the New Year's Eve bell.

vocab.note: {東京|とうきょう}タワー is a タワー; old Buddhist towers are {塔|とう}. Sounds like N2's {党|とう} (party).
vocab.example: {丘|おか}の{上|うえ}に{古|ふる}い{塔|とう}が{見|み}える。
vocab.exampleEn: An old tower can be seen on the hill.

vocab.note: Note the reading: ごじゅう + の + とう.
vocab.example: {雪|ゆき}の{中|なか}の{五重塔|ごじゅうのとう}は、{絵|え}のように{美|うつく}しかった。
vocab.exampleEn: The five-storey pagoda in the snow was as beautiful as a picture.

meanings: temple priest (head of a temple, especially Zen)
vocab.note: Often お{寺|てら}の{和尚|おしょう}さん. 尚 read しょう; 和 read お.
vocab.example: {和尚|おしょう}さんは、{子供|こども}たちに{昔話|むかしばなし}を{聞|き}かせてくれた。
vocab.exampleEn: The temple priest told the children old stories.

vocab.note: な-adjective. {高尚|こうしょう}な{趣味|しゅみ}. Opposite: lesson 6's {低俗|ていぞく}.
vocab.example: {高尚|こうしょう}な{話|はなし}ばかりでは、{子供|こども}は{退屈|たいくつ}してしまう。
vocab.exampleEn: All high-minded talk and the children get bored.

meanings: premature (too early, said of a decision or plan)
vocab.note: {時期尚早|じきしょうそう}だ: it's too soon. 4-character compound.
vocab.example: {結論|けつろん}を{出|だ}すのは{時期尚早|じきしょうそう}だ。
vocab.exampleEn: It's too early to draw a conclusion.

vocab.note: Special reading: 数 じゅ, 珠 ず. Carried at Buddhist funerals and memorial services.
vocab.example: {仏式|ぶっしき}の{葬儀|そうぎ}には、{数珠|じゅず}を{持|も}っていくのが{一般的|いっぱんてき}だ。
vocab.exampleEn: It's usual to take prayer beads to a Buddhist funeral.

vocab.note: {真珠|しんじゅ}のネックレス: often worn with mourning clothes.
vocab.example: {母|はは}は{喪服|もふく}に{一連|いちれん}の{真珠|しんじゅ}のネックレスを{合|あ}わせた。
vocab.exampleEn: My mother wore a single string of pearls with her mourning clothes.

vocab.note: Today's word is {刑務所|けいむしょ}. 監 is lesson 11's kanji.
vocab.example: {明治|めいじ}{時代|じだい}の{監獄|かんごく}が、{博物館|はくぶつかん}として{公開|こうかい}されている。
vocab.exampleEn: A Meiji-era prison is open to the public as a museum.

meanings: unlucky year (an age believed to bring misfortune)
vocab.note: Many people visit a shrine or temple for {厄払|やくばら}い in such a year.
vocab.example: {今年|ことし}は{厄年|やくどし}なので、{神社|じんじゃ}で{厄払|やくばら}いをしてもらった。
vocab.exampleEn: This is an unlucky year for me, so I had my bad luck warded off at the shrine.

meanings: a nuisance (troublesome, hard to deal with)
vocab.note: な-adjective. {厄介|やっかい}な{問題|もんだい}; {厄介|やっかい}になる: to impose on someone ({一晩|ひとばん}ご{厄介|やっかい}になります).
vocab.example: {相続|そうぞく}の{手続|てつづ}きは、{思|おも}った{以上|いじょう}に{厄介|やっかい}だった。
vocab.exampleEn: The inheritance procedures were more troublesome than I expected.

meanings: warding off bad luck (a purification rite)
vocab.note: Also 〜する. Also {厄落|やくお}とし.
vocab.example: {四十二歳|よんじゅうにさい}の{父|ちち}は、{正月|しょうがつ}に{厄払|やくばら}いに{行|い}った。
vocab.exampleEn: My father, who is 42, went to have his bad luck warded off at New Year.

meanings: protection against misfortune (a charm or rite)
vocab.note: {厄除|やくよ}けのお{守|まも}り.
vocab.example: この{寺|てら}は{厄除|やくよ}けで{知|し}られている。
vocab.exampleEn: This temple is known for protection against misfortune.

vocab.note: な-adjective. {不吉|ふきつ}な{予感|よかん}, {不吉|ふきつ}な{数字|すうじ} (four and nine, by sound).
vocab.example: {結婚式|けっこんしき}の{朝|あさ}に{鏡|かがみ}が{割|わ}れるなんて、{不吉|ふきつ}だと{祖母|そぼ}は{言|い}った。
vocab.exampleEn: My grandmother said that a mirror breaking on the morning of a wedding was a bad omen.

meanings: excellent luck (the best fortune on a fortune slip)
vocab.note: Then {吉|きち}, {小吉|しょうきち}…; the worst is {凶|きょう} or {大凶|だいきょう}.
vocab.example: {初詣|はつもうで}で{引|ひ}いたおみくじは{大吉|だいきち}だった。
vocab.exampleEn: The fortune slip I drew at the New Year shrine visit said "excellent luck".

vocab.note: Also きちにち. On formal invitations: {令和|れいわ}〇{年|ねん}〇{月|がつ}{吉日|きちじつ} (an auspicious day of the month).
vocab.example: {結婚式|けっこんしき}の{招待状|しょうたいじょう}には、{日付|ひづけ}の{代|か}わりに「{吉日|きちじつ}」と{書|か}くことがある。
vocab.exampleEn: On wedding invitations, people sometimes write "an auspicious day" instead of the date.

vocab.note: {儀式|ぎしき}を{行|おこな}う. {儀式的|ぎしきてき}: ritualistic, a mere formality.
vocab.example: {成人|せいじん}の{儀式|ぎしき}は、{国|くに}によってさまざまだ。
vocab.exampleEn: Coming-of-age rituals vary from country to country.

vocab.note: {極楽|ごくらく}{浄土|じょうど}. {浄土|じょうど}{宗|しゅう}: the Pure Land school.
vocab.example: {昔|むかし}の{人々|ひとびと}は、{死後|しご}に{浄土|じょうど}に{生|う}まれ{変|か}わることを{願|ねが}った。
vocab.exampleEn: People in the past prayed to be reborn in the Pure Land after death.

meanings: purification (of water, air or the mind)
vocab.note: Also 〜する. {浄化|じょうか}{装置|そうち}: a purification device.
vocab.example: {森|もり}には、{空気|くうき}や{水|みず}を{浄化|じょうか}する{働|はたら}きがある。
vocab.exampleEn: Forests work to purify the air and water.

meanings: clean and pure (free of pollution, formal)
vocab.note: な-adjective. {清浄|せいじょう}な{空気|くうき}. Also used of sacred places.
vocab.example: {高原|こうげん}の{清浄|せいじょう}な{空気|くうき}を{胸|むね}いっぱいに{吸|す}い{込|こ}んだ。
vocab.exampleEn: I breathed the clean, pure air of the highlands deep into my lungs.

vocab.note: Buddhist sutras, and also the holy books of other religions.
vocab.example: {寺|てら}には、{千年|せんねん}{前|まえ}に{写|うつ}された{経典|きょうてん}が{残|のこ}っている。
vocab.exampleEn: The temple has scriptures copied a thousand years ago.

vocab.note: Where photos and memorial tablets of the dead are kept. 壇 is lesson 29's kanji.
vocab.example: {朝|あさ}ご{飯|はん}の{前|まえ}に、{祖母|そぼ}は{仏壇|ぶつだん}にご{飯|はん}を{供|そな}える。
vocab.exampleEn: Before breakfast, my grandmother offers rice at the family altar.

vocab.note: Given to the dead by a priest. 戒 is lesson 14's kanji.
vocab.example: {祖父|そふ}の{戒名|かいみょう}は、{和尚|おしょう}さんが{付|つ}けてくださった。
vocab.exampleEn: The priest gave Grandfather his Buddhist name after death.

vocab.note: お{彼岸|ひがん}: the weeks around the spring and autumn equinoxes; {暑|あつ}さ{寒|さむ}さも{彼岸|ひがん}まで (the heat and cold last until the equinox).
vocab.example: お{彼岸|ひがん}には{家族|かぞく}でお{墓参|はかまい}りに{行|い}く。
vocab.exampleEn: At the equinox the family goes to visit the grave.

vocab.note: In kana: its second kanji is outside the course list.
vocab.example: {仏教|ぶっきょう}では、{人|ひと}はりんねから{抜|ぬ}け{出|だ}すことを{目指|めざ}すとされる。
vocab.exampleEn: In Buddhism, people are said to aim to escape the cycle of rebirth.

vocab.note: Opposite: {現世|げんせ} (this life).
vocab.example: {来世|らいせ}でもまた{会|あ}おうと、{二人|ふたり}は{約束|やくそく}した。
vocab.exampleEn: The two promised to meet again in the next life.

meanings: the other world (the world of the dead)
vocab.note: Opposite: この{世|よ}. Everyday, a little humorous: あの{世|よ}に{持|も}っていけない (you can't take it with you).
vocab.example: お{金|かね}はあの{世|よ}まで{持|も}っていけないよ。
vocab.exampleEn: You can't take money with you to the other world.

meanings: this world (the world of the living)
vocab.note: この{世|よ}を{去|さ}る: to depart this life.
vocab.example: この{世|よ}にかんぺきな{人間|にんげん}などいない。
vocab.exampleEn: There's no such thing as a perfect person in this world.

meanings: divine retribution (a curse from a spirit or god)
vocab.note: In kana: its kanji is outside the course list. Verb: たたる.
vocab.example: {古|ふる}い{木|き}を{切|き}るとたたりがあると、{村|むら}では{言|い}い{伝|つた}えられている。
vocab.exampleEn: In the village it has long been said that cutting down the old tree will bring a curse.

meanings: votive tablet (wooden plaque with a wish, at a shrine)
vocab.note: People write wishes on them, such as passing an exam.
vocab.example: {受験生|じゅけんせい}たちの{絵馬|えま}が、{境内|けいだい}にびっしりと{掛|か}けられている。
vocab.exampleEn: The precincts are hung thick with wooden wish plaques left by exam candidates.

meanings: offering of money (coins at a shrine or temple)
vocab.note: In kana: its first kanji is outside the course list. さいせん{箱|ばこ}: the offering box.
vocab.example: {五円玉|ごえんだま}をさいせん{箱|ばこ}に{入|い}れて、{手|て}を{合|あ}わせた。
vocab.exampleEn: I put a five-yen coin into the offering box and put my hands together.

vocab.note: In kana: its first kanji is outside the course list.
vocab.example: お{正月|しょうがつ}には、みこさんがお{守|まも}りを{売|う}っている。
vocab.exampleEn: At New Year, the shrine maidens sell good-luck charms.

meanings: memorial service (Buddhist prayers for the dead)
vocab.note: Also 〜する. Also for things: {人形|にんぎょう}{供養|くよう} (a service for old dolls).
vocab.example: {祖母|そぼ}の{七回忌|ななかいき}の{供養|くよう}を{寺|てら}で{行|おこな}った。
vocab.exampleEn: We held a memorial service at the temple for the sixth anniversary of Grandmother's death.

meanings: to offer (to the gods, the Buddha or the dead)
vocab.note: Group 2. ます form: {供|そな}えます; て form: {供|そな}えて. Sounds like N3's {備|そな}える (to prepare). Noun: お{供|そな}え.
vocab.example: {墓|はか}に{花|はな}と{線香|せんこう}を{供|そな}えた。
vocab.exampleEn: We offered flowers and incense at the grave.

meanings: offering (food or flowers for the dead or the gods)
vocab.note: お{供|そな}え{物|もの}. Also the round rice cakes of New Year (お{供|そな}え{餅|もち}).
vocab.example: お{供|そな}えの{果物|くだもの}を、{後|あと}で{家族|かぞく}でいただいた。
vocab.exampleEn: Afterwards, the family ate the fruit that had been offered.

vocab.note: In kana: its first kanji is outside the course list. ごめいふくをお{祈|いの}りします (a Buddhist phrase).
vocab.example: {心|こころ}よりごめいふくをお{祈|いの}り{申|もう}し{上|あ}げます。
vocab.exampleEn: I pray from my heart that they may rest in peace.

vocab.note: な-adjective. Often of fortune-telling, healing and "power spots"; can sound slightly sceptical.
vocab.example: {最近|さいきん}は、スピリチュアルな{話題|わだい}に{関心|かんしん}を{持|も}つ{若者|わかもの}も{多|おお}い。
vocab.exampleEn: These days many young people are interested in spiritual topics.

vocab.note: Also a fan of a brand or person, half joking.
vocab.example: その{寺|てら}には、{全国|ぜんこく}から{信者|しんじゃ}が{集|あつ}まる。
vocab.exampleEn: Believers gather at that temple from all over the country.

vocab.note: Also 〜する. {信心深|しんじんぶか}い (devout). Sounds like N4's {新人|しんじん} (newcomer).
vocab.example: {祖父|そふ}は{信心深|しんじんぶか}く、{毎朝|まいあさ}{仏壇|ぶつだん}に{手|て}を{合|あ}わせていた。
vocab.exampleEn: My grandfather was devout and put his hands together at the family altar every morning.

vocab.note: Also 〜する. Sounds like N2's {不況|ふきょう} (recession).
vocab.example: {十六世紀|じゅうろくせいき}、{宣教師|せんきょうし}たちが{日本|にほん}で{布教|ふきょう}を{始|はじ}めた。
vocab.exampleEn: In the sixteenth century, missionaries began spreading their faith in Japan.

meanings: worldly desires (Buddhist: passions that cause suffering)
vocab.note: 煩 is lesson 16's kanji. {子|こ}{煩悩|ぼんのう}: doting on one's children.
vocab.example: {煩悩|ぼんのう}を{捨|す}てるのは、{僧侶|そうりょ}にとっても{簡単|かんたん}ではない。
vocab.exampleEn: Casting off worldly desires isn't easy even for a priest.

meanings: attaining Buddhahood (resting in peace after death)
vocab.note: Also 〜する. Of a ghost: to be at peace at last.
vocab.example: {思|おも}い{残|のこ}すことなく{成仏|じょうぶつ}してほしい。
vocab.exampleEn: I hope they rest in peace with nothing left undone.

vocab.note: Also 〜する. {大往生|だいおうじょう}: dying peacefully at a great age. Also {往生|おうじょう}する (to be stuck) and {立|た}ち{往生|おうじょう} (lesson 1).
vocab.example: {祖父|そふ}は{百歳|ひゃくさい}で{大往生|だいおうじょう}を{遂|と}げた。
vocab.exampleEn: My grandfather died peacefully at a hundred.

vocab.note: Usually お{通夜|つや}. 通 is read つ here (a rare on'yomi), 夜 や.
vocab.example: {仕事|しごと}の{後|あと}、お{通夜|つや}に{駆|か}けつけた。
vocab.exampleEn: After work I hurried to the wake.

vocab.note: Usually the day after the wake.
vocab.example: {告別式|こくべつしき}には、{会社|かいしゃ}を{代表|だいひょう}して{部長|ぶちょう}が{参列|さんれつ}した。
vocab.exampleEn: The department head attended the farewell ceremony on behalf of the company.

vocab.note: In a special envelope ({香典袋|こうでんぶくろ}). The family often sends a gift in return ({香典返|こうでんがえ}し).
vocab.example: {受付|うけつけ}で{香典|こうでん}を{渡|わた}し、{記帳|きちょう}した。
vocab.exampleEn: At the reception I handed over my condolence money and signed the book.

meanings: portrait of the deceased (photo at a funeral)
vocab.note: The framed photo on the altar.
vocab.example: {遺影|いえい}の{祖母|そぼ}は、{穏|おだ}やかに{笑|わら}っていた。
vocab.exampleEn: In the funeral portrait, Grandmother was smiling gently.

vocab.note: After cremation; also remains found long after death.
vocab.example: {遺骨|いこつ}は{四十九日|しじゅうくにち}の{法要|ほうよう}の{後|あと}、{墓|はか}に{納|おさ}められた。
vocab.exampleEn: The ashes were placed in the grave after the service on the forty-ninth day.

meanings: interment of ashes (placing them in a grave)
vocab.note: Also 〜する. 納 is lesson 26's kanji.
vocab.example: {納骨|のうこつ}は{一周忌|いっしゅうき}に{合|あ}わせて{行|おこな}うことにした。
vocab.exampleEn: We decided to inter the ashes at the first anniversary.

meanings: Buddhist memorial service (held by a family)
vocab.note: Everyday word; {法要|ほうよう} is more formal.
vocab.example: {法事|ほうじ}で{久|ひさ}しぶりに{親戚|しんせき}が{集|あつ}まった。
vocab.exampleEn: The relatives got together for the first time in a while at the memorial service.

vocab.note: {四十九日|しじゅうくにち}の{法要|ほうよう}, {一周忌|いっしゅうき}{法要|ほうよう}.
vocab.example: {法要|ほうよう}は{午前|ごぜん}{十時|じゅうじ}から{本堂|ほんどう}で{営|いとな}まれる。
vocab.exampleEn: The memorial rite will be held in the main hall from ten in the morning.

vocab.note: Then {三回忌|さんかいき} (second anniversary), {七回忌|ななかいき}…: the counting includes the year of death.
vocab.example: {父|ちち}の{一周忌|いっしゅうき}に、{家族|かぞく}と{親戚|しんせき}が{集|あつ}まった。
vocab.exampleEn: Family and relatives gathered on the first anniversary of Father's death.

vocab.note: Where the main image of the Buddha is kept.
vocab.example: {本堂|ほんどう}に{上|あ}がる{前|まえ}に、{靴|くつ}を{脱|ぬ}いでください。
vocab.exampleEn: Please take off your shoes before going up into the main hall.

vocab.note: 境 read けい here (N3's 境 is usually きょう). A reading trap.
vocab.example: {神社|じんじゃ}の{境内|けいだい}では、{毎月|まいつき}こっとう{市|いち}が{開|ひら}かれる。
vocab.exampleEn: An antiques market is held every month in the shrine precincts.

vocab.note: Rites at a shrine; many festivals began as {神事|しんじ}.
vocab.example: {相撲|すもう}はもともと、{豊作|ほうさく}を{祈|いの}る{神事|しんじ}だった。
vocab.exampleEn: Sumo was originally a Shinto ritual praying for a good harvest.

vocab.note: Priests, ministers, monks: a general word.
vocab.example: {式|しき}では、{宗教|しゅうきょう}の{異|こと}なる{聖職者|せいしょくしゃ}たちが{並|なら}んで{祈|いの}った。
vocab.exampleEn: At the ceremony, clergy of different religions prayed side by side.

vocab.note: A Catholic priest is a {神父|しんぷ}.
vocab.example: {結婚式|けっこんしき}は、{教会|きょうかい}の{牧師|ぼくし}が{執|と}り{行|おこな}った。
vocab.exampleEn: The wedding was conducted by the church's pastor.

vocab.note: Sounds like N3's {新婦|しんぷ} (bride).
vocab.example: {神父|しんぷ}は{静|しず}かな{声|こえ}で{祈|いの}りをささげた。
vocab.exampleEn: The priest offered a prayer in a quiet voice.

vocab.note: Sounds like N2's {境界|きょうかい} (boundary) and {協会|きょうかい} (association).
vocab.example: {日曜日|にちようび}の{朝|あさ}、{教会|きょうかい}の{鐘|かね}が{鳴|な}った。
vocab.exampleEn: On Sunday morning the church bell rang.

vocab.note: Also 〜する. The Buddhist word with the same kanji is read らいはい.
vocab.example: {毎週|まいしゅう}{日曜日|にちようび}に{礼拝|れいはい}に{通|かよ}っている。
vocab.exampleEn: I go to the worship service every Sunday.

vocab.note: Also 〜する. {四国|しこく}{八十八|はちじゅうはち}か{所|しょ}{巡|めぐ}り is a famous Buddhist pilgrimage.
vocab.example: {定年後|ていねんご}、{父|ちち}は{歩|ある}いて{巡礼|じゅんれい}の{旅|たび}に{出|で}た。
vocab.exampleEn: After retiring, my father set out on a pilgrimage on foot.

meanings: fortune (one's luck as told by fortune-telling)
vocab.note: {今年|ことし}の{運勢|うんせい}, {運勢|うんせい}を{占|うらな}う.
vocab.example: {雑誌|ざっし}の{最後|さいご}のページに、{今月|こんげつ}の{運勢|うんせい}が{載|の}っている。
vocab.exampleEn: This month's horoscope is on the last page of the magazine.

meanings: lucky charm (an object said to bring good fortune)
vocab.note: {招|まね}き{猫|ねこ}, だるま and {熊手|くまで} are typical {縁起物|えんぎもの}.
vocab.example: {店|みせ}の{入口|いりぐち}には、{縁起物|えんぎもの}の{招|まね}き{猫|ねこ}が{置|お}いてある。
vocab.exampleEn: A beckoning cat is placed at the shop entrance for good luck.

meanings: to be possessed by a sudden evil impulse (to give in to temptation)
vocab.note: Excuse for a bad act: つい{魔|ま}が{差|さ}して (I just gave in to temptation).
vocab.example: {魔|ま}が{差|さ}したとしか{言|い}いようがない。
vocab.exampleEn: All I can say is that something came over me.

vocab.note: {数学|すうがく}は{私|わたし}にとって{鬼門|きもん}だ: maths is my weak spot.
vocab.example: {古|ふる}い{家|いえ}では、{鬼門|きもん}の{方角|ほうがく}に{玄関|げんかん}を{作|つく}らなかったという。
vocab.exampleEn: In old houses, it's said, people didn't put the entrance on the unlucky north-east side.

meanings: good or bad luck (fortune, either way)
vocab.note: {吉凶|きっきょう}を{占|うらな}う: to read whether something will be lucky.
vocab.example: {昔|むかし}の{人|ひと}は、{旅立|たびだ}ちの{日|ひ}の{吉凶|きっきょう}まで{気|き}にした。
vocab.exampleEn: People long ago even worried about whether the day they set out would be lucky.

vocab.note: {霊感|れいかん}が{強|つよ}い: sensitive to spirits.
vocab.example: {霊感|れいかん}が{強|つよ}い{友人|ゆうじん}は、{古|ふる}い{旅館|りょかん}に{泊|と}まりたがらない。
vocab.exampleEn: A friend who claims to sense spirits doesn't like staying at old inns.

vocab.note: Also of the past: {過去|かこ}の{亡霊|ぼうれい}.
vocab.example: その{城|しろ}には、{戦|たたか}いで{死|し}んだ{武士|ぶし}の{亡霊|ぼうれい}が{出|で}るという。
vocab.exampleEn: They say the ghosts of warriors who died in battle appear in that castle.

vocab.note: 霊 read りょう here. Also あくれい.
vocab.example: {悪霊|あくりょう}を{追|お}い{払|はら}うための{儀式|ぎしき}が{行|おこな}われた。
vocab.exampleEn: A ritual was held to drive out evil spirits.

meanings: the dead (dead people, in reports and religion)
vocab.note: {死者|ししゃ}{数|すう}: the number of dead. Sounds like N3's {支社|ししゃ} (branch office).
vocab.example: {死者|ししゃ}を{悼|いた}む{気持|きも}ちに、{国境|こっきょう}はない。
vocab.exampleEn: There are no borders to the wish to mourn the dead.

vocab.note: Also figurative: {歩行者|ほこうしゃ}{天国|てんごく} (a car-free street).
vocab.example: {天国|てんごく}のおじいちゃんも、きっと{喜|よろこ}んでいるよ。
vocab.exampleEn: Grandpa in heaven must be happy too.

vocab.note: Also 〜する. {合掌|がっしょう}{造|づく}り: the steep-roofed farmhouses of Shirakawa-gō.
vocab.example: {遺影|いえい}の{前|まえ}で、{静|しず}かに{合掌|がっしょう}した。
vocab.exampleEn: I put my palms together quietly before the portrait of the deceased.

meanings: no religion (not belonging to any faith)
vocab.note: {無宗教|むしゅうきょう}の{葬儀|そうぎ}: a non-religious funeral.
vocab.example: {自分|じぶん}は{無宗教|むしゅうきょう}だと{言|い}う{人|ひと}でも、{初詣|はつもうで}には{行|い}く。
vocab.exampleEn: Even people who say they have no religion go to the shrine at New Year.

meanings: like giving an iron club to an ogre (even stronger than before)
vocab.note: Said when someone already strong gets an extra advantage.
vocab.example: {経験|けいけん}{豊富|ほうふ}な{彼|かれ}が{加|くわ}われば、{鬼|おに}に{金棒|かなぼう}だ。
vocab.exampleEn: If someone as experienced as him joins, we'll be unstoppable.

vocab.note: Sounds like N2's {礼状|れいじょう} (thank-you letter).
vocab.example: {四国|しこく}には{八十八|はちじゅうはち}の{霊場|れいじょう}がある。
vocab.exampleEn: There are eighty-eight sacred sites in Shikoku.

vocab.note: Formal word for N4's {塾|じゅく}.
vocab.example: {小学生|しょうがくせい}のころから{学習塾|がくしゅうじゅく}に{通|かよ}う{子供|こども}も{少|すく}なくない。
vocab.exampleEn: Quite a few children go to cram school from primary school age.

meanings: doctor of learning (everyday word; also an expert)
vocab.note: Special reading. {物知|ものし}り{博士|はかせ}: someone who knows everything. The degree is {博士号|はくしごう}.
vocab.example: {弟|おとうと}は{恐竜|きょうりゅう}{博士|はかせ}と{呼|よ}ばれるほど{恐竜|きょうりゅう}に{詳|くわ}しい。
vocab.exampleEn: My younger brother knows so much about dinosaurs that they call him the dinosaur professor.

meanings: erudite (widely read, knowing a great deal)
vocab.note: な-adjective. {博識|はくしき}な{人|ひと}. Also a noun: {博識|はくしき}ぶり.
vocab.example: {祖父|そふ}は{歴史|れきし}はおろか{植物|しょくぶつ}にも{詳|くわ}しい{博識|はくしき}な{人|ひと}だった。
vocab.exampleEn: My grandfather was a learned man who knew all about plants, never mind history.

vocab.note: {博士号|はくしごう}を{取得|しゅとく}する. 博士 is read はくし in formal words.
vocab.example: {三十|さんじゅう}{代|だい}で{働|はたら}きながら{博士号|はくしごう}を{取得|しゅとく}した。
vocab.exampleEn: They earned a doctorate in their thirties while working.

vocab.note: After a master's: {修士|しゅうし}{課程|かてい} → {博士課程|はくしかてい}.
vocab.example: {博士課程|はくしかてい}に{進|すす}むかどうか、{指導|しどう}{教員|きょういん}に{相談|そうだん}した。
vocab.exampleEn: I consulted my supervisor about whether to go on to a doctoral programme.

meanings: licensed teacher (official title at a school)
vocab.note: On documents and in news: {中学校|ちゅうがっこう}{教諭|きょうゆ}. In speech {先生|せんせい}.
vocab.example: {記事|きじ}によると、{容疑者|ようぎしゃ}は{市内|しない}の{小学校|しょうがっこう}の{教諭|きょうゆ}だった。
vocab.exampleEn: According to the article, the suspect was a teacher at a primary school in the city.

meanings: to admonish (gently, to make someone understand)
vocab.note: Group 1. ます form: {諭|さと}します; て form: {諭|さと}して. Of a parent, teacher or elder: {優|やさ}しく{諭|さと}す.
vocab.example: {泣|な}きじゃくる{子供|こども}を、{母親|ははおや}は{静|しず}かに{諭|さと}した。
vocab.exampleEn: The mother quietly talked sense to the sobbing child.

vocab.note: Also 〜する. {啓発|けいはつ}{活動|かつどう} (an awareness campaign), {自己|じこ}{啓発|けいはつ} (self-improvement).
vocab.example: {交通|こうつう}{安全|あんぜん}の{啓発|けいはつ}のため、{警察|けいさつ}が{学校|がっこう}で{講演|こうえん}を{行|おこな}った。
vocab.exampleEn: The police gave a talk at the school to raise awareness of road safety.

meanings: to cultivate (an ability or quality over time)
vocab.note: Group 1. ます form: {培|つちか}います; て form: {培|つちか}って. {力|ちから}を{培|つちか}う, {経験|けいけん}で{培|つちか}われた{判断力|はんだんりょく}.
vocab.example: {部活動|ぶかつどう}で{培|つちか}った{粘|ねば}り{強|づよ}さが、{社会|しゃかい}に{出|で}てから{役|やく}に{立|た}った。
vocab.exampleEn: The perseverance I built up in school club activities came in useful once I started work.

meanings: culture (growing cells or bacteria in a lab)
vocab.note: Also 〜する. {細胞|さいぼう}を{培養|ばいよう}する.
vocab.example: {研究室|けんきゅうしつ}では、{細胞|さいぼう}の{培養|ばいよう}に{一|いっ}か{月|げつ}かかった。
vocab.exampleEn: In the lab, culturing the cells took a month.

vocab.note: Also 〜する: {読書|どくしょ}を{奨励|しょうれい}する. {奨励|しょうれい}{金|きん}: a grant.
vocab.example: {市|し}は、{若|わか}い{農業|のうぎょう}{従事者|じゅうじしゃ}に{奨励|しょうれい}{金|きん}を{出|だ}している。
vocab.exampleEn: The city gives grants to young people working in farming.

vocab.note: Group 3. ます form: {推奨|すいしょう}します; て form: {推奨|すいしょう}して. Of authorities and makers: {推奨|すいしょう}{環境|かんきょう} (recommended system requirements). The noun {推奨|すいしょう} is common too.
vocab.example: {専門家|せんもんか}は、{一日|いちにち}{三十分|さんじゅっぷん}の{運動|うんどう}を{推奨|すいしょう}している。
vocab.exampleEn: Experts recommend thirty minutes of exercise a day.

vocab.note: Sounds like N3's {小学生|しょうがくせい} (primary pupil); context tells them apart.
vocab.example: {奨学生|しょうがくせい}に{選|えら}ばれ、{学費|がくひ}の{心配|しんぱい}がなくなった。
vocab.exampleEn: I was chosen as a scholarship student, and no longer had to worry about fees.

vocab.note: Also {寮|りょう} (carried).
vocab.example: {一年生|いちねんせい}の{間|あいだ}は、{全員|ぜんいん}が{学生寮|がくせいりょう}に{住|す}むことになっている。
vocab.exampleEn: All first-year students are required to live in the student dormitory.

vocab.note: Compare {天才|てんさい} (a genius, born so); {秀才|しゅうさい} suggests hard work and good marks.
vocab.example: {彼|かれ}は{学年|がくねん}{一|いち}の{秀才|しゅうさい}として{知|し}られていた。
vocab.exampleEn: He was known as the brightest student in his year.

meanings: to stand out (excel in a field, written)
vocab.note: Group 2. ます form: {秀|ひい}でます; て form: {秀|ひい}でて. 〜に{秀|ひい}でる: {語学|ごがく}に{秀|ひい}でる. Written.
vocab.example: {彼女|かのじょ}は{幼|おさな}いころから{音楽|おんがく}に{秀|ひい}でていた。
vocab.exampleEn: She excelled at music from an early age.

meanings: superb (outstandingly good, of work or ideas)
vocab.note: な-adjective. {秀逸|しゅういつ}な{作品|さくひん}, {秀逸|しゅういつ}なアイデア. Written.
vocab.example: {今年|ことし}の{応募|おうぼ}{作品|さくひん}の{中|なか}で、この{詩|し}は{特|とく}に{秀逸|しゅういつ}だった。
vocab.exampleEn: Among this year's entries, this poem was particularly outstanding.

vocab.note: Also 〜する. {履修|りしゅう}{登録|とうろく}: course registration.
vocab.example: {卒業|そつぎょう}までに、{外国語|がいこくご}を{二|ふた}つ{履修|りしゅう}しなければならない。
vocab.exampleEn: Before graduating, students must take courses in two foreign languages.

vocab.note: Special reading: 草 ぞう, 履 り. Worn with kimono.
vocab.example: {着物|きもの}に{合|あ}わせて、{新|あたら}しい{草履|ぞうり}を{買|か}った。
vocab.exampleEn: I bought new sandals to go with the kimono.

meanings: history (record of past activity: browsing, calls, career)
vocab.note: {閲覧|えつらん}{履歴|りれき}, {着信|ちゃくしん}{履歴|りれき}. {履歴書|りれきしょ} (CV) is carried.
vocab.example: {検索|けんさく}{履歴|りれき}を{見|み}れば、その{人|ひと}の{関心|かんしん}がだいたい{分|わ}かる。
vocab.exampleEn: Look at someone's search history and you can roughly tell what they're interested in.

vocab.note: {必須|ひっす}{科目|かもく}, {必須|ひっす}{条件|じょうけん}. ひつ + す → ひっす, not ひっしゅ.
vocab.example: この{仕事|しごと}では、{英語|えいご}の{読解力|どっかいりょく}が{必須|ひっす}だ。
vocab.exampleEn: In this job, the ability to read English is essential.

vocab.note: In titles: {国語|こくご}{辞典|じてん}, {英和|えいわ}{辞典|じてん}. Everyday: {辞書|じしょ}.
vocab.example: {大学|だいがく}{図書館|としょかん}には、{古|ふる}い{漢和|かんわ}{辞典|じてん}がそろっている。
vocab.exampleEn: The university library has a complete set of old kanji dictionaries.

vocab.note: {古典|こてん}{文学|ぶんがく}, {古典|こてん}を{読|よ}む. Sounds like N2's {個展|こてん} (solo exhibition).
vocab.example: {古典|こてん}といえども、{現代|げんだい}の{読者|どくしゃ}に{響|ひび}く{言葉|ことば}は{多|おお}い。
vocab.exampleEn: They may be classics, but they contain many words that speak to today's readers.

vocab.note: {典型|てんけい}{例|れい}; {典型的|てんけいてき} (typical) is the common form.
vocab.example: これは{詰|つ}め{込|こ}み{教育|きょういく}の{失敗|しっぱい}の{典型|てんけい}だ。
vocab.exampleEn: This is a typical example of the failure of cramming.

vocab.note: な-adjective. {典型的|てんけいてき}な{例|れい}, {典型的|てんけいてき}な{日本|にほん}の{家庭|かてい}.
vocab.example: {朝|あさ}ご{飯|はん}にご{飯|はん}とみそ{汁|しる}というのは、{典型的|てんけいてき}な{和食|わしょく}だ。
vocab.exampleEn: Rice and miso soup for breakfast is a typical Japanese meal.

meanings: perk (special benefit for members or buyers)
vocab.note: {会員|かいいん}{特典|とくてん}, {初回|しょかい}{特典|とくてん}. Sounds like N3's {得点|とくてん} (score).
vocab.example: {学生|がくせい}には、{入館料|にゅうかんりょう}が{半額|はんがく}になる{特典|とくてん}がある。
vocab.exampleEn: Students get the benefit of half-price admission.

vocab.note: {記念|きねん}{式典|しきてん}, {式典|しきてん}に{出席|しゅっせき}する.
vocab.example: {創立|そうりつ}{記念|きねん}の{式典|しきてん}で、{卒業生|そつぎょうせい}{代表|だいひょう}がスピーチをした。
vocab.exampleEn: At the ceremony marking the founding, a representative of the graduates gave a speech.

vocab.note: {試験|しけん}{範囲|はんい}, {範囲|はんい}{内|ない}.
vocab.example: {試験|しけん}の{範囲|はんい}は、{教科書|きょうかしょ}の{五十|ごじゅう}ページまでです。
vocab.exampleEn: The exam covers the textbook up to page fifty.

vocab.note: {模範|もはん}{解答|かいとう} (model answers), {模範的|もはんてき}な{生徒|せいと}.
vocab.example: {先輩|せんぱい}の{態度|たいど}は、{後輩|こうはい}たちの{模範|もはん}となった。
vocab.exampleEn: The senior student's attitude became a model for the juniors.

vocab.note: {社会|しゃかい}{規範|きはん}, {行動|こうどう}{規範|きはん}. Written.
vocab.example: {社会|しゃかい}の{規範|きはん}は、{時代|じだい}とともに{変|か}わっていく。
vocab.exampleEn: Social norms change with the times.

vocab.note: な-adjective. {広範|こうはん}な{知識|ちしき}, {広範|こうはん}{囲|い}に (over a wide area). Sounds like N2's {後半|こうはん}.
vocab.example: その{講義|こうぎ}は、{古代|こだい}から{現代|げんだい}までの{広範|こうはん}な{内容|ないよう}を{扱|あつか}う。
vocab.exampleEn: The lectures cover a wide range, from ancient times to the present.

vocab.note: Also 〜する. {試行錯誤|しこうさくご}を{重|かさ}ねる.
vocab.example: {試行錯誤|しこうさくご}を{繰|く}り{返|かえ}して、{自分|じぶん}に{合|あ}った{勉強法|べんきょうほう}を{見|み}つけた。
vocab.exampleEn: Through repeated trial and error, I found a way of studying that suits me.

vocab.note: Also 〜する. {目|め}の{錯覚|さっかく}: an optical illusion.
vocab.example: {分|わ}かったつもりになるのは、よくある{錯覚|さっかく}だ。
vocab.exampleEn: Thinking you've understood is a common illusion.

meanings: mingling (of feelings or lines that cross)
vocab.note: Also 〜する: {期待|きたい}と{不安|ふあん}が{交錯|こうさく}する.
vocab.example: {入学式|にゅうがくしき}の{朝|あさ}は、{期待|きたい}と{不安|ふあん}が{交錯|こうさく}していた。
vocab.exampleEn: On the morning of the entrance ceremony, hope and anxiety were mixed together.

meanings: putting into practice (action, not just theory)
vocab.note: Also 〜する. Opposite: {理論|りろん}.
vocab.example: {学|まな}んだことを{実践|じっせん}しなければ、{本当|ほんとう}の{力|ちから}にはならない。
vocab.exampleEn: Unless you put what you've learned into practice, it won't become real ability.

vocab.note: Also 〜する: {状況|じょうきょう}を{把握|はあく}する. Very common in business and news.
vocab.example: {新|あたら}しい{担任|たんにん}は、{一週間|いっしゅうかん}でクラス{全員|ぜんいん}の{名前|なまえ}を{把握|はあく}した。
vocab.exampleEn: Within a week, the new homeroom teacher had got the whole class's names.

vocab.note: Group 1. ます form: {握|にぎ}ります; て form: {握|にぎ}って. {手|て}を{握|にぎ}る, {鍵|かぎ}を{握|にぎ}る (to hold the key), {寿司|すし}を{握|にぎ}る.
vocab.example: {成功|せいこう}の{鍵|かぎ}を{握|にぎ}るのは、{毎日|まいにち}の{積|つ}み{重|かさ}ねだ。
vocab.exampleEn: The key to success lies in what you build up every day.

vocab.note: Also 〜する.
vocab.example: {卒業式|そつぎょうしき}の{後|あと}、{恩師|おんし}と{固|かた}く{握手|あくしゅ}を{交|か}わした。
vocab.exampleEn: After the graduation ceremony, I shook hands firmly with my old teacher.

vocab.note: Measured in school fitness tests.
vocab.example: {体力|たいりょく}テストで、{握力|あくりょく}を{測|はか}った。
vocab.exampleEn: We measured grip strength in the fitness test.

meanings: compound word (of two or more kanji)
vocab.note: {四字熟語|よじじゅくご} (carried): a four-character compound.
vocab.example: {新聞|しんぶん}には、{漢字|かんじ}の{熟語|じゅくご}が{多|おお}く{使|つか}われている。
vocab.exampleEn: Newspapers use a lot of kanji compounds.

vocab.note: Also 〜する. {熟練|じゅくれん}した{職人|しょくにん}, {熟練|じゅくれん}の{技|わざ}.
vocab.example: この{作業|さぎょう}には{熟練|じゅくれん}が{必要|ひつよう}で、{新人|しんじん}にはまだ{任|まか}せられない。
vocab.exampleEn: This work requires experience, so it can't be left to newcomers yet.

vocab.note: な-adjective. {未熟|みじゅく}{者|もの}: a novice (also said humbly of oneself).
vocab.example: {未熟|みじゅく}な{私|わたし}ですが、どうぞよろしくお{願|ねが}いいたします。
vocab.exampleEn: I'm still inexperienced, but I hope you'll bear with me.

vocab.note: Also 〜する: {成熟|せいじゅく}した{社会|しゃかい}.
vocab.example: {市場|しじょう}が{成熟|せいじゅく}し、{急|きゅう}な{成長|せいちょう}は{見込|みこ}めない。
vocab.exampleEn: The market has matured, and rapid growth can't be expected.

vocab.note: Also 〜する. {熟読|じゅくどく}の{上|うえ}、ご{署名|しょめい}ください (please read carefully before signing).
vocab.example: {契約書|けいやくしょ}は{熟読|じゅくどく}してから{署名|しょめい}すること。
vocab.exampleEn: Read the contract carefully before signing it.

vocab.note: Also 〜する: {地元|じもと}を{熟知|じゅくち}している.
vocab.example: この{地域|ちいき}を{熟知|じゅくち}した{案内人|あんないにん}と{一緒|いっしょ}に{歩|ある}いた。
vocab.exampleEn: We walked with a guide who knew the area inside out.

vocab.note: Also 〜する. ジュク + コウ → じゅっこう. {熟考|じゅっこう}の{末|すえ}: after long deliberation.
vocab.example: {熟考|じゅっこう}の{末|すえ}、{留学|りゅうがく}を{一年|いちねん}{延|の}ばすことにした。
vocab.exampleEn: After long deliberation, I decided to put off studying abroad for a year.

vocab.note: Also 〜する: {苦手|にがて}を{克服|こくふく}する.
vocab.example: {毎日|まいにち}{人前|ひとまえ}で{話|はな}す{練習|れんしゅう}をして、{緊張|きんちょう}を{克服|こくふく}した。
vocab.exampleEn: By practising speaking in front of people every day, I overcame my nerves.

vocab.note: な-adjective. {克明|こくめい}に{記録|きろく}する, {克明|こくめい}な{描写|びょうしゃ}.
vocab.example: {祖父|そふ}は{毎日|まいにち}の{天気|てんき}を{克明|こくめい}に{記録|きろく}していた。
vocab.exampleEn: My grandfather kept a detailed record of the weather every day.

vocab.note: Also 〜する: {詩|し}を{暗唱|あんしょう}する. Not N3's {暗証|あんしょう}{番号|ばんごう} (PIN), which has 証.
vocab.example: {小学校|しょうがっこう}で、{有名|ゆうめい}な{詩|し}を{暗唱|あんしょう}させられた。
vocab.exampleEn: At primary school we were made to recite famous poems by heart.

meanings: advocacy (proposing a new idea or theory)
vocab.note: Also 〜する: {新|あたら}しい{理論|りろん}を{提唱|ていしょう}する.
vocab.example: その{教育法|きょういくほう}は、{百年|ひゃくねん}ほど{前|まえ}に{一人|ひとり}の{医師|いし}が{提唱|ていしょう}したものだ。
vocab.exampleEn: That method of education was put forward by a doctor about a hundred years ago.

vocab.note: Group 2. ます form: {唱|とな}えます; て form: {唱|とな}えて. {念仏|ねんぶつ}を{唱|とな}える, {異議|いぎ}を{唱|とな}える (to raise an objection).
vocab.example: {会議|かいぎ}で{一人|ひとり}だけ{異議|いぎ}を{唱|とな}えた。
vocab.exampleEn: Only one person raised an objection at the meeting.

vocab.note: Also 〜する. {合唱|がっしょう}コンクール: a choir contest.
vocab.example: {文化祭|ぶんかさい}では、クラスごとに{合唱|がっしょう}を{発表|はっぴょう}する。
vocab.exampleEn: At the school festival, each class performs a choral piece.

vocab.note: Mostly {一斉|いっせい}に (all together) and {一斉|いっせい}〜: {一斉|いっせい}{休校|きゅうこう}.
vocab.example: チャイムが{鳴|な}ると、{生徒|せいと}たちは{一斉|いっせい}に{立|た}ち{上|あ}がった。
vocab.exampleEn: When the bell rang, the pupils stood up all at once.

vocab.note: Also 〜する: {卓越|たくえつ}した{技術|ぎじゅつ}.
vocab.example: {彼女|かのじょ}の{卓越|たくえつ}した{語学力|ごがくりょく}は、{現場|げんば}で{高|たか}く{評価|ひょうか}された。
vocab.exampleEn: Her outstanding language skills were highly valued on the job.

vocab.note: {食卓|しょくたく}を{囲|かこ}む: to sit round the table together.
vocab.example: {日曜日|にちようび}の{夜|よる}は、{家族|かぞく}{全員|ぜんいん}で{食卓|しょくたく}を{囲|かこ}む。
vocab.exampleEn: On Sunday evenings, the whole family sits down to eat together.

vocab.note: Short for {電子|でんし}{式|しき}{卓上|たくじょう}{計算機|けいさんき}.
vocab.example: {簿記|ぼき}の{試験|しけん}には、{電卓|でんたく}を{持|も}ち{込|こ}める。
vocab.exampleEn: You may bring a calculator into the bookkeeping exam.

vocab.note: {会員|かいいん}{名簿|めいぼ}, {卒業生|そつぎょうせい}{名簿|めいぼ}.
vocab.example: {同窓会|どうそうかい}の{名簿|めいぼ}を{作|つく}るため、{連絡先|れんらくさき}を{集|あつ}めている。
vocab.exampleEn: We're collecting contact details to make a list for the alumni association.

vocab.note: {簿記|ぼき}{検定|けんてい}: a bookkeeping qualification.
vocab.example: {就職|しゅうしょく}に{役立|やくだ}つと{思|おも}って、{簿記|ぼき}を{勉強|べんきょう}している。
vocab.exampleEn: I'm studying bookkeeping because I think it'll help me find a job.

vocab.note: {帳簿|ちょうぼ}をつける: to keep the books.
vocab.example: {小|ちい}さな{店|みせ}だが、{帳簿|ちょうぼ}は{毎日|まいにち}きちんとつけている。
vocab.exampleEn: It's a small shop, but the books are kept properly every day.

meanings: informal meeting (for discussion, as between parents and teachers)
vocab.note: {保護者|ほごしゃ}{懇談会|こんだんかい}: a parent–teacher meeting.
vocab.example: {来週|らいしゅう}、{進路|しんろ}についての{懇談会|こんだんかい}がある。
vocab.exampleEn: Next week there's a meeting to talk about pupils' future plans.

vocab.note: After a conference or at the start of a year.
vocab.example: {学会|がっかい}の{後|あと}、{懇親会|こんしんかい}で{多|おお}くの{研究者|けんきゅうしゃ}と{知|し}り{合|あ}った。
vocab.exampleEn: After the conference, I got to know many researchers at the social gathering.

meanings: thorough and kind (in explaining or helping)
vocab.note: な-adjective. {懇切|こんせつ}{丁寧|ていねい}に (very kindly and carefully).
vocab.example: {先生|せんせい}は{分|わ}からないところを{懇切|こんせつ}{丁寧|ていねい}に{教|おし}えてくれた。
vocab.exampleEn: The teacher explained what I didn't understand very patiently and carefully.

vocab.note: Also 〜する: {必死|ひっし}に{懇願|こんがん}する.
vocab.example: {試験|しけん}をもう{一度|いちど}{受|う}けさせてほしいと、{学生|がくせい}は{教授|きょうじゅ}に{懇願|こんがん}した。
