vocab.note: Group 3. ます form: {惨敗|ざんぱい}します; て form: {惨敗|ざんぱい}して. Read ざんぱい (惨 as ザン). Also the noun {惨敗|ざんぱい}.
vocab.example: {強豪|きょうごう}チームに{〇対七|ゼロたいなな}で{惨敗|ざんぱい}した。
vocab.exampleEn: We were crushed 0–7 by a top team.

meanings: cruel (horrible to behold, of a sight)
vocab.note: な-adjective. Also written {無残|むざん}. Of a sight or an outcome: {無惨|むざん}な{姿|すがた}.
vocab.example: {台風|たいふう}のあと、{公園|こうえん}の{桜|さくら}は{無惨|むざん}な{姿|すがた}になっていた。
vocab.exampleEn: After the typhoon, the cherry trees in the park were a pitiful sight.

meanings: to feel rushed (anxious to get it done in time)
vocab.note: Group 1. ます form: {焦|あせ}ります; て form: {焦|あせ}って. A group 1 verb that looks like group 2: {焦|あせ}らない, {焦|あせ}って. Causative {焦|あせ}らせる (to rush someone) is natural.
vocab.example: {締|し}め{切|き}りが{近|ちか}づいて、だんだん{焦|あせ}ってきた。
vocab.exampleEn: As the deadline approached, I started to feel rushed.

vocab.example: {周|まわ}りがみんな{就職|しゅうしょく}を{決|き}めて、{焦|あせ}りを{感|かん}じた。
vocab.exampleEn: Everyone around me had found a job, and I felt the pressure.

vocab.note: Written: {焦燥感|しょうそうかん} (a sense of agitation).
vocab.example: {何|なに}も{進|すす}まない{日々|ひび}に、{彼|かれ}は{焦燥感|しょうそうかん}を{募|つの}らせた。
vocab.exampleEn: As the days passed and nothing moved forward, his restlessness grew.

meanings: focus (of a lens or of attention)
vocab.note: {焦点|しょうてん}を{当|あ}てる (to focus on), {焦点|しょうてん}を{絞|しぼ}る (to narrow down). Sounds like carried {商店|しょうてん} (a shop).
vocab.example: {議論|ぎろん}の{焦点|しょうてん}は、{費用|ひよう}を{誰|だれ}が{負担|ふたん}するかに{移|うつ}った。
vocab.exampleEn: The focus of the debate shifted to who would bear the cost.

vocab.note: Group 2. ます form: {待|ま}ち{焦|こ}がれます; て form: {待|ま}ち{焦|こ}がれて.
vocab.example: {子|こ}どもたちは{夏休|なつやす}みを{待|ま}ち{焦|こ}がれている。
vocab.exampleEn: The children can hardly wait for the summer holidays.

vocab.note: Group 1. ます form: {嘆|なげ}きます; て form: {嘆|なげ}いて. Causative {嘆|なげ}かせる (to grieve someone) is natural: {親|おや}を{嘆|なげ}かせる.
vocab.example: {祖父|そふ}は、{町|まち}の{商店街|しょうてんがい}がさびれたことを{嘆|なげ}いている。
vocab.exampleEn: My grandfather laments how the town's shopping street has declined.

meanings: deplorable (regrettable, of a state of affairs)
vocab.note: Judgement of something you disapprove of, usually social: {嘆|なげ}かわしい{風潮|ふうちょう}.
vocab.example: {公共|こうきょう}の{場|ば}でのマナーの{低下|ていか}は{嘆|なげ}かわしい。
vocab.exampleEn: The decline in manners in public places is deplorable.

meanings: to marvel at (be struck with admiration)
vocab.note: Group 3. ます form: {感嘆|かんたん}します; て form: {感嘆|かんたん}して. Also the noun: {感嘆|かんたん}の{声|こえ} (a cry of admiration). Sounds like carried かんたん (simple).
vocab.example: {職人|しょくにん}の{技|わざ}の{細|こま}かさに、{見学者|けんがくしゃ}は{感嘆|かんたん}した。
vocab.exampleEn: The visitors marvelled at the fineness of the craftsman's work.

vocab.note: {悲嘆|ひたん}に{暮|く}れる: to be overcome with grief.
vocab.example: {一人息子|ひとりむすこ}を{亡|な}くし、{夫婦|ふうふ}は{悲嘆|ひたん}に{暮|く}れた。
vocab.exampleEn: Having lost their only son, the couple were overcome with grief.

meanings: to heave a sigh (in grief or dismay, literary)
vocab.note: Group 3. ます form: {嘆息|たんそく}します; て form: {嘆息|たんそく}して. Literary; everyday speech uses ため{息|いき}をつく.
vocab.example: {報告書|ほうこくしょ}を{読|よ}み{終|お}えた{部長|ぶちょう}は、{深|ふか}く{嘆息|たんそく}した。
vocab.exampleEn: The department head finished reading the report and heaved a deep sigh.

meanings: to be flustered (lose one's composure in a hurry)
vocab.note: Group 2. ます form: {慌|あわ}てます; て form: {慌|あわ}てて. {慌|あわ}てて (in a hurry): {慌|あわ}てて{家|いえ}を{出|で}る. Causative {慌|あわ}てさせる is natural.
vocab.example: {地震|じしん}のときは{慌|あわ}てずに、まず{身|み}の{安全|あんぜん}を{守|まも}ってください。
vocab.exampleEn: In an earthquake, don't panic: first protect yourself.

meanings: hectic (busy and rushed, of a time or place)
vocab.example: {年末|ねんまつ}は{何|なに}かと{慌|あわ}ただしい。
vocab.exampleEn: The end of the year is hectic, one way or another.

meanings: a mad rush (great haste and confusion)
vocab.note: {大慌|おおあわ}てで (in a mad rush).
vocab.example: {寝坊|ねぼう}して、{大慌|おおあわ}てで{駅|えき}まで{走|はし}った。
vocab.exampleEn: I overslept and ran to the station in a mad rush.

vocab.note: Three uses: a near miss ({惜|お}しい！), something too valuable to lose ({命|いのち}が{惜|お}しい), and a pity ({捨|す}てるのは{惜|お}しい).
vocab.example: あと{一点|いってん}で{合格|ごうかく}だったなんて、{惜|お}しかったね。
vocab.exampleEn: You missed passing by one point? So close.

meanings: to be sparing with (reluctant to give or lose)
vocab.note: Group 1. ます form: {惜|お}しみます; て form: {惜|お}しんで. {努力|どりょく}を{惜|お}しまない (to spare no effort), {別|わか}れを{惜|お}しむ (to be sad to part).
vocab.example: {彼女|かのじょ}は、{後輩|こうはい}を{育|そだ}てる{手間|てま}を{惜|お}しまなかった。
vocab.exampleEn: She never begrudged the effort of training the younger staff.

vocab.note: Written: {惜別|せきべつ}の{言葉|ことば}, {惜別|せきべつ}の{情|じょう}.
vocab.example: {退任|たいにん}する{校長|こうちょう}に、{生徒|せいと}{代表|だいひょう}が{惜別|せきべつ}の{言葉|ことば}を{述|の}べた。
vocab.exampleEn: A student representative gave words of farewell to the retiring head teacher.

meanings: reluctant to part (sad that it's ending)
vocab.note: {名残|なごり} is what lingers of something that has passed; {名残惜|なごりお}しい is the feeling at a parting.
vocab.example: {楽|たの}しい{旅|たび}も{今日|きょう}で{終|お}わりかと{思|おも}うと、{名残惜|なごりお}しい。
vocab.exampleEn: To think this lovely trip ends today — I hate to see it end.

vocab.note: Written; in speech {面倒臭|めんどうくさ}い.
vocab.example: {毎回|まいかい}{同|おな}じ{書類|しょるい}に{記入|きにゅう}するのは{煩|わずら}わしい。
vocab.exampleEn: Filling in the same forms every time is tiresome.

vocab.note: Group 1. ます form: {煩|わずら}わします; て form: {煩|わずら}わして. Polite formula: お{手|て}を{煩|わずら}わせてすみません (sorry to put you to the trouble).
vocab.example: こんなことで{先生|せんせい}のお{手|て}を{煩|わずら}わせるわけにはいかない。
vocab.exampleEn: I can't trouble the teacher over something like this.

meanings: to be dejected (lose heart after a letdown)
vocab.note: Group 3. ます form: {落胆|らくたん}します; て form: {落胆|らくたん}して. Also the noun {落胆|らくたん}. Compare carried {失望|しつぼう} (disappointment in someone or something).
vocab.example: {不合格|ふごうかく}の{知|し}らせに{落胆|らくたん}したが、すぐに{気持|きも}ちを{切|き}り{替|か}えた。
vocab.exampleEn: I was crushed by the news that I'd failed, but I soon pulled myself together.

vocab.note: な-adjective.
vocab.example: {新社長|しんしゃちょう}は{大胆|だいたん}な{改革|かいかく}に{踏|ふ}み{切|き}った。
vocab.exampleEn: The new president went ahead with bold reforms.

vocab.note: Critical: {何|なに}か{魂胆|こんたん}がある (to be up to something).
vocab.example: {急|きゅう}に{優|やさ}しくなるなんて、{何|なに}か{魂胆|こんたん}があるに{違|ちが}いない。
vocab.exampleEn: Suddenly being so nice — there must be something behind it.

vocab.note: Read けんお (嫌 as ケン, 悪 as オ). {自己嫌悪|じこけんお} (self-loathing), {嫌悪感|けんおかん}.
vocab.example: {失敗|しっぱい}を{人|ひと}のせいにした{自分|じぶん}に、{自己嫌悪|じこけんお}を{覚|おぼ}えた。
vocab.exampleEn: I was disgusted with myself for blaming my mistake on someone else.

meanings: to have a dislike of (verb, also of things that avoid a condition)
vocab.note: Group 1. ます form: {嫌|きら}います; て form: {嫌|きら}って. The verb beside carried {嫌|きら}い. Passive {嫌|きら}われる (to be disliked) is very common. Also of things: この{植物|しょくぶつ}は{湿気|しっけ}を{嫌|きら}う.
vocab.example: {彼|かれ}は{変化|へんか}を{嫌|きら}う{性格|せいかく}だ。
vocab.exampleEn: He's the kind of person who dislikes change.

vocab.example: {近所|きんじょ}の{人|ひと}から{嫌|いや}がらせを{受|う}けている。
vocab.exampleEn: I'm being harassed by a neighbour.

vocab.note: Also written {嫌|いや}み. {嫌味|いやみ}を{言|い}う; as a な-adjective: {嫌味|いやみ}な{人|ひと}.
vocab.example: {遅刻|ちこく}したら、{部長|ぶちょう}に「ずいぶん{早|はや}いね」と{嫌味|いやみ}を{言|い}われた。
vocab.exampleEn: When I was late, the department head said sarcastically, "You're early."

meanings: to have a strong aversion to (without good reason)
vocab.note: Group 3. ます form: {毛嫌|けぎら}いします; て form: {毛嫌|けぎら}いして.
vocab.example: {食|た}べたこともないのに、{納豆|なっとう}を{毛嫌|けぎら}いしている。
vocab.exampleEn: He can't stand fermented soybeans even though he's never tried them.

meanings: bosom (the inside front of one's clothes)
vocab.note: {懐|ふところ}が{寒|さむ}い / {懐|ふところ}が{温|あたた}かい (to be short of / flush with money); {敵|てき}の{懐|ふところ}に{飛|と}び{込|こ}む.
vocab.example: {給料日前|きゅうりょうびまえ}で、{懐|ふところ}が{寂|さび}しい。
vocab.exampleEn: It's just before payday and I'm short of money.

meanings: to look back fondly (on, the verb)
vocab.note: Group 1. ます form: {懐|なつ}かしみます; て form: {懐|なつ}かしんで. The verb beside carried {懐|なつ}かしい.
vocab.example: {祖母|そぼ}は{古|ふる}い{写真|しゃしん}を{見|み}ながら、{若|わか}い{頃|ころ}を{懐|なつ}かしんでいた。
vocab.exampleEn: Looking at old photographs, my grandmother reminisced about her youth.

meanings: to become attached (of a child or animal, to a person)
vocab.note: Group 1. ます form: {懐|なつ}きます; て form: {懐|なつ}いて. With に: {犬|いぬ}が{私|わたし}に{懐|なつ}く. Causative {懐|なつ}かせる is possible.
vocab.example: {保護|ほご}した{猫|ねこ}が、ようやく{私|わたし}に{懐|なつ}いてくれた。
vocab.exampleEn: The cat we took in has finally taken to me.

meanings: to reminisce (speak of one's past feelings, formal)
vocab.note: Group 3. ます form: {述懐|じゅっかい}します; て form: {述懐|じゅっかい}して. News and interviews: 〜と{述懐|じゅっかい}する.
vocab.example: 「あの{頃|ころ}が{一番|いちばん}{苦|くる}しかった」と、{監督|かんとく}は{述懐|じゅっかい}した。
vocab.exampleEn: "Those were the hardest days," the coach recalled.

meanings: sense of pride (in what one is or has done)
vocab.note: Sounds like carried ほこり (dust), which stays in kana.
vocab.example: {彼|かれ}は{伝統|でんとう}を{守|まも}る{仕事|しごと}に{誇|ほこ}りを{持|も}っている。
vocab.exampleEn: He takes pride in work that preserves tradition.

meanings: to boast of (take pride in, be proud to have)
vocab.note: Group 1. ます form: {誇|ほこ}ります; て form: {誇|ほこ}って. Often of a record: {世界一|せかいいち}を{誇|ほこ}る (to boast the world's best).
vocab.example: この{寺|てら}は、{千年|せんねん}を{超|こ}える{歴史|れきし}を{誇|ほこ}る。
vocab.exampleEn: This temple boasts a history of more than a thousand years.

meanings: filled with pride (of oneself or one's own)
vocab.example: {娘|むすめ}が{賞|しょう}をもらい、{誇|ほこ}らしい{気持|きも}ちになった。
vocab.exampleEn: My daughter won a prize, and I felt proud.

vocab.note: Group 3. ます form: {誇張|こちょう}します; て form: {誇張|こちょう}して. Formal; in speech {大|おお}げさに{言|い}う. Also the noun {誇張|こちょう}.
vocab.example: その{記事|きじ}は、{事実|じじつ}を{誇張|こちょう}して{伝|つた}えている。
vocab.exampleEn: The article exaggerates the facts.

meanings: homesick nostalgia (longing for home or the past, written)
vocab.note: Written. The katakana ノスタルジー is close.
vocab.example: {古|ふる}い{駅舎|えきしゃ}は、{見|み}る{人|ひと}に{郷愁|きょうしゅう}を{呼|よ}び{起|お}こす。
vocab.exampleEn: The old station building stirs nostalgia in those who see it.

meanings: the loneliness of travel (melancholy far from home)
vocab.example: {知|し}らない{町|まち}で{夕日|ゆうひ}を{見|み}ていると、{旅愁|りょしゅう}を{感|かん}じた。
vocab.exampleEn: Watching the sunset in an unfamiliar town, I felt the loneliness of travelling.

meanings: to be concerned that (formal, a bad outcome may occur)
vocab.note: Group 3. ます form: {懸念|けねん}します; て form: {懸念|けねん}して. Read けねん (懸 as ケ). Also the noun: {懸念|けねん}が{残|のこ}る, {懸念材料|けねんざいりょう}.
vocab.example: {専門家|せんもんか}は、{物価|ぶっか}がさらに{上|あ}がることを{懸念|けねん}している。
vocab.exampleEn: Experts fear that prices will rise further.

vocab.note: な-adjective. Mostly {懸命|けんめい}に and {懸命|けんめい}な{努力|どりょく}. Carried いっしょうけんめい is now {一生懸命|いっしょうけんめい}. Sounds like {件名|けんめい} (an email's subject) and {賢明|けんめい} (wise).
vocab.example: {救助隊|きゅうじょたい}は{夜通|よどお}し{懸命|けんめい}の{捜索|そうさく}を{続|つづ}けた。
vocab.exampleEn: The rescue team kept up a strenuous search all night.

meanings: prize competition (a contest or reward with prizes)
vocab.note: {懸賞|けんしょう}に{応募|おうぼ}する (to enter a prize draw). Sounds like {検証|けんしょう} (verification).
vocab.example: {雑誌|ざっし}の{懸賞|けんしょう}で{旅行券|りょこうけん}が{当|あ}たった。
vocab.exampleEn: I won travel vouchers in a magazine competition.

vocab.example: {長年|ながねん}の{懸案|けんあん}だった{駅前|えきまえ}の{再開発|さいかいはつ}が、ようやく{動|うご}き{出|だ}した。
vocab.exampleEn: The redevelopment around the station, an issue pending for years, has finally got moving.

meanings: at the risk of one's life (desperate, life-or-death)
vocab.note: Also a な-adjective: {命懸|いのちが}けの{仕事|しごと}, {命懸|いのちが}けで{守|まも}る.
vocab.example: {消防士|しょうぼうし}たちは{命懸|いのちが}けで{住民|じゅうみん}を{救|すく}い{出|だ}した。
vocab.exampleEn: The firefighters rescued the residents at the risk of their own lives.

vocab.note: な-adjective. Official statements: {誠|まこと}に{遺憾|いかん}である, {遺憾|いかん}の{意|い}を{表|ひょう}する. Not an apology: it says the speaker is displeased. {遺憾|いかん}なく (fully, to the full) is different: {実力|じつりょく}を{遺憾|いかん}なく{発揮|はっき}する. Different from 15's いかん (how, depending on), written in kana.
vocab.example: {今回|こんかい}の{事態|じたい}は{誠|まこと}に{遺憾|いかん}であると、{大臣|だいじん}は{述|の}べた。
vocab.exampleEn: The minister said the situation was most regrettable.

meanings: to extend a welcome (receive gladly, guests or ideas)
vocab.note: Group 3. ます form: {歓迎|かんげい}します; て form: {歓迎|かんげい}して. Also the noun: {歓迎会|かんげいかい} (a welcome party), {大歓迎|だいかんげい}.
vocab.example: {町|まち}の{人々|ひとびと}は、{海外|かいがい}からの{選手|せんしゅ}を{温|あたた}かく{歓迎|かんげい}した。
vocab.exampleEn: The townspeople gave the athletes from abroad a warm welcome.

meanings: cheer (a shout of joy from a crowd)
vocab.note: Sounds like carried {完成|かんせい} (completion) and lesson 25's {閑静|かんせい} (quiet).
vocab.example: ゴールが{決|き}まると、{客席|きゃくせき}から{大|おお}きな{歓声|かんせい}が{上|あ}がった。
vocab.exampleEn: When the goal went in, a great cheer went up from the stands.

vocab.note: Sounds like carried {換気|かんき} (ventilation) and {乾季|かんき} (dry season).
vocab.example: {優勝|ゆうしょう}が{決|き}まった{瞬間|しゅんかん}、{町|まち}は{歓喜|かんき}に{包|つつ}まれた。
vocab.exampleEn: The moment the championship was decided, the town was swept up in jubilation.

meanings: to chat pleasantly (formal, at a party or meeting)
vocab.note: Group 3. ます form: {歓談|かんだん}します; て form: {歓談|かんだん}して. Formal events: しばらくご{歓談|かんだん}ください (please enjoy your conversation for a while).
vocab.example: {式|しき}のあと、{参加者|さんかしゃ}はお{茶|ちゃ}を{飲|の}みながら{歓談|かんだん}した。
vocab.exampleEn: After the ceremony, the participants chatted over tea.

meanings: to cherish (love tenderly and care for, written)
vocab.note: Group 1. ます form: {慈|いつく}しみます; て form: {慈|いつく}しんで. Written and literary.
vocab.example: {祖母|そぼ}は{庭|にわ}の{花|はな}を、{子|こ}どものように{慈|いつく}しんでいた。
vocab.exampleEn: My grandmother cherished the flowers in her garden as if they were her children.

meanings: charity (benevolence, giving to those in need)
vocab.note: {慈善事業|じぜんじぎょう} (charitable work), {慈善団体|じぜんだんたい} (a charity). Sounds like carried {事前|じぜん} (beforehand).
vocab.example: {収益|しゅうえき}はすべて{慈善団体|じぜんだんたい}に{寄付|きふ}される。
vocab.exampleEn: All the proceeds will be donated to a charity.

vocab.example: {母|はは}は{慈愛|じあい}に{満|み}ちたまなざしで{子|こ}どもを{見|み}つめた。
vocab.exampleEn: The mother gazed at her child with eyes full of tender affection.

vocab.note: {幻|まぼろし}の{名酒|めいしゅ}: a legendary sake hardly anyone can get.
vocab.example: {砂漠|さばく}の{向|む}こうに{見|み}えた{町|まち}は、{幻|まぼろし}だった。
vocab.exampleEn: The town seen across the desert was a mirage.

meanings: to be disillusioned (see the ideal shatter)
vocab.note: Group 3. ます form: {幻滅|げんめつ}します; て form: {幻滅|げんめつ}して. With に: {政治|せいじ}に{幻滅|げんめつ}する. Also the noun {幻滅|げんめつ}.
vocab.example: {憧|あこが}れていた{業界|ぎょうかい}の{実態|じったい}を{知|し}って、{幻滅|げんめつ}した。
vocab.exampleEn: When I learned what the industry I'd admired was really like, I was disillusioned.

meanings: fantasy (an illusion one holds, an unrealistic belief)
vocab.note: {幻想|げんそう}を{抱|いだ}く (to harbour illusions), {幻想的|げんそうてき} (dreamlike, fantastical).
vocab.example: {都会|とかい}に{出|で}れば{何|なに}もかもうまくいくというのは{幻想|げんそう}だ。
vocab.exampleEn: The idea that everything will go well once you move to the city is a fantasy.

vocab.note: な-adjective.
vocab.example: {霧|きり}に{包|つつ}まれた{湖|みずうみ}は{幻想的|げんそうてき}だった。
vocab.exampleEn: The lake shrouded in mist was dreamlike.

vocab.note: Sounds like {厳格|げんかく} (strict).
vocab.example: {高熱|こうねつ}で、{一時|いちじ}{幻覚|げんかく}を{見|み}た。
vocab.exampleEn: I had a high fever and hallucinated for a while.

meanings: to be apprehensive (formal, about the future)
vocab.note: Group 3. ます form: {危惧|きぐ}します; て form: {危惧|きぐ}して. Written and formal: 〜を{危惧|きぐ}する, 〜と{危惧|きぐ}される. {絶滅危惧種|ぜつめつきぐしゅ}: an endangered species. Also the noun {危惧|きぐ}.
vocab.example: {地元|じもと}の{人々|ひとびと}は、{伝統|でんとう}の{祭|まつ}りが{途絶|とだ}えることを{危惧|きぐ}している。
vocab.exampleEn: Local people fear that the traditional festival will die out.

vocab.note: {畏敬|いけい}の{念|ねん}を{抱|いだ}く: to feel awe. 畏 also writes おそ(れる) (to stand in awe), a spelling of N3's {恐|おそ}れる.
vocab.example: {人々|ひとびと}は{古|ふる}くから、{山|やま}に{畏敬|いけい}の{念|ねん}を{抱|いだ}いてきた。
vocab.exampleEn: Since ancient times, people have regarded the mountains with awe.

vocab.note: Literary: {自然|しぜん}への{畏怖|いふ}.
vocab.example: {巨大|きょだい}な{滝|たき}を{前|まえ}に、{彼|かれ}は{畏怖|いふ}の{念|ねん}に{打|う}たれた。
vocab.exampleEn: Before the enormous waterfall, he was struck with awe.

meanings: to captivate (enchant, hold the attention of)
vocab.note: Group 3. ます form: {魅了|みりょう}します; て form: {魅了|みりょう}して. Very often passive: {魅了|みりょう}される (to be captivated).
vocab.example: {彼女|かのじょ}の{歌声|うたごえ}は{世界中|せかいじゅう}の{人々|ひとびと}を{魅了|みりょう}してやまない。
vocab.exampleEn: Her singing never ceases to captivate people all over the world.

vocab.example: この{町|まち}の{魅力|みりょく}は、{古|ふる}い{街並|まちな}みにある。
vocab.exampleEn: The appeal of this town lies in its old streets.

meanings: attractive (appealing, of an offer or a person)
vocab.note: な-adjective.
vocab.example: {条件|じょうけん}は{魅力的|みりょくてき}だが、{引|ひ}っ{越|こ}しが{必要|ひつよう}になる。
vocab.exampleEn: The terms are attractive, but it would mean moving.

vocab.note: {魅惑的|みわくてき} (bewitching).
vocab.example: {夜|よる}の{港町|みなとまち}には、{独特|どくとく}の{魅惑|みわく}がある。
vocab.exampleEn: A port town at night has an enchantment all its own.

meanings: to give up on (abandon a hope or attempt)
vocab.note: Group 2. ます form: {諦|あきら}めます; て form: {諦|あきら}めて. {諦|あきら}めがつく (to be able to accept it), {諦|あきら}めきれない (can't give up).
vocab.example: {雨|あめ}で{登山|とざん}は{諦|あきら}めざるを{得|え}なかった。
vocab.exampleEn: Because of the rain, we had no choice but to give up the climb.

meanings: giving up hope (acceptance that it can't be helped)
vocab.note: {諦|あきら}めが{悪|わる}い: unable to let go.
vocab.example: {何度|なんど}{断|ことわ}られても、{彼|かれ}は{諦|あきら}めが{悪|わる}かった。
vocab.exampleEn: However many times he was turned down, he couldn't let it go.

meanings: resigned detachment (literary, acceptance of how things are)
vocab.note: Literary and philosophical; read ていかん.
vocab.example: {晩年|ばんねん}の{作品|さくひん}には、{静|しず}かな{諦観|ていかん}が{感|かん}じられる。
vocab.exampleEn: A quiet resignation can be felt in the late works.

vocab.note: Often printed 虚しい or 空しい, but neither reading is jōyō, so the course writes it in kana.
vocab.example: {誰|だれ}にも{読|よ}まれない{報告書|ほうこくしょ}を{書|か}くのはむなしい。
vocab.exampleEn: Writing reports nobody reads feels pointless.

vocab.note: Group 3. ます form: {動揺|どうよう}します; て form: {動揺|どうよう}して. 揺 is lesson 23's kanji. Also of markets: {市場|しじょう}が{動揺|どうよう}する.
vocab.example: {突然|とつぜん}の{知|し}らせに、{彼|かれ}は{明|あき}らかに{動揺|どうよう}していた。
vocab.exampleEn: He was visibly shaken by the sudden news.

meanings: to be thrown into confusion (by a shock)
vocab.note: Group 3. ます form: {動転|どうてん}します; て form: {動転|どうてん}して. Mostly {気|き}が{動転|どうてん}する. Sounds like carried {同点|どうてん} (a tie).
vocab.example: {事故|じこ}の{知|し}らせを{聞|き}いて、{気|き}が{動転|どうてん}してしまった。
vocab.exampleEn: When I heard about the accident, I was beside myself.

meanings: foreboding (an uneasy feeling that something is wrong)
vocab.note: Read むな (胸 as むな, as in {胸元|むなもと}).
vocab.example: {朝|あさ}から{妙|みょう}な{胸騒|むなさわ}ぎがしていた。
vocab.exampleEn: I'd had a strange sense of foreboding since the morning.

meanings: tears of frustration (shed after a loss)
vocab.example: {決勝|けっしょう}で{敗|やぶ}れ、{選手|せんしゅ}たちは{悔|くや}し{涙|なみだ}を{流|なが}した。
vocab.exampleEn: Beaten in the final, the players shed tears of frustration.

meanings: overcome with emotion (too moved for words)
vocab.note: な-adjective, used almost only as a predicate: {感無量|かんむりょう}だ / です (so it isn't drilled).
vocab.example: {十年|じゅうねん}かけた{橋|はし}が{完成|かんせい}し、{感無量|かんむりょう}です。
vocab.exampleEn: The bridge we spent ten years on is finished, and I'm overcome with emotion.

meanings: tears of gratitude (or of being moved)
vocab.note: {感涙|かんるい}にむせぶ: to be choked with tears of emotion.
vocab.example: {再会|さいかい}した{親子|おやこ}は{感涙|かんるい}にむせんだ。
vocab.exampleEn: Reunited, parent and child were choked with tears.

meanings: to be overcome with emotion (at the height of feeling)
vocab.note: Group 1. ます form: {感極|かんきわ}まります; て form: {感極|かんきわ}まって. Mostly {感極|かんきわ}まって (overcome with emotion): lesson 18 teaches 〜{極|きわ}まる.
vocab.example: {受賞|じゅしょう}のスピーチで、{彼女|かのじょ}は{感極|かんきわ}まって{言葉|ことば}に{詰|つ}まった。
vocab.exampleEn: In her acceptance speech, she was overcome with emotion and lost her words.

meanings: sentimental (wistful, easily moved to sad nostalgia)
vocab.note: な-adjective. {感傷|かんしょう} (sentimentality) sounds like carried {鑑賞|かんしょう} (appreciation); センチメンタル is close.
vocab.example: {雨|あめ}の{日|ひ}は、なぜか{感傷的|かんしょうてき}な{気分|きぶん}になる。
vocab.exampleEn: Rainy days somehow make me feel sentimental.

meanings: to be crestfallen (lose all one's spirit)
vocab.note: Group 3. ます form: {意気消沈|いきしょうちん}します; て form: {意気消沈|いきしょうちん}して. Four-character compound.
vocab.example: {初戦|しょせん}で{負|ま}けて、チームは{意気消沈|いきしょうちん}していた。
vocab.exampleEn: Having lost the first match, the team was downcast.

meanings: to lose one's nerve (feel intimidated and hold back)
vocab.note: Group 3. ます form: {気後|きおく}れします; て form: {気後|きおく}れして.
vocab.example: {有名|ゆうめい}な{人|ひと}ばかりの{会|かい}で、すっかり{気後|きおく}れしてしまった。
vocab.exampleEn: At a gathering full of famous people, I completely lost my nerve.

meanings: preoccupation (a care on one's mind, mostly negated)
vocab.note: Almost always negative: {屈託|くったく}のない{笑顔|えがお} (a carefree smile). 屈 is lesson 17's.
vocab.example: {子|こ}どもたちの{屈託|くったく}のない{笑顔|えがお}に{救|すく}われた。
vocab.exampleEn: The children's carefree smiles were a comfort to me.

meanings: sense of loss (emptiness after losing someone or something)
vocab.example: {長年|ながねん}{飼|か}っていた{犬|いぬ}が{死|し}んで、{大|おお}きな{喪失感|そうしつかん}に{襲|おそ}われた。
vocab.exampleEn: When the dog we'd had for years died, I was overwhelmed by a sense of loss.

meanings: heartrending (full of anguish, of a voice or expression)
vocab.note: な-adjective.
vocab.example: {現場|げんば}には、{家族|かぞく}の{悲痛|ひつう}な{叫|さけ}びが{響|ひび}いた。
vocab.exampleEn: The family's heartrending cries echoed at the scene.

meanings: to be wild with joy (go mad with delight)
vocab.note: Group 3. ます form: {狂喜|きょうき}します; て form: {狂喜|きょうき}して. 狂 is lesson 11's kanji. Sounds like 11's {凶器|きょうき} (a weapon).
vocab.example: {合格|ごうかく}の{知|し}らせに、{彼|かれ}は{狂喜|きょうき}した。
vocab.exampleEn: He was wild with joy at the news that he'd passed.

meanings: sense of emptiness (feeling that nothing has meaning)
vocab.example: {目標|もくひょう}を{達成|たっせい}したとたん、{虚無感|きょむかん}に{襲|おそ}われた。
vocab.exampleEn: The moment I reached my goal, a sense of emptiness came over me.

vocab.note: な-adjective. Also a noun: {無念|むねん}を{晴|は}らす (to avenge a wrong). {無念|むねん}{無想|むそう}: a calm, empty mind (different sense).
vocab.example: あと{一歩|いっぽ}で{記録|きろく}に{届|とど}かず、{無念|むねん}でなりません。
vocab.exampleEn: I fell just short of the record, and it is bitterly disappointing.

vocab.example: {両家|りょうけ}の{間|あいだ}には、{今|いま}も{遺恨|いこん}が{残|のこ}っている。
vocab.exampleEn: There is still lasting bad blood between the two families.

meanings: peace of mind (tranquillity, a sense of calm)
vocab.example: {森|もり}の{中|なか}を{歩|ある}くと、{心|こころ}に{安|やす}らぎを{感|かん}じる。
vocab.exampleEn: Walking in the forest brings me peace of mind.

vocab.note: Group 3. ます form: {高揚|こうよう}します; て form: {高揚|こうよう}して. Usually {気分|きぶん}が{高揚|こうよう}する, {高揚感|こうようかん}. 揚 is lesson 13's kanji. Sounds like carried {紅葉|こうよう} (autumn colours).
vocab.example: {大観衆|だいかんしゅう}の{前|まえ}に{立|た}つと、{気分|きぶん}が{高揚|こうよう}した。
vocab.exampleEn: Standing before the huge crowd, I felt elated.

vocab.note: 至 is lesson 26's kanji.
vocab.example: {仕事|しごと}のあとの{一杯|いっぱい}が、{私|わたし}にとって{至福|しふく}のひとときだ。
vocab.exampleEn: A drink after work is my moment of pure bliss.

vocab.note: 劣 is lesson 18's kanji. Opposite: {優越感|ゆうえつかん}.
vocab.example: {優秀|ゆうしゅう}な{兄|あに}に、ずっと{劣等感|れっとうかん}を{抱|いだ}いていた。
vocab.exampleEn: I always felt inferior to my brilliant older brother.

meanings: to be ashamed (of one's own conduct, formal)
vocab.note: Group 2. ます form: {恥|は}じます; て form: {恥|は}じて. {恥|は}じることはない (nothing to be ashamed of); 〜に{恥|は}じない (worthy of: {名|な}に{恥|は}じない).
vocab.example: {彼|かれ}は{自分|じぶん}の{軽率|けいそつ}な{発言|はつげん}を{恥|は}じた。
vocab.exampleEn: He was ashamed of his careless remark.

vocab.note: Also loosely of a bad memory: {子|こ}どもの{頃|ころ}の{事故|じこ}がトラウマになっている.
vocab.example: {犬|いぬ}にかまれたことがトラウマで、{今|いま}も{犬|いぬ}が{怖|こわ}い。
vocab.exampleEn: Being bitten as a child left me traumatized, and I'm still afraid of dogs.

vocab.note: In Japanese mostly a feeling of inferiority: {背|せ}が{低|ひく}いのがコンプレックスだ.
vocab.example: {彼女|かのじょ}は{字|じ}が{下手|へた}なのがコンプレックスだった。
vocab.exampleEn: She was self-conscious about her poor handwriting.

vocab.example: {昭和|しょうわ}の{町並|まちな}みに、{若者|わかもの}までがノスタルジーを{感|かん}じるという。
vocab.exampleEn: They say even young people feel nostalgic about streets from the Shōwa era.

vocab.example: {恋人|こいびと}の{元|もと}カノの{話|はなし}を{聞|き}いて、ちょっとジェラシーを{感|かん}じた。
vocab.exampleEn: Hearing my partner talk about an ex-girlfriend, I felt a little jealous.

vocab.note: パニックになる / パニックに{陥|おちい}る ({陥|おちい}る: lesson 18).
vocab.example: {突然|とつぜん}の{停電|ていでん}で、{会場|かいじょう}はパニックになった。
vocab.exampleEn: The sudden power cut threw the venue into a panic.

vocab.note: Often shortened to フラスト in speech. Compare carried {悔|くや}しい (vexed at losing).
vocab.example: {思|おも}うように{練習|れんしゅう}できず、フラストレーションがたまっている。
vocab.exampleEn: I can't practise the way I want to, and the frustration is building up.

vocab.note: Japanese uses it as a noun: メンタルが{強|つよ}い (mentally tough), メンタルヘルス.
vocab.example: {大事|だいじ}な{試合|しあい}では、{技術|ぎじゅつ}よりメンタルが{試|ため}される。
vocab.exampleEn: In an important match, it's mental strength more than technique that gets tested.

vocab.note: な-adjective.
vocab.example: {成功|せいこう}して{傲慢|ごうまん}になった{彼|かれ}から、{友人|ゆうじん}は{離|はな}れていった。
vocab.exampleEn: As success made him arrogant, his friends drifted away.

vocab.note: Also 〜する: {慢心|まんしん}する. A warning word in sports and business: {慢心|まんしん}は{禁物|きんもつ}.
vocab.example: {連勝|れんしょう}が{続|つづ}いても、{監督|かんとく}は{慢心|まんしん}を{戒|いまし}めた。
vocab.exampleEn: Even as the winning streak went on, the coach warned against complacency.

vocab.note: Also a な-adjective. Critical: {職務怠慢|しょくむたいまん} (neglect of duty).
vocab.example: {事故|じこ}の{原因|げんいん}は、{点検|てんけん}を{怠|おこた}った{会社|かいしゃ}の{怠慢|たいまん}にある。
vocab.exampleEn: The cause of the accident lies in the negligence of the company, which failed to carry out inspections.

vocab.note: な-adjective. Close to {傲慢|ごうまん}; {高慢|こうまん} is more about a superior air, {傲慢|ごうまん} about overbearing behaviour.
vocab.example: {彼女|かのじょ}の{高慢|こうまん}な{態度|たいど}に、{周|まわ}りは{反感|はんかん}を{持|も}った。
vocab.exampleEn: Her haughty manner put people's backs up.

meanings: bragging (showing off what one has or did)
vocab.note: Also 〜する: {子|こ}どもを{自慢|じまん}する. {自慢話|じまんばなし} (bragging), {自慢|じまん}の{料理|りょうり} (one's signature dish). 慢 is this lesson's kanji.
vocab.example: {祖父|そふ}の{自慢|じまん}は、{一度|いちど}も{病気|びょうき}で{休|やす}んだことがないことだ。
vocab.exampleEn: My grandfather's proudest boast is that he's never once taken a day off sick.

meanings: long-suffering (able to put up with a lot)
vocab.note: Carried がまんする now takes kanji: {我慢|がまん}する.
vocab.example: {我慢強|がまんづよ}い{人|ひと}ほど、{限界|げんかい}まで{助|たす}けを{求|もと}めない。
vocab.exampleEn: The more long-suffering someone is, the longer they go before asking for help.

vocab.note: な-adjective.
vocab.example: {彼|かれ}は{賞|しょう}をもらっても、{謙虚|けんきょ}な{姿勢|しせい}を{崩|くず}さなかった。
vocab.exampleEn: Even after winning the prize, he remained modest.

vocab.note: Mainly in {謙譲|けんじょう}の{美徳|びとく} (the virtue of modesty) and the carried {謙譲語|けんじょうご} (humble language), now in kanji.
vocab.example: {日本|にほん}では、{謙譲|けんじょう}の{美徳|びとく}が{重|おも}んじられてきたと{言|い}われる。
vocab.exampleEn: It is said that the virtue of modesty has long been valued in Japan.

vocab.note: Also 〜する. Its second kanji is off the list, so the course writes it in kana. {謙虚|けんきょ} describes a character; けんそん is the act of playing oneself down.
vocab.example: 「たいしたことはしていません」と{彼|かれ}はけんそんしたが、{実際|じっさい}は{一番|いちばん}の{功労者|こうろうしゃ}だった。
vocab.exampleEn: "I didn't do much," he said modestly, but in fact he had contributed more than anyone.

meanings: vanity (wanting to look better than one is)
vocab.note: {虚栄心|きょえいしん} (vanity) is the usual form.
vocab.example: {虚栄心|きょえいしん}から、{彼|かれ}は{収入|しゅうにゅう}に{見合|みあ}わない{車|くるま}を{買|か}った。
vocab.exampleEn: Out of vanity, he bought a car beyond his income.

meanings: bluff (a show of strength one doesn't have)
vocab.note: {虚勢|きょせい}を{張|は}る: to put on a bold front.
vocab.example: {本当|ほんとう}は{怖|こわ}かったが、{子|こ}どもの{前|まえ}で{虚勢|きょせい}を{張|は}った。
vocab.exampleEn: I was actually scared, but I put on a brave front in front of the children.

meanings: hollow (empty of content or meaning, written)
vocab.note: な-adjective.
vocab.example: {中身|なかみ}のない{空虚|くうきょ}な{言葉|ことば}では、{人|ひと}の{心|こころ}は{動|うご}かない。
vocab.exampleEn: Hollow words with nothing behind them won't move anyone.

vocab.note: な-adjective.
vocab.example: {幼|おさな}い{頃|ころ}{虚弱|きょじゃく}だった{彼女|かのじょ}が、{今|いま}ではマラソン{選手|せんしゅ}だ。
vocab.exampleEn: She was a sickly child, and now she's a marathon runner.

vocab.note: な-adjective.
vocab.example: {匿名|とくめい}で{人|ひと}を{攻撃|こうげき}するのは{卑劣|ひれつ}な{行為|こうい}だ。
vocab.exampleEn: Attacking people anonymously is a despicable thing to do.

vocab.note: Also of greed for food: {食|た}べ{物|もの}に{卑|いや}しい. {卑|いや}しむ / {卑|いや}しめる: to despise.
vocab.example: {人|ひと}の{不幸|ふこう}を{喜|よろこ}ぶような{卑|いや}しい{心|こころ}は{持|も}ちたくない。
vocab.exampleEn: I don't want to have the kind of base heart that rejoices at other people's misfortune.

vocab.note: な-adjective. The opposite failing to {傲慢|ごうまん}: lowering oneself too far.
vocab.example: {失敗|しっぱい}したからといって、そんなに{卑屈|ひくつ}になることはない。
vocab.exampleEn: Just because you failed doesn't mean you have to grovel like that.

vocab.note: な-adjective. The usual kanji spelling has an off-list second kanji, so the course writes it in kana. Children say ずるい; ひきょう is stronger.
vocab.example: {後|うし}ろから{攻撃|こうげき}するなんて、ひきょうだ。
vocab.exampleEn: Attacking from behind — that's a dirty trick.

vocab.note: Everyday and childish too: ずるい！ (that's not fair!).
vocab.example: {自分|じぶん}だけ{先|さき}に{帰|かえ}るなんて、ずるいよ。
vocab.exampleEn: Going home early on your own — that's not fair.

vocab.note: {屈辱的|くつじょくてき} (humiliating).
vocab.example: {大差|たいさ}で{負|ま}けた{選手|せんしゅ}たちの{屈辱|くつじょく}は、{想像|そうぞう}にかたくない。
vocab.exampleEn: It isn't hard to imagine the humiliation the players felt at losing by such a margin.

meanings: to give in (bow to pressure, written)
vocab.note: Group 3. ます form: {屈|くっ}します; て form: {屈|くっ}して. With に: {圧力|あつりょく}に{屈|くっ}する, {暴力|ぼうりょく}に{屈|くっ}しない. A one-kanji する verb.
vocab.example: {彼|かれ}らは{脅|おど}しに{屈|くっ}することなく、{証言|しょうげん}を{続|つづ}けた。
vocab.exampleEn: They kept testifying without giving in to threats.

meanings: to submit (give in completely, to force or argument)
vocab.note: Group 3. ます form: {屈服|くっぷく}します; て form: {屈服|くっぷく}して.
vocab.example: {長|なが}い{交渉|こうしょう}の{末|すえ}、{相手|あいて}はついに{屈服|くっぷく}した。
vocab.exampleEn: After long negotiations, the other side finally submitted.

vocab.note: {不屈|ふくつ}の{精神|せいしん} (an indomitable spirit).
vocab.example: {彼女|かのじょ}は{不屈|ふくつ}の{精神|せいしん}で{病気|びょうき}を{乗|の}り{越|こ}えた。
vocab.exampleEn: With an indomitable spirit, she overcame her illness.

vocab.note: な-adjective. Also a noun and 〜する: {退屈|たいくつ}する (to be bored), {退屈|たいくつ}しのぎ (a way to kill time).
vocab.example: {雨|あめ}の{日|ひ}は{外|そと}に{出|で}られず、{子|こ}どもたちは{退屈|たいくつ}していた。
vocab.exampleEn: The children couldn't go out on the rainy day and were bored.

vocab.note: Group 3. ます form: {侮辱|ぶじょく}します; て form: {侮辱|ぶじょく}して. Also the noun: {侮辱|ぶじょく}を{受|う}ける (to be insulted).
vocab.example: {人前|ひとまえ}で{侮辱|ぶじょく}され、{彼|かれ}は{黙|だま}って{席|せき}を{立|た}った。
vocab.exampleEn: Insulted in public, he silently got up and left.

meanings: to underestimate (look down on, take lightly)
vocab.note: Group 1. ます form: {侮|あなど}ります; て form: {侮|あなど}って. Often negated: {侮|あなど}れない (not to be underestimated), {相手|あいて}を{侮|あなど}る.
vocab.example: {小|ちい}さなチームだと{侮|あなど}っていたら、{一回戦|いっかいせん}で{負|ま}けてしまった。
vocab.exampleEn: We took them lightly as a small team, and lost in the first round.

vocab.note: Group 2. ます form: {辱|はずかし}めます; て form: {辱|はずかし}めて. Literary: {名|な}を{辱|はずかし}める (to disgrace one's name).
vocab.example: {先祖|せんぞ}の{名|な}を{辱|はずかし}めるようなことはするな、と{父|ちち}は{言|い}った。
vocab.exampleEn: Don't do anything that would disgrace our ancestors' name, my father said.

meanings: generous (lenient and broad-minded, toward a fault)
vocab.note: な-adjective.
vocab.example: {部長|ぶちょう}は{私|わたし}の{失敗|しっぱい}に{寛大|かんだい}だった。
vocab.exampleEn: The department head was generous about my mistake.

vocab.note: な-adjective. Also a noun: {異|こと}なる{意見|いけん}への{寛容|かんよう}. {寛大|かんだい} forgives a fault; {寛容|かんよう} accepts difference.
vocab.example: {多様|たよう}な{価値観|かちかん}に{寛容|かんよう}な{社会|しゃかい}をめざしたい。
vocab.exampleEn: I want us to aim for a society that is tolerant of diverse values.

vocab.note: な-adjective.
vocab.example: {彼|かれ}は{信頼|しんらい}するに{足|た}る{誠実|せいじつ}な{人物|じんぶつ}だ。
vocab.exampleEn: He is a sincere person, worthy of trust.

meanings: good faith (sincere intent, shown in action)
vocab.note: {誠意|せいい}を{見|み}せる, {誠意|せいい}ある{対応|たいおう} (a response in good faith).
vocab.example: {謝罪|しゃざい}の{言葉|ことば}だけでなく、{誠意|せいい}ある{行動|こうどう}を{求|もと}めたい。
vocab.exampleEn: We want not just words of apology but action in good faith.

vocab.note: Literary and in names. The adverb {誠|まこと}に is common in formal speech.
vocab.example: {誠|まこと}を{尽|つ}くせば、いつかは{相手|あいて}に{伝|つた}わる。
vocab.exampleEn: If you are sincere in all you do, it will reach the other person in time.

vocab.note: Formal apologies and thanks: {誠|まこと}に{申|もう}し{訳|わけ}ございません, {誠|まこと}にありがとうございます.
vocab.example: ご{迷惑|めいわく}をおかけし、{誠|まこと}に{申|もう}し{訳|わけ}ございません。
vocab.exampleEn: We sincerely apologize for the inconvenience.

meanings: loyalty (allegiance, to a ruler or cause)
vocab.note: {忠誠|ちゅうせい}を{誓|ちか}う (to swear allegiance). Sounds like carried {中世|ちゅうせい} (the Middle Ages).
vocab.example: {武士|ぶし}は{主君|しゅくん}に{忠誠|ちゅうせい}を{誓|ちか}った。
vocab.exampleEn: The samurai swore loyalty to their lord.

meanings: faithful (true to an original or a duty)
vocab.note: な-adjective. {原作|げんさく}に{忠実|ちゅうじつ}な{映画|えいが} (a film faithful to the book), {職務|しょくむ}に{忠実|ちゅうじつ}.
vocab.example: この{翻訳|ほんやく}は{原文|げんぶん}に{忠実|ちゅうじつ}だが、{読|よ}みにくい。
vocab.exampleEn: This translation is faithful to the original but hard to read.

meanings: to advise against (warn someone kindly, as a friend)
vocab.note: Group 3. ます form: {忠告|ちゅうこく}します; て form: {忠告|ちゅうこく}して. Also the noun {忠告|ちゅうこく}. Compare {助言|じょげん} (advice in general).
vocab.example: {友人|ゆうじん}に{忠告|ちゅうこく}されたのに、{聞|き}かなかったことを{悔|く}やんでいる。
vocab.exampleEn: I regret not listening when my friend warned me.

vocab.note: {忍耐力|にんたいりょく} (stamina, patience).
vocab.example: {研究|けんきゅう}には{才能|さいのう}だけでなく{忍耐|にんたい}が{必要|ひつよう}だ。
vocab.exampleEn: Research needs not just talent but perseverance.

vocab.example: {先生|せんせい}は{忍耐強|にんたいづよ}く、{私|わたし}が{理解|りかい}するまで{説明|せつめい}してくれた。
vocab.exampleEn: The teacher patiently explained until I understood.

vocab.note: Group 1. ます form: {忍|しの}びます; て form: {忍|しの}んで. Two senses: to endure ({恥|はじ}を{忍|しの}んで, swallowing one's pride) and to stay hidden ({人目|ひとめ}を{忍|しの}んで, avoiding notice). 〜に{忍|しの}びない (can't bring oneself to): lesson 16.
vocab.example: {恥|はじ}を{忍|しの}んでお{願|ねが}いします。もう{一度|いちど}チャンスをください。
vocab.exampleEn: I swallow my pride to ask you this: please give me one more chance.

vocab.example: {寝|ね}ている{子|こ}どもを{起|お}こさないよう、{忍|しの}び{足|あし}で{部屋|へや}を{出|で}た。
vocab.exampleEn: I tiptoed out of the room so as not to wake the sleeping child.

meanings: brutal (merciless, of a crime or act)
vocab.note: な-adjective.
vocab.example: {事件|じけん}の{残忍|ざんにん}な{手口|てぐち}に、{社会|しゃかい}は{衝撃|しょうげき}を{受|う}けた。
vocab.exampleEn: Society was shocked by the brutal way the crime was committed.

vocab.note: Group 2. ます form: {耐|た}えます; て form: {耐|た}えて. Also written {堪|た}える, the spelling in 〜に{堪|た}えない (lesson 16). {耐|た}え{難|がた}い: unbearable.
vocab.example: {彼|かれ}は{痛|いた}みに{耐|た}えながら、{最後|さいご}まで{走|はし}った。
vocab.exampleEn: He ran to the finish, enduring the pain.

vocab.note: {耐久性|たいきゅうせい} (durability), {耐久|たいきゅう}レース (an endurance race).
vocab.example: この{素材|そざい}は、{軽|かる}くて{耐久性|たいきゅうせい}にも{優|すぐ}れている。
vocab.exampleEn: This material is light and highly durable.

vocab.note: な-adjective. Sounds like carried {身長|しんちょう} (height): {慎重|しんちょう}に{判断|はんだん}する.
vocab.example: {大切|たいせつ}な{決断|けつだん}だから、{慎重|しんちょう}に{考|かんが}えたい。
vocab.exampleEn: It's an important decision, so I want to think it over carefully.

meanings: to be careful about (exercise restraint in words or conduct)
vocab.note: Group 1. ます form: {慎|つつし}みます; て form: {慎|つつし}んで. {言動|げんどう}を{慎|つつし}む (to watch what one says and does), {酒|さけ}を{慎|つつし}む. 謹 has the same reading in {謹|つつし}んで (respectfully).
vocab.example: {公|おおやけ}の{場|ば}では、{軽率|けいそつ}な{発言|はつげん}を{慎|つつし}むべきだ。
vocab.exampleEn: In public one should refrain from careless remarks.

vocab.example: {慎|つつし}みのない{質問|しつもん}に、{会場|かいじょう}は{静|しず}まり{返|かえ}った。
vocab.exampleEn: The hall fell silent at the indiscreet question.

meanings: frugal and modest (of a way of life)
vocab.note: Of a way of life: つつましい{暮|く}らし. Often printed 慎ましい, but that reading of 慎 isn't jōyō, so the course writes it in kana.
vocab.example: {二人|ふたり}は{郊外|こうがい}でつつましく{暮|く}らしている。
vocab.exampleEn: The two of them live modestly in the suburbs.

meanings: being confined to home (as a punishment)
vocab.note: Also 〜する. {自宅謹慎|じたくきんしん}: being told to stay at home as a disciplinary measure.
vocab.example: {問題|もんだい}を{起|お}こした{選手|せんしゅ}は、{一か月|いっかげつ}の{謹慎|きんしん}{処分|しょぶん}となった。
vocab.exampleEn: The player who caused the trouble was suspended for a month.

vocab.note: な-adjective. Of jokes at a bad time: {不謹慎|ふきんしん}な{発言|はつげん}.
vocab.example: {災害|さいがい}の{最中|さいちゅう}に{冗談|じょうだん}を{言|い}うのは{不謹慎|ふきんしん}だ。
vocab.exampleEn: Making jokes in the middle of a disaster is in poor taste.

vocab.note: Fixed phrases: {謹|つつし}んでお{悔|く}やみ{申|もう}し{上|あ}げます (my deepest condolences), {謹|つつし}んで{新年|しんねん}のお{喜|よろこ}びを{申|もう}し{上|あ}げます (New Year cards).
vocab.example: {謹|つつし}んでお{悔|く}やみ{申|もう}し{上|あ}げます。
vocab.exampleEn: Please accept my deepest condolences.

vocab.note: Sounds like {帰宅|きたく} (going home).
vocab.example: {祖父|そふ}が{危篤|きとく}だと{聞|き}き、{急|いそ}いで{病院|びょういん}に{向|む}かった。
vocab.exampleEn: Hearing my grandfather was in a critical condition, I hurried to the hospital.

meanings: philanthropist (a charitable person who gives generously)
vocab.example: {図書館|としょかん}は、{地元|じもと}の{篤志家|とくしか}の{寄付|きふ}で{建|た}てられた。
vocab.exampleEn: The library was built with donations from a local benefactor.

vocab.note: な-adjective. {真摯|しんし}に{受|う}け{止|と}める (to take something seriously, a common apology phrase). Sounds like lesson 7's {紳士|しんし} (gentleman).
vocab.example: {皆様|みなさま}からのご{意見|いけん}を、{真摯|しんし}に{受|う}け{止|と}めております。
vocab.exampleEn: We are taking your comments very seriously.

vocab.note: な-adjective.
vocab.example: {夏休|なつやす}みを{怠惰|たいだ}に{過|す}ごしてしまった。
vocab.exampleEn: I idled away the summer holidays.

meanings: to neglect (fail to do one's duty, formal)
vocab.note: Group 1. ます form: {怠|おこた}ります; て form: {怠|おこた}って. Carried なまける (to be lazy) now takes this kanji too: {怠|なま}ける. {怠|おこた}る is failing to do what one should: {注意|ちゅうい}を{怠|おこた}る.
vocab.example: {確認|かくにん}を{怠|おこた}ったために、{大|おお}きなミスにつながった。
vocab.exampleEn: Neglecting to check led to a big mistake.

meanings: force of habit (inertia, continuing without thought)
vocab.note: {惰性|だせい}で{続|つづ}ける: to keep doing something out of mere habit.
vocab.example: {楽|たの}しくもないのに、{惰性|だせい}でゲームを{続|つづ}けている。
vocab.exampleEn: It isn't even fun, but I keep playing the game out of habit.

vocab.note: な-adjective. {粗末|そまつ}にする: to waste or treat carelessly ({食|た}べ{物|もの}を{粗末|そまつ}にするな). The polite 「{粗末|そまつ}なものですが」 offers a gift modestly.
vocab.example: {食|た}べ{物|もの}を{粗末|そまつ}にしてはいけないと、{祖母|そぼ}によく{言|い}われた。
vocab.exampleEn: My grandmother often told me never to waste food.

vocab.note: な-adjective.
vocab.example: {彼|かれ}は{粗野|そや}に{見|み}えるが、{実|じつ}は{細|こま}かい{気配|きくば}りのできる{人|ひと}だ。
vocab.exampleEn: He looks uncouth, but he's actually very considerate.

vocab.note: な-adjective.
vocab.example: {粗暴|そぼう}な{振|ふ}る{舞|ま}いを{繰|く}り{返|かえ}し、{彼|かれ}は{退学|たいがく}になった。
vocab.exampleEn: After repeated violent behaviour, he was expelled.

vocab.note: Often written in kana: あらすじ. 粗 is read あら as in {粗|あら}い, a spelling of carried {荒|あら}い (rough, coarse).
vocab.example: {映画|えいが}を{見|み}る{前|まえ}に、{粗筋|あらすじ}だけ{読|よ}んでおいた。
vocab.exampleEn: Before seeing the film, I read just the synopsis.

vocab.note: Of a knife ({鈍|にぶ}い{刃|は}), of reactions ({反応|はんのう}が{鈍|にぶ}い), of a person slow to notice feelings ({鈍|にぶ}い{人|ひと}).
vocab.example: {寒|さむ}さで{指|ゆび}の{動|うご}きが{鈍|にぶ}くなった。
vocab.exampleEn: The cold made my fingers sluggish.

meanings: to grow dull (lose sharpness or skill)
vocab.note: Group 1. ます form: {鈍|にぶ}ります; て form: {鈍|にぶ}って. {腕|うで}が{鈍|にぶ}る (to get rusty), {決心|けっしん}が{鈍|にぶ}る (one's resolve wavers).
vocab.example: {一年|いちねん}もピアノを{弾|ひ}かなかったので、{腕|うで}が{鈍|にぶ}った。
vocab.exampleEn: I didn't play the piano for a whole year, so I've got rusty.

vocab.note: な-adjective.
vocab.example: {彼|かれ}は{鈍感|どんかん}で、{彼女|かのじょ}の{気持|きも}ちにまったく{気|き}づいていない。
vocab.exampleEn: He's so obtuse that he has no idea how she feels.

vocab.note: Of a blade ({鋭|するど}い{刃|は}), a look, pain, a question ({鋭|するど}い{質問|しつもん}).
vocab.example: {記者|きしゃ}の{鋭|するど}い{質問|しつもん}に、{大臣|だいじん}は{言葉|ことば}に{詰|つ}まった。
vocab.exampleEn: The minister was lost for words at the reporter's sharp question.

meanings: keen (acutely sensitive, of senses or mind, written)
vocab.note: な-adjective.
vocab.example: {犬|いぬ}の{嗅覚|きゅうかく}は{人間|にんげん}よりはるかに{鋭敏|えいびん}だ。
vocab.exampleEn: A dog's sense of smell is far keener than a human's.

vocab.note: {少数精鋭|しょうすうせいえい}: a small but elite team.
vocab.example: {各国|かっこく}から{集|あつ}まった{精鋭|せいえい}が、{技|わざ}を{競|きそ}い{合|あ}った。
vocab.exampleEn: An elite gathered from every country competed in skill.

vocab.note: {期待|きたい}の{新鋭|しんえい}: a promising newcomer.
vocab.example: {新鋭|しんえい}の{作家|さっか}が、{初|はじ}めての{長編|ちょうへん}で{賞|しょう}を{取|と}った。
vocab.exampleEn: A promising new writer won a prize with a first full-length novel.

vocab.note: な-adjective. {巧|たく}みな{話術|わじゅつ} (a skilful way with words). Sounds like lesson 21's {匠|たくみ} (a master craftsman).
vocab.example: {彼|かれ}は{巧|たく}みな{話術|わじゅつ}で{客|きゃく}の{心|こころ}をつかんだ。
vocab.exampleEn: With his skilful patter he won the customers over.

meanings: ingenious (cleverly contrived, often of a trick)
vocab.note: な-adjective. Often of fraud: {巧妙|こうみょう}な{手口|てぐち} (a cunning method).
vocab.example: {詐欺|さぎ}の{手口|てぐち}は、{年々|ねんねん}{巧妙|こうみょう}になっている。
vocab.exampleEn: The methods of fraud become more ingenious every year.

vocab.example: {技巧|ぎこう}に{走|はし}りすぎて、{作品|さくひん}の{魅力|みりょく}が{失|うしな}われている。
vocab.exampleEn: By relying too much on technique, the work loses its appeal.

meanings: elaborate (finely made, of a mechanism or model)
vocab.note: な-adjective. Sounds like {成功|せいこう} (success).
vocab.example: {江戸時代|えどじだい}のからくり{人形|にんぎょう}は、{驚|おどろ}くほど{精巧|せいこう}にできている。
vocab.exampleEn: Edo-period mechanical dolls are astonishingly finely made.

meanings: unskilled (humble, of one's own words or work)
vocab.note: Mostly humble, of one's own words or work: {拙|つたな}い{文章|ぶんしょう}ですが. The same kanji is read まずい in print, but that reading isn't jōyō: carried まずい stays in kana.
vocab.example: {拙|つたな}い{日本語|にほんご}ですが、{一生懸命|いっしょうけんめい}{書|か}きました。
vocab.exampleEn: My Japanese is poor, but I wrote this as best I could.

vocab.note: な-adjective.
vocab.example: {稚拙|ちせつ}なうそは、すぐに{見破|みやぶ}られた。
vocab.exampleEn: The crude lie was seen through at once.

vocab.note: な-adjective.
vocab.example: {彼女|かのじょ}は{流行|りゅうこう}に{敏感|びんかん}だ。
vocab.exampleEn: She's quick to pick up on trends.

vocab.note: な-adjective.
vocab.example: {店員|てんいん}の{機敏|きびん}な{対応|たいおう}で、{混乱|こんらん}はすぐに{収|おさ}まった。
vocab.exampleEn: Thanks to the staff's quick response, the confusion soon died down.

vocab.note: な-adjective. {神経過敏|しんけいかびん} (nervousness). Sounds like {花瓶|かびん} (a vase).
vocab.example: {周|まわ}りの{評価|ひょうか}に{過敏|かびん}になりすぎないほうがいい。
vocab.exampleEn: It's better not to be too sensitive to what others think of you.

meanings: highly capable (of a professional, before a noun)
vocab.note: Usually before a noun: {敏腕|びんわん}{記者|きしゃ}, {敏腕|びんわん}{弁護士|べんごし}.
vocab.example: {敏腕|びんわん}の{編集者|へんしゅうしゃ}が、{無名|むめい}の{作家|さっか}を{見|み}いだした。
vocab.exampleEn: A brilliant editor discovered the unknown writer.

meanings: deliberately (going out of one's way to, despite reasons not to)
vocab.note: Written {敢|あ}えて in some texts, but that reading isn't jōyō: kana in this course's prose. {敢|あ}えて{言|い}えば (if I may venture to say), あえて{言|い}わない (I choose not to say).
vocab.example: {反対|はんたい}されるのはわかっていたが、あえて{意見|いけん}を{述|の}べた。
vocab.exampleEn: I knew I'd meet opposition, but I deliberately spoke my mind.

vocab.note: な-adjective. Sounds like carried {夕刊|ゆうかん} (evening paper).
vocab.example: {少年|しょうねん}は{川|かわ}に{落|お}ちた{子|こ}どもを{勇敢|ゆうかん}にも{助|たす}け{出|だ}した。
vocab.exampleEn: The boy bravely rescued the child who had fallen into the river.

meanings: daring (boldly decisive, in attack or challenge)
vocab.note: な-adjective. Mostly {果敢|かかん}に: {果敢|かかん}に{挑|いど}む (to take on boldly).
vocab.example: {彼女|かのじょ}は{格上|かくうえ}の{相手|あいて}にも{果敢|かかん}に{挑|いど}んだ。
vocab.exampleEn: She boldly took on even higher-ranked opponents.

vocab.note: Mostly in {質実剛健|しつじつごうけん} (plain living and sturdy spirit, often a school motto).
vocab.example: {質実剛健|しつじつごうけん}を{校訓|こうくん}とする{学校|がっこう}は{少|すく}なくない。
vocab.exampleEn: Quite a few schools have plain living and sturdy spirit as their motto.

meanings: hearty (big-hearted and bold, on a grand scale)
vocab.note: な-adjective.
vocab.example: {親方|おやかた}は{豪快|ごうかい}に{笑|わら}って、{私|わたし}の{肩|かた}をたたいた。
vocab.exampleEn: The master laughed heartily and slapped me on the shoulder.

vocab.note: な-adjective.
vocab.example: {結婚式|けっこんしき}の{料理|りょうり}は{驚|おどろ}くほど{豪華|ごうか}だった。
vocab.exampleEn: The food at the wedding was astonishingly lavish.

vocab.note: News: {集中豪雨|しゅうちゅうごうう}, {記録的|きろくてき}な{豪雨|ごうう}.
vocab.example: {記録的|きろくてき}な{豪雨|ごうう}で、{川|かわ}が{氾濫|はんらん}した。
vocab.exampleEn: The record downpour made the river burst its banks.

meanings: virtue (moral excellence, character that wins respect)
vocab.note: {徳|とく}の{高|たか}い{僧|そう} (a monk of great virtue). Sounds like carried {得|とく} (gain).
vocab.example: {孔子|こうし}は、{政治|せいじ}は{法|ほう}より{徳|とく}によって{行|おこな}うべきだと{説|と}いた。
vocab.exampleEn: Confucius taught that government should be by virtue rather than by law.

vocab.note: {道徳|どうとく} is also the school subject of moral education.
vocab.example: {電車|でんしゃ}で{席|せき}を{譲|ゆず}るのは、{法律|ほうりつ}ではなく{道徳|どうとく}の{問題|もんだい}だ。
vocab.exampleEn: Giving up your seat on the train is a question of morals, not law.

vocab.note: {謙譲|けんじょう}の{美徳|びとく} (the virtue of modesty).
vocab.example: {我慢|がまん}することが{美徳|びとく}とされた{時代|じだい}もあった。
vocab.exampleEn: There was a time when putting up with things was considered a virtue.

meanings: personal virtue (goodness that draws people to someone)
vocab.example: {彼|かれ}の{周|まわ}りに{人|ひと}が{集|あつ}まるのは、{人徳|じんとく}のなせる{業|わざ}だ。
vocab.exampleEn: People gather around him thanks to his innate goodness.

vocab.note: Before a noun: {悪徳|あくとく}{業者|ぎょうしゃ} (a crooked business), {悪徳|あくとく}{商法|しょうほう} (fraudulent sales methods).
vocab.example: {高齢者|こうれいしゃ}をねらう{悪徳|あくとく}{業者|ぎょうしゃ}に{注意|ちゅうい}してください。
vocab.exampleEn: Beware of crooked businesses that target the elderly.

vocab.example: {孔子|こうし}の{教|おし}えでは、{仁|じん}が{最|もっと}も{重要|じゅうよう}な{徳|とく}とされる。
vocab.exampleEn: In Confucianism, benevolence is regarded as the most important virtue.

meanings: duty and honour (a code of loyalty and humanity)
vocab.note: Also of the loyalty code of certain groups; {仁義|じんぎ}に{反|はん}する (to break the code).
vocab.example: {世話|せわ}になった{人|ひと}を{裏切|うらぎ}るのは、{仁義|じんぎ}に{反|はん}する。
vocab.exampleEn: Betraying someone who has helped you goes against all sense of honour.

vocab.note: な-adjective.
vocab.example: {彼女|かのじょ}の{朗|ほが}らかな{笑|わら}い{声|ごえ}が、{教室|きょうしつ}を{明|あか}るくした。
vocab.exampleEn: Her cheerful laughter brightened up the classroom.

vocab.note: Written and news: {待望|たいぼう}の{朗報|ろうほう}.
vocab.example: {長|なが}く{待|ま}っていた{合格|ごうかく}の{朗報|ろうほう}が{届|とど}いた。
vocab.exampleEn: The long-awaited good news that I'd passed arrived.

vocab.note: な-adjective. {明朗会計|めいろうかいけい}: clear, honest pricing (no hidden charges).
vocab.example: {明朗|めいろう}な{人柄|ひとがら}で、{誰|だれ}からも{好|す}かれている。
vocab.exampleEn: With an open, cheerful personality, everyone likes them.

meanings: gentle (calm and peaceful, of a person, the weather or the sea)
vocab.note: な-adjective.
vocab.example: {祖父|そふ}は{穏|おだ}やかな{人|ひと}で、{怒|おこ}ったところを{見|み}たことがない。
vocab.exampleEn: My grandfather is a gentle person; I've never seen him angry.

vocab.note: な-adjective. {穏便|おんびん}に{済|す}ませる: to settle a matter quietly.
vocab.example: {近所|きんじょ}とのトラブルは、できるだけ{穏便|おんびん}に{解決|かいけつ}したい。
vocab.exampleEn: I'd like to settle the trouble with the neighbours as quietly as possible.

meanings: tranquil (peaceful and uneventful, of days or a life)
vocab.note: な-adjective. {平穏|へいおん}な{日々|ひび}, {平穏無事|へいおんぶじ}.
vocab.example: {事件|じけん}の{後|あと}、{村|むら}にはまた{平穏|へいおん}な{日々|ひび}が{戻|もど}った。
vocab.exampleEn: After the incident, tranquil days returned to the village.

meanings: moderate (not extreme, of views or a party)
vocab.note: な-adjective. {穏健派|おんけんは} (the moderates).
vocab.example: {彼|かれ}は{党内|とうない}でも{穏健|おんけん}な{立場|たちば}で{知|し}られている。
vocab.exampleEn: He's known for moderate views even within the party.

vocab.note: な-adjective. {不穏|ふおん}な{空気|くうき} (a tense atmosphere), {不穏|ふおん}な{動|うご}き.
vocab.example: {会議|かいぎ}が{始|はじ}まる{前|まえ}から、{不穏|ふおん}な{空気|くうき}が{漂|ただよ}っていた。
vocab.exampleEn: A tense atmosphere hung in the air even before the meeting began.

vocab.note: な-adjective. 淡 is lesson 25's kanji.
vocab.example: {困|こま}っている{人|ひと}に{冷淡|れいたん}な{態度|たいど}を{取|と}るべきではない。
vocab.exampleEn: One shouldn't be cold toward people in trouble.

vocab.note: な-adjective. Often written in kana: おおらか.
vocab.example: {大|おお}らかな{性格|せいかく}で、{細|こま}かいことは{気|き}にしない。
vocab.exampleEn: With an easygoing nature, they don't worry about little things.

vocab.note: な-adjective.
vocab.example: {彼|かれ}は{律儀|りちぎ}な{人|ひと}で、{借|か}りたものは{必|かなら}ず{期日|きじつ}までに{返|かえ}す。
vocab.exampleEn: He's very conscientious; he always returns things he borrows by the due date.

vocab.note: Often printed 図々しい, but that reading isn't jōyō: kana in this course.
vocab.example: {頼|たの}まれてもいないのに{上|あ}がり{込|こ}むなんて、ずうずうしい。
vocab.exampleEn: Barging in without being asked — what a nerve.

vocab.note: The humble 「{厚|あつ}かましいお{願|ねが}いですが」 (I know it's a lot to ask, but…) is common in requests.
vocab.example: {厚|あつ}かましいお{願|ねが}いですが、{推薦状|すいせんじょう}を{書|か}いていただけないでしょうか。
vocab.exampleEn: I know it's a lot to ask, but could you write me a letter of recommendation?

vocab.example: {何|なに}を{言|い}われても{平気|へいき}な{図太|ずぶと}さが、{今|いま}の{私|わたし}には{必要|ひつよう}だ。
vocab.exampleEn: What I need now is to be thick-skinned enough not to care what people say.

vocab.note: な-adjective.
vocab.example: {社長|しゃちょう}は{気|き}さくな{人|ひと}で、{新人|しんじん}にも{気軽|きがる}に{声|こえ}をかける。
vocab.exampleEn: The president is approachable and chats easily even with new staff.

vocab.note: な-adjective.
vocab.example: {父|ちち}は{実直|じっちょく}な{会社員|かいしゃいん}として、{四十年|よんじゅうねん}{働|はたら}いた。
vocab.exampleEn: My father worked forty years as an honest, steady company employee.

meanings: plucky (brave and admirable, of a child or the weak)
vocab.note: な-adjective. Praise for effort beyond what one would expect: けなげな{子|こ}ども. Often printed 健気, an ateji spelling whose reading isn't jōyō: kana in this course.
vocab.example: {病気|びょうき}の{母|はは}を{支|ささ}える{少女|しょうじょ}のけなげな{姿|すがた}に{心|こころ}を{打|う}たれた。
vocab.exampleEn: I was moved by the plucky girl caring for her sick mother.

meanings: high-handed (rude and arrogant, toward people one sees as below)
vocab.note: な-adjective. 柄 is lesson 25's kanji, read へい here.
vocab.example: {店員|てんいん}に{横柄|おうへい}な{態度|たいど}を{取|と}る{客|きゃく}は、{嫌|きら}われる。
vocab.exampleEn: Customers who are high-handed with shop staff are disliked.

vocab.note: な-adjective.
vocab.example: {目先|めさき}の{利益|りえき}だけで{決|き}めたのは、{浅|あさ}はかだった。
vocab.exampleEn: Deciding only on short-term profit was short-sighted.

vocab.note: な-adjective.
vocab.example: {軽率|けいそつ}な{発言|はつげん}で、{大臣|だいじん}は{辞任|じにん}に{追|お}い{込|こ}まれた。
vocab.exampleEn: A careless remark forced the minister to resign.

vocab.note: Also 〜する: もう{少|すこ}し{辛抱|しんぼう}して. {辛抱強|しんぼうづよ}い: patient.
vocab.example: {辛抱|しんぼう}したかいがあって、{店|みせ}はようやく{軌道|きどう}に{乗|の}った。
vocab.exampleEn: Our patience paid off: the shop is finally on track.

meanings: staying power (patience for long, steady work)
vocab.note: {根気|こんき}がいる (it takes patience), {根気強|こんきづよ}い.
vocab.example: {古|ふる}い{文書|ぶんしょ}の{整理|せいり}には、{根気|こんき}がいる。
vocab.exampleEn: Sorting old documents takes a lot of patience.

vocab.note: Two senses: grit ({根性|こんじょう}がある) and, with a modifier, a nasty nature ({意地悪|いじわる}な{根性|こんじょう}).
vocab.example: {最後|さいご}まで{走|はし}り{抜|ぬ}いたのは、{根性|こんじょう}だけだった。
vocab.exampleEn: It was sheer grit that got me to the finish.

vocab.note: {横綱|よこづな}の{品格|ひんかく} (the dignity expected of a grand champion).
vocab.example: {勝|か}っても{負|ま}けても、{品格|ひんかく}のある{振|ふ}る{舞|ま}いを{心|こころ}がけたい。
vocab.exampleEn: Win or lose, I want to behave with dignity.

meanings: refinement (good taste in manners or appearance)
vocab.note: {品|ひん}がある / {品|ひん}がない (refined / vulgar). Carried {上品|じょうひん} and {下品|げひん} share it.
vocab.example: {彼女|かのじょ}の{話|はな}し{方|かた}には{品|ひん}がある。
vocab.exampleEn: There's an elegance to the way she speaks.

meanings: moral character (a person as a whole)
vocab.note: {人格者|じんかくしゃ}: a person of fine character.
vocab.example: {相手|あいて}の{意見|いけん}を{批判|ひはん}しても、{人格|じんかく}を{否定|ひてい}してはいけない。
vocab.exampleEn: You can criticize someone's opinion, but you mustn't attack them as a person.

meanings: character (the kind of person someone is, warmly seen)
vocab.note: 柄 is lesson 25's kanji. Usually positive: {人柄|ひとがら}がいい, {温|あたた}かい{人柄|ひとがら}.
vocab.example: {彼|かれ}の{温|あたた}かい{人柄|ひとがら}は、{誰|だれ}からも{愛|あい}された。
vocab.exampleEn: Everyone loved his warm nature.

vocab.note: な-adjective. {気長|きなが}に{待|ま}つ: to wait patiently. Opposite: carried {短気|たんき}.
vocab.example: {急|いそ}がなくていいから、{気長|きなが}に{待|ま}ってるよ。
vocab.exampleEn: No need to hurry; I'll wait as long as it takes.

vocab.note: な-adjective. The opposite of carried {器用|きよう}; also of social awkwardness: {生|い}き{方|かた}が{不器用|ぶきよう}.
vocab.example: {私|わたし}は{不器用|ぶきよう}で、ボタン{一|ひと}つつけるのにも{時間|じかん}がかかる。
vocab.exampleEn: I'm so clumsy it takes me ages just to sew on a button.

vocab.note: な-adjective. 臆 is lesson 26's kanji. {臆病者|おくびょうもの}: a coward.
vocab.example: うちの{犬|いぬ}は{臆病|おくびょう}で、{雷|かみなり}が{鳴|な}ると{隠|かく}れてしまう。
vocab.exampleEn: Our dog is timid and hides whenever it thunders.

meanings: to throw one's weight around (act self-important)
vocab.note: Group 1. ます form: {威張|いば}ります; て form: {威張|いば}って. 威 is lesson 14's kanji. A group 1 verb: {威張|いば}らない, {威張|いば}って.
vocab.example: {肩書|かたが}きがあるからといって、{威張|いば}る{人|ひと}は{尊敬|そんけい}されない。
vocab.exampleEn: People who throw their weight around just because of their title don't earn respect.

vocab.note: な-adjective. Its first kanji is off the list (the usual spelling is {几帳面|きちょうめん}), so the course writes it in kana.
vocab.example: {彼女|かのじょ}はきちょうめんで、{毎日|まいにち}の{支出|ししゅつ}を{一円|いちえん}{単位|たんい}で{記録|きろく}している。
vocab.exampleEn: She's meticulous and records every day's spending down to the last yen.

vocab.note: プライドが{高|たか}い (proud, easily hurt), プライドが{傷|きず}つく (one's pride is hurt).
vocab.example: プライドが{高|たか}くて、{人|ひと}に{助|たす}けを{求|もと}められない。
vocab.exampleEn: Too proud to ask anyone for help.

meanings: lax (sloppy about time, money or rules)
vocab.note: な-adjective. Japanese ルーズ (from "loose") is of habits: {時間|じかん}にルーズ.
vocab.example: {彼|かれ}は{時間|じかん}にルーズで、いつも{待|ま}ち{合|あ}わせに{遅|おく}れる。
vocab.exampleEn: He's lax about time and is always late for appointments.

vocab.note: な-adjective. In Japanese it usually means "sensitive, easily hurt", not "naive".
vocab.example: {彼女|かのじょ}はナイーブな{性格|せいかく}で、{少|すこ}しの{批判|ひはん}にも{傷|きず}つく。
vocab.exampleEn: She's a sensitive soul and is hurt by the slightest criticism.

vocab.note: な-adjective.
vocab.example: {失敗|しっぱい}しても、ポジティブに{考|かんが}えるようにしている。
vocab.exampleEn: Even when I fail, I try to look on the bright side.

vocab.note: な-adjective.
vocab.example: そんなにネガティブにならないで、もう{一度|いちど}やってみよう。
vocab.exampleEn: Don't be so negative; let's try once more.

vocab.note: な-adjective. In Japanese mostly of strict self-discipline: ストイックに{練習|れんしゅう}する.
vocab.example: {彼|かれ}はストイックな{生活|せいかつ}を{送|おく}り、{毎朝|まいあさ}{五時|ごじ}に{起|お}きて{走|はし}る。
vocab.exampleEn: He leads a disciplined life, getting up at five every morning to run.

meanings: doing things at one's own pace (unbothered by others)
vocab.note: な-adjective. Made-in-Japan English; can be praise or mild criticism.
vocab.example: {彼女|かのじょ}はマイペースで、{周|まわ}りが{急|いそ}いでいても{慌|あわ}てない。
vocab.exampleEn: She goes at her own pace and doesn't panic even when everyone around her is rushing.

vocab.note: Also before a noun: カリスマ{店員|てんいん} (a star shop assistant).
vocab.example: {創業者|そうぎょうしゃ}は{強|つよ}いカリスマで{社員|しゃいん}を{引|ひ}っ{張|ぱ}った。
vocab.exampleEn: The founder led the staff through sheer charisma.

vocab.example: ネット{上|じょう}のモラルが{問|と}われている。
vocab.exampleEn: Online morals are being called into question.

vocab.note: Group 3. ます form: {値|あたい}します; て form: {値|あたい}して. With に: {称賛|しょうさん}に{値|あたい}する (praiseworthy), {一読|いちどく}に{値|あたい}する (worth reading). N2 met the pattern 〜に{値|あたい}する; lesson 17 compares it with 〜に{足|た}る.
vocab.example: {彼女|かのじょ}の{勇気|ゆうき}ある{行動|こうどう}は、{称賛|しょうさん}に{値|あたい}する。
vocab.exampleEn: Her brave action deserves praise.

vocab.note: Also {取|と}るに{足|た}らない. A fixed form of lesson 17's 〜に{足|た}りない.
vocab.example: {取|と}るに{足|た}りないことでけんかするのはやめよう。
vocab.exampleEn: Let's stop quarrelling over trivial things.

vocab.note: Written and news: {飢餓|きが}に{苦|くる}しむ{地域|ちいき}. Sounds like {気|き}が (as in {気|き}がする).
vocab.example: {干|かん}ばつが{続|つづ}き、その{地域|ちいき}は{深刻|しんこく}な{飢餓|きが}に{見舞|みま}われた。
vocab.exampleEn: After a long drought, the region was struck by severe famine.

meanings: to hunger for (with に, love or knowledge)
vocab.note: Group 2. ます form: {飢|う}えます; て form: {飢|う}えて. Also figurative: {愛情|あいじょう}に{飢|う}える. Sounds like carried {植|う}える (to plant).
vocab.example: {戦後|せんご}、{多|おお}くの{人|ひと}が{飢|う}えに{苦|くる}しみ、{子|こ}どもたちも{飢|う}えていた。
vocab.exampleEn: After the war, many people suffered from hunger, and the children were starving too.

meanings: pangs of hunger (want of food, written)
vocab.note: Sounds like carried {上|うえ} (on top).
vocab.example: {飢|う}えをしのぐために、{人々|ひとびと}は{草|くさ}の{根|ね}まで{食|た}べた。
vocab.exampleEn: To stave off hunger, people ate even the roots of grass.

vocab.note: Also 〜する. The written word is {餓死|がし}.
vocab.example: {冬|ふゆ}の{山|やま}で{道|みち}に{迷|まよ}い、{危|あや}うく{飢|う}え{死|じ}にするところだった。
vocab.exampleEn: I got lost in the mountains in winter and nearly starved to death.

vocab.note: Also 〜する.
vocab.example: {記録|きろく}によれば、その{年|とし}のききんで{多|おお}くの{農民|のうみん}が{餓死|がし}した。
vocab.exampleEn: According to the records, many farmers starved to death in that year's famine.

meanings: crop famine (food shortage after a bad harvest)
vocab.note: Its second kanji is off the list ({飢饉|ききん}), so the course writes it in kana. {天明|てんめい}の{大|だい}ききん: the Tenmei famine of the 1780s.
vocab.example: {江戸時代|えどじだい}には、{冷害|れいがい}による{大|おお}きなききんが{何度|なんど}も{起|お}きた。
vocab.exampleEn: In the Edo period, great famines caused by cold summers happened several times.

meanings: maltreatment (cruel treatment of a child, an elder or an animal)
vocab.note: Also 〜する; very often passive: {虐待|ぎゃくたい}される.
vocab.example: {動物|どうぶつ}の{虐待|ぎゃくたい}を{防|ふせ}ぐため、{法律|ほうりつ}が{改正|かいせい}された。
vocab.exampleEn: The law was amended to prevent cruelty to animals.

vocab.example: {児童虐待|じどうぎゃくたい}が{疑|うたが}われる{場合|ばあい}は、{児童相談所|じどうそうだんじょ}に{相談|そうだん}できる。
vocab.exampleEn: If child abuse is suspected, you can contact a child guidance centre.

vocab.note: Group 2. ます form: {虐|しいた}げます; て form: {虐|しいた}げて. Mostly passive: {虐|しいた}げられた{人々|ひとびと} (the oppressed).
vocab.example: {長|なが}く{虐|しいた}げられてきた{人々|ひとびと}が、ついに{声|こえ}を{上|あ}げた。
vocab.exampleEn: People who had been oppressed for so long finally raised their voices.

meanings: alienation (being shut out by society or a group)
vocab.note: Also 〜する: {仲間|なかま}から{疎外|そがい}される.
vocab.example: {新|あたら}しい{技術|ぎじゅつ}についていけない{人|ひと}が、{社会|しゃかい}から{疎外|そがい}されてはならない。
vocab.exampleEn: People who can't keep up with new technology must not be shut out of society.

vocab.example: {転校|てんこう}したばかりの{頃|ころ}は、{教室|きょうしつ}で{疎外感|そがいかん}を{覚|おぼ}えた。
vocab.exampleEn: When I'd just changed schools, I felt left out in the classroom.

meanings: estranged (out of touch, of people who were once close)
vocab.note: な-adjective. {疎遠|そえん}になる: to drift apart.
vocab.example: {大学|だいがく}を{出|で}てから、{昔|むかし}の{友人|ゆうじん}とはすっかり{疎遠|そえん}になった。
vocab.exampleEn: Since leaving university, I've completely lost touch with my old friends.

meanings: out of touch (with, knowing little about)
vocab.note: With に: {世事|せじ}に{疎|うと}い, {機械|きかい}に{疎|うと}い.
vocab.example: {父|ちち}は{機械|きかい}に{疎|うと}く、スマートフォンの{設定|せってい}はいつも{私|わたし}がしている。
vocab.exampleEn: My father knows little about gadgets, so I always set up his smartphone.

meanings: neglected (given too little care, of a duty)
vocab.note: な-adjective. Often printed 疎か, but that reading isn't jōyō, so the course writes it in kana. Mostly 〜をおろそかにする.
vocab.example: {部活|ぶかつ}に{夢中|むちゅう}で、{勉強|べんきょう}がおろそかになっている。
vocab.exampleEn: I'm so caught up in club activities that I'm neglecting my studies.

meanings: rural depopulation (the process of an area losing its people)
vocab.note: Carried {過疎|かそ} now takes kanji (疎). Also 〜する.
vocab.example: {過疎化|かそか}が{進|すす}み、{村|むら}の{小学校|しょうがっこう}は{閉校|へいこう}になった。
vocab.exampleEn: As depopulation advanced, the village primary school closed.

vocab.note: Carried {孤独|こどく} and {孤立|こりつ} now take kanji (孤).
vocab.example: {都市部|としぶ}では、{高齢者|こうれいしゃ}の{孤独死|こどくし}が{問題|もんだい}になっている。
vocab.exampleEn: In urban areas, old people dying alone has become a problem.

meanings: isolated and helpless (with no one to turn to)
vocab.note: Four-character compound: {孤立|こりつ} (isolation) + {無援|むえん} (no help).
vocab.example: {助|たす}けを{求|もと}める{相手|あいて}もなく、{彼女|かのじょ}は{孤立無援|こりつむえん}だった。
vocab.exampleEn: With no one to turn to for help, she was completely on her own.

meanings: to be lopsided (lean to one side, be biased)
vocab.note: Group 1. ます form: {偏|かたよ}ります; て form: {偏|かたよ}って. {偏|かたよ}った{食事|しょくじ} (an unbalanced diet), {意見|いけん}が{偏|かたよ}る. Causative {偏|かたよ}らせる is possible but rare.
vocab.example: {報道|ほうどう}が{一方|いっぽう}の{意見|いけん}に{偏|かたよ}らないよう、{注意|ちゅうい}が{必要|ひつよう}だ。
vocab.exampleEn: Care is needed so that the coverage doesn't lean toward one side.

meanings: picky eating (an unbalanced diet from likes and dislikes)
vocab.note: Also 〜する.
vocab.example: {子|こ}どもの{偏食|へんしょく}に{悩|なや}む{親|おや}は{多|おお}い。
vocab.exampleEn: Many parents worry about their children being picky eaters.

vocab.note: {偏向報道|へんこうほうどう}: biased coverage. Sounds like carried へんこう (a change of plans).
vocab.example: その{番組|ばんぐみ}は{偏向|へんこう}していると{批判|ひはん}された。
vocab.exampleEn: The programme was criticized as biased.

meanings: standard score (a school-exam ranking score, mean 50)
vocab.note: Japanese exam culture ranks students and schools by it.
vocab.example: {偏差値|へんさち}だけで{志望校|しぼうこう}を{決|き}めるのは{考|かんが}えものだ。
vocab.exampleEn: Choosing a school by its standard score alone is questionable.

vocab.note: Often printed 禍, but that reading of lesson 18's 禍 isn't jōyō; 災 (N2) carries the jōyō reading. {口|くち}は{災|わざわ}いの{門|もん}: careless words invite trouble (a proverb).
vocab.example: {軽|かる}い{一言|ひとこと}が{災|わざわ}いを{招|まね}くこともある。
vocab.exampleEn: A careless word can sometimes bring disaster.

meanings: ravages of war (destruction caused by war)
vocab.example: {戦禍|せんか}を{逃|のが}れた{人々|ひとびと}が、{国境|こっきょう}を{越|こ}えて{避難|ひなん}している。
vocab.exampleEn: People fleeing the ravages of war are crossing the border to safety.

meanings: root of future trouble (a source of lasting harm, written)
vocab.note: {禍根|かこん}を{残|のこ}す: to leave a legacy of trouble.
vocab.example: {十分|じゅうぶん}な{話|はな}し{合|あ}いなしに{決|き}めれば、{将来|しょうらい}に{禍根|かこん}を{残|のこ}すだろう。
vocab.exampleEn: Deciding without proper discussion would sow the seeds of future trouble.

vocab.note: Also 〜する: {生活|せいかつ}に{困窮|こんきゅう}する. {生活困窮者|せいかつこんきゅうしゃ}: people in financial hardship.
vocab.example: {物価|ぶっか}の{上昇|じょうしょう}で、{生活|せいかつ}に{困窮|こんきゅう}する{家庭|かてい}が{増|ふ}えている。
vocab.exampleEn: With rising prices, more households are struggling to get by.

meanings: constricting (too tight, of space or clothes)
vocab.note: な-adjective.
vocab.example: {規則|きそく}が{多|おお}すぎて、{窮屈|きゅうくつ}な{職場|しょくば}だ。
vocab.exampleEn: There are too many rules; it's a stifling place to work.

meanings: predicament (a tight corner, hard to escape)
vocab.note: {窮地|きゅうち}に{立|た}たされる / {陥|おちい}る.
vocab.example: {主力|しゅりょく}{選手|せんしゅ}のけがで、チームは{窮地|きゅうち}に{立|た}たされた。
vocab.exampleEn: With its key player injured, the team found itself in a tight corner.

vocab.note: {窮状|きゅうじょう}を{訴|うった}える. Sounds like carried {球場|きゅうじょう} (ballpark).
vocab.example: {農家|のうか}の{人々|ひとびと}は、{肥料|ひりょう}{価格|かかく}の{高騰|こうとう}による{窮状|きゅうじょう}を{訴|うった}えた。
vocab.exampleEn: Farmers spoke out about their plight caused by soaring fertilizer prices.

meanings: very poor (of conditions, far below standard)
vocab.note: な-adjective. {劣悪|れつあく}な{環境|かんきょう} / {労働条件|ろうどうじょうけん}.
vocab.example: {劣悪|れつあく}な{労働条件|ろうどうじょうけん}のもとで、{多|おお}くの{人|ひと}が{働|はたら}かされていた。
vocab.exampleEn: Many people were made to work under dreadful conditions.

vocab.note: Group 1. ます form: {劣|おと}ります; て form: {劣|おと}って. 〜に{劣|おと}る / 〜より{劣|おと}る; 〜に{勝|まさ}るとも{劣|おと}らない (every bit as good as).
vocab.example: {値段|ねだん}は{安|やす}いが、{品質|ひんしつ}は{有名|ゆうめい}ブランドに{勝|まさ}るとも{劣|おと}らない。
vocab.exampleEn: It's cheap, but its quality is every bit as good as the famous brands'.

meanings: deterioration (of materials or quality over time)
vocab.note: Also 〜する.
vocab.example: {古|ふる}いゴムは{劣化|れっか}して、ひびが{入|はい}りやすい。
vocab.exampleEn: Old rubber deteriorates and cracks easily.

meanings: superiority or inferiority (which is better and which worse)
vocab.note: {優劣|ゆうれつ}をつける (to rank); {優劣|ゆうれつ}つけがたい (hard to choose between).
vocab.example: どちらの{作品|さくひん}もすばらしく、{優劣|ゆうれつ}をつけがたい。
vocab.exampleEn: Both works are wonderful; it's hard to say which is better.

meanings: disadvantage (being on the losing side, in a contest)
vocab.note: Opposite: {優勢|ゆうせい}.
vocab.example: {前半|ぜんはん}は{劣勢|れっせい}だったが、{後半|こうはん}に{逆転|ぎゃくてん}した。
vocab.exampleEn: We were behind in the first half but turned it around in the second.

meanings: decline (of a town, an industry or a culture: losing strength over time)
vocab.note: Also 〜する: {産業|さんぎょう}が{衰退|すいたい}する.
vocab.example: {大型店|おおがたてん}の{進出|しんしゅつ}で、{駅前|えきまえ}の{商店街|しょうてんがい}は{衰退|すいたい}した。
vocab.exampleEn: With big stores moving in, the shopping street in front of the station declined.

meanings: to weaken (with age or time, of strength or power)
vocab.note: Group 2. ます form: {衰|おとろ}えます; て form: {衰|おとろ}えて.
vocab.example: {年|とし}を{取|と}って{体力|たいりょく}が{衰|おとろ}えても、{好奇心|こうきしん}は{衰|おとろ}えない。
vocab.exampleEn: Even as age weakens the body, curiosity doesn't fade.

vocab.example: {最近|さいきん}、{目|め}の{衰|おとろ}えを{感|かん}じるようになった。
vocab.exampleEn: Lately I've started to notice my eyesight weakening.

vocab.note: Also 〜する: {衰弱|すいじゃく}した{犬|いぬ} (a weak, emaciated dog).
vocab.example: {保護|ほご}された{子猫|こねこ}は、ひどく{衰弱|すいじゃく}していた。
vocab.exampleEn: The rescued kitten was terribly weak.

meanings: decrepitude (old age as a cause of death)
vocab.note: {老衰|ろうすい}で{亡|な}くなる: to die of old age.
vocab.example: {祖母|そぼ}は{九十八歳|きゅうじゅうはっさい}で、{老衰|ろうすい}のため{静|しず}かに{息|いき}を{引|ひ}き{取|と}った。
vocab.exampleEn: My grandmother passed away peacefully of old age at ninety-eight.

meanings: rise and fall (of a nation or a family)
vocab.note: {栄枯盛衰|えいこせいすい}: the rise and fall of fortune (four-character compound).
vocab.example: この{本|ほん}は、{一|ひと}つの{商家|しょうか}の{三百年|さんびゃくねん}にわたる{盛衰|せいすい}を{描|えが}いている。
vocab.exampleEn: This book traces the rise and fall of a merchant house over three hundred years.

vocab.note: {長寿|ちょうじゅ}{社会|しゃかい}, {長寿|ちょうじゅ}{番組|ばんぐみ} (a long-running programme). Carried {寿命|じゅみょう} (lifespan) now takes kanji.
vocab.example: {日本|にほん}は{世界|せかい}でも{有数|ゆうすう}の{長寿|ちょうじゅ}{国|こく}だ。
vocab.exampleEn: Japan is one of the countries with the longest life expectancy in the world.

vocab.example: {医療|いりょう}の{進歩|しんぽ}により、{平均寿命|へいきんじゅみょう}は{大|おお}きく{延|の}びた。
vocab.exampleEn: Thanks to advances in medicine, life expectancy has risen greatly.

vocab.note: Written on wedding gifts and envelopes: {寿|ことぶき}. {寿退社|ことぶきたいしゃ}: leaving one's job on marriage (old-fashioned).
vocab.example: お{祝|いわ}いの{袋|ふくろ}には「{寿|ことぶき}」と{書|か}かれていた。
vocab.exampleEn: The gift envelope had the character for "congratulations" written on it.

vocab.note: Also 〜する: {言論|げんろん}を{抑圧|よくあつ}する.
vocab.example: {長|なが}い{抑圧|よくあつ}の{時代|じだい}を{経|へ}て、{人々|ひとびと}はようやく{自由|じゆう}を{手|て}にした。
vocab.exampleEn: After a long era of oppression, the people finally won their freedom.

meanings: curbing (keeping costs or growth in check)
vocab.note: Also 〜する: {物価|ぶっか}の{上昇|じょうしょう}を{抑制|よくせい}する.
vocab.example: {感染|かんせん}の{拡大|かくだい}を{抑制|よくせい}するため、{様々|さまざま}な{対策|たいさく}が{取|と}られた。
vocab.exampleEn: Various measures were taken to keep the spread of infection in check.

meanings: to hold down (keep in check, of costs, feelings or a rise)
vocab.note: Group 2. ます form: {抑|おさ}えます; て form: {抑|おさ}えて. {費用|ひよう}を{抑|おさ}える, {怒|いか}りを{抑|おさ}える. Different from {押|お}さえる (to press with the hand).
vocab.example: {彼|かれ}は{怒|いか}りを{抑|おさ}えて、{冷静|れいせい}に{話|はな}し{続|つづ}けた。
vocab.exampleEn: He held back his anger and went on speaking calmly.

vocab.note: Also 〜する. {抑止力|よくしりょく}: deterrent power.
vocab.example: {防犯|ぼうはん}カメラには、{犯罪|はんざい}を{抑止|よくし}する{効果|こうか}があるとされる。
vocab.exampleEn: Security cameras are said to have the effect of deterring crime.

meanings: intonation (the rise and fall of the voice)
vocab.example: {抑揚|よくよう}のない{話|はな}し{方|かた}では、{聞|き}き{手|て}は{眠|ねむ}くなる。
vocab.exampleEn: Speaking in a monotone makes listeners sleepy.

vocab.note: Its second kanji ({鬱|うつ}) is off the list, so the course writes it in kana. Everyday speech uses うつ{病|びょう} (depression, the illness).
vocab.example: {長時間労働|ちょうじかんろうどう}が{続|つづ}き、{抑|よく}うつの{症状|しょうじょう}が{出|で}る{人|ひと}もいる。
vocab.exampleEn: With long working hours going on and on, some people develop symptoms of depression.

vocab.note: Also 〜する: {可能性|かのうせい}を{排除|はいじょ}しない (not to rule out).
vocab.example: {異|こと}なる{意見|いけん}を{排除|はいじょ}する{組織|そしき}は、やがて{行|い}き{詰|づ}まる。
vocab.exampleEn: An organization that shuts out different opinions will eventually reach a dead end.

vocab.note: Also 〜する: {二酸化炭素|にさんかたんそ}の{排出|はいしゅつ}{量|りょう}. Carried にさんかたんそ now takes kanji (lesson 20).
vocab.example: {工場|こうじょう}からの{排出|はいしゅつ}ガスは{厳|きび}しく{規制|きせい}されている。
vocab.exampleEn: Emissions from factories are strictly regulated.

vocab.note: な-adjective. {排他的経済水域|はいたてきけいざいすいいき}: exclusive economic zone.
vocab.example: {古|ふる}い{村|むら}には、よそ{者|もの}に{排他的|はいたてき}なところもあった。
vocab.exampleEn: Old villages could be closed to outsiders.

vocab.example: {大通|おおどお}りは{排気|はいき}ガスで{空気|くうき}が{悪|わる}い。
vocab.exampleEn: The air along the main road is bad because of exhaust fumes.

vocab.note: {生活排水|せいかつはいすい}: household waste water.
vocab.example: {大雨|おおあめ}のあと、{排水|はいすい}が{追|お}いつかず{道路|どうろ}が{冠水|かんすい}した。
vocab.exampleEn: After the heavy rain, the drains couldn't cope and the road flooded.

vocab.example: {落|お}ち{葉|ば}が{排水溝|はいすいこう}に{詰|つ}まっていた。
vocab.exampleEn: Fallen leaves were blocking the drain.

meanings: rift (a gap between people or groups)
vocab.note: Literal ditch or groove, and figurative: {両国|りょうこく}の{間|あいだ}の{溝|みぞ} (the rift between the two countries).
vocab.example: {話|はな}し{合|あ}いを{重|かさ}ねたが、{労使|ろうし}の{溝|みぞ}は{埋|う}まらなかった。
vocab.exampleEn: Despite repeated talks, the rift between management and workers wasn't bridged.

meanings: inner conflict (being torn between two wishes)
vocab.note: Also 〜する. Originally kudzu ({葛|くず}) and wisteria ({藤|ふじ}): two climbers tangled together.
vocab.example: {親|おや}の{期待|きたい}と{自分|じぶん}の{夢|ゆめ}の{間|あいだ}で、{彼|かれ}は{長|なが}く{葛藤|かっとう}した。
vocab.exampleEn: He was long torn between his parents' expectations and his own dream.

vocab.note: {葛湯|くずゆ} (a hot kudzu-starch drink), {葛餅|くずもち}. Different from くず (rubbish), whose kanji is off the list.
vocab.example: {風邪|かぜ}のときは、{祖母|そぼ}がよく{葛湯|くずゆ}を{作|つく}ってくれた。
vocab.exampleEn: When I had a cold, my grandmother would make me hot kudzu drink.

meanings: to devote oneself (do everything one can, for someone)
vocab.note: Group 1. ます form: {尽|つ}くします; て form: {尽|つ}くして. {全力|ぜんりょく}を{尽|つ}くす, {手|て}を{尽|つ}くす (try every means), {社会|しゃかい}に{尽|つ}くす. ます stem + {尽|つ}くす: to do completely ({食|た}べ{尽|つ}くす).
vocab.example: {医師|いし}たちは{最後|さいご}まで{手|て}を{尽|つ}くした。
vocab.exampleEn: The doctors did everything they could to the very end.

meanings: to run out (be used up, of supplies or patience)
vocab.note: Group 2. ます form: {尽|つ}きます; て form: {尽|つ}きて. 〜に{尽|つ}きる: comes down to ({感謝|かんしゃ}の{一言|ひとこと}に{尽|つ}きる). {愛想|あいそ}が{尽|つ}きる: to be fed up with.
vocab.example: {話題|わだい}が{尽|つ}きることなく、{気|き}づけば{夜中|よなか}になっていた。
vocab.exampleEn: We never ran out of things to talk about, and before we knew it, it was midnight.

meanings: efforts (formal, exerting oneself for a cause)
vocab.note: Also 〜する; ご{尽力|じんりょく} in thanks: ご{尽力|じんりょく}いただき、ありがとうございました.
vocab.example: {多|おお}くの{方|かた}のご{尽力|じんりょく}により、{大会|たいかい}は{無事|ぶじ}{終了|しゅうりょう}した。
vocab.exampleEn: Thanks to the efforts of many people, the tournament ended without a hitch.

vocab.note: な-adjective.
vocab.example: {理不尽|りふじん}な{要求|ようきゅう}には、はっきり{断|ことわ}るべきだ。
vocab.exampleEn: You should clearly refuse unreasonable demands.

meanings: pay and conditions (how one is treated at work)
vocab.note: {待遇|たいぐう}を{改善|かいぜん}する; {待遇|たいぐう}{表現|ひょうげん} (expressions of politeness, in linguistics).
vocab.example: {介護職|かいごしょく}の{待遇|たいぐう}を{改善|かいぜん}しなければ、{人手不足|ひとでぶそく}は{解消|かいしょう}しない。
vocab.exampleEn: Unless care workers' pay and conditions improve, the labour shortage won't be resolved.

vocab.note: Also a な-adjective: {不遇|ふぐう}な{時代|じだい}.
vocab.example: その{画家|がか}は{生前|せいぜん}{不遇|ふぐう}で、{死後|しご}に{評価|ひょうか}された。
vocab.exampleEn: The painter was unrecognized in life and acclaimed only after death.

vocab.example: {似|に}た{境遇|きょうぐう}で{育|そだ}った{二人|ふたり}は、すぐに{打|う}ち{解|と}けた。
vocab.exampleEn: Having grown up in similar circumstances, the two of them soon became close.

vocab.note: Also 〜する: {子育|こそだ}て{世帯|せたい}を{優遇|ゆうぐう}する.
vocab.example: {若|わか}い{世帯|せたい}への{家賃|やちん}の{優遇|ゆうぐう}で、{町|まち}の{人口|じんこう}は{少|すこ}し{増|ふ}えた。
vocab.exampleEn: Thanks to favourable rents for young households, the town's population grew a little.

vocab.note: Also 〜する; often passive: {冷遇|れいぐう}される.
vocab.example: {彼|かれ}は{社長|しゃちょう}に{意見|いけん}したため、{社内|しゃない}で{冷遇|れいぐう}された。
vocab.exampleEn: Because he spoke up to the president, he was given the cold shoulder at work.

vocab.note: Also 〜する: {事故|じこ}に{遭遇|そうぐう}する, クマに{遭遇|そうぐう}する. 遭 is lesson 23's kanji.
vocab.example: {登山中|とざんちゅう}にクマと{遭遇|そうぐう}したら、{背中|せなか}を{見|み}せずにゆっくり{離|はな}れること。
vocab.exampleEn: If you encounter a bear while climbing, move away slowly without turning your back.

meanings: prime of life (roughly the thirties to fifties)
vocab.example: {壮年|そうねん}{期|き}の{働|はたら}き{盛|ざか}りの{人|ひと}たちが、{過労|かろう}で{倒|たお}れている。
vocab.exampleEn: People in the prime of their working lives are collapsing from overwork.

meanings: grand (on a magnificent scale, of a view or plan)
vocab.note: な-adjective.
vocab.example: {彼|かれ}らは{百年後|ひゃくねんご}を{見据|みす}えた{壮大|そうだい}な{計画|けいかく}を{立|た}てた。
vocab.exampleEn: They drew up a grand plan looking a hundred years ahead.

vocab.note: な-adjective. {悲壮|ひそう}な{決意|けつい}: a grim, desperate resolve.
vocab.example: {選手|せんしゅ}たちは{悲壮|ひそう}な{決意|けつい}で{最後|さいご}の{試合|しあい}に{臨|のぞ}んだ。
vocab.exampleEn: The players went into the last match with grim determination.

meanings: fierce (extreme and dramatic, of a fight or an end)
vocab.note: な-adjective.
vocab.example: {両者|りょうしゃ}は{最後|さいご}まで{壮絶|そうぜつ}な{戦|たたか}いを{繰|く}り{広|ひろ}げた。
vocab.exampleEn: The two sides fought a fierce battle to the very end.

vocab.example: {安全対策|あんぜんたいさく}の{盲点|もうてん}を{突|つ}かれた{事件|じけん}だった。
vocab.exampleEn: It was an incident that exploited a blind spot in the safety measures.

vocab.note: Also figurative: {恋|こい}は{盲目|もうもく} (love is blind).
vocab.example: {盲目|もうもく}のピアニストの{演奏|えんそう}に、{会場|かいじょう}は{感動|かんどう}に{包|つつ}まれた。
vocab.exampleEn: The hall was moved by the blind pianist's performance.

vocab.example: {盲導犬|もうどうけん}を{連|つ}れた{人|ひと}の{入店|にゅうてん}を{断|ことわ}ってはいけない。
vocab.exampleEn: Shops must not refuse entry to people with guide dogs.

meanings: setback (a defeat that breaks one's resolve)
vocab.note: Also 〜する: {夢|ゆめ}に{挫折|ざせつ}する.
vocab.example: {若|わか}い{頃|ころ}の{挫折|ざせつ}が、{今|いま}の{私|わたし}を{作|つく}った。
vocab.exampleEn: The setbacks of my youth made me who I am.

vocab.note: Group 1. ます form: くじきます; て form: くじいて. Often printed 挫く, but that reading isn't jōyō (挫 is only ザ): kana in this course. {足|あし}をくじく (to sprain an ankle), {出鼻|でばな}をくじく (to dampen someone's enthusiasm at the start).
vocab.example: {階段|かいだん}で{足|あし}をくじいて、{一週間|いっしゅうかん}{歩|ある}けなかった。
vocab.exampleEn: I sprained my ankle on the stairs and couldn't walk for a week.

vocab.note: Also 〜する. 頓 is lesson 19's kanji.
vocab.example: {資金不足|しきんぶそく}で、{計画|けいかく}は{途中|とちゅう}で{頓挫|とんざ}した。
vocab.exampleEn: For lack of funds, the plan collapsed halfway.

vocab.note: Also 〜する. {傍観者|ぼうかんしゃ}: a bystander.
vocab.example: いじめを{傍観|ぼうかん}することも、{加害|かがい}の{一部|いちぶ}だと{言|い}われる。
vocab.exampleEn: It's said that standing by while bullying happens is also part of the harm.

vocab.note: {路傍|ろぼう}の{石|いし}: a stone by the road (something no one notices).
vocab.example: {路傍|ろぼう}に{咲|さ}く{小|ちい}さな{花|はな}に、{足|あし}を{止|と}めた。
vocab.exampleEn: I stopped at a little flower blooming by the roadside.

vocab.note: Also figurative: お{金|かね}の{奴隷|どれい}.
vocab.example: {奴隷|どれい}{制度|せいど}が{廃止|はいし}されたのは、それほど{昔|むかし}のことではない。
vocab.exampleEn: It wasn't so very long ago that slavery was abolished.

meanings: miser (someone who lives only for money)
vocab.example: {彼|かれ}は{守銭奴|しゅせんど}と{呼|よ}ばれたが、{死後|しご}に{全財産|ぜんざいさん}を{寄付|きふ}していたことがわかった。
vocab.exampleEn: He was called a miser, but after his death it emerged that he had donated his entire fortune.

vocab.note: Casual and often rude of people: いいやつ (a good guy), あいつ / こいつ. Also "thing": もっと{安|やす}いやつ. Often printed 奴, but that reading isn't jōyō: kana in this course.
vocab.example: {彼|かれ}は{口|くち}は{悪|わる}いけど、{根|ね}はいいやつだよ。
vocab.exampleEn: He's got a sharp tongue, but he's a good guy at heart.

vocab.note: Also 〜する: {地域|ちいき}に{奉仕|ほうし}する. {奉仕活動|ほうしかつどう}: community service.
vocab.example: {毎月|まいつき}{一回|いっかい}、{公園|こうえん}の{清掃|せいそう}{奉仕|ほうし}に{参加|さんか}している。
vocab.exampleEn: Once a month, I take part in volunteer clean-ups of the park.

meanings: service (as an apprentice or servant, historical)
vocab.note: Historical: {奉公|ほうこう}に{出|で}る (to go into service). Sounds like carried {方向|ほうこう} (direction) and lesson 25's {芳香|ほうこう}.
vocab.example: {江戸時代|えどじだい}には、{十歳|じゅっさい}ほどで{商家|しょうか}に{奉公|ほうこう}に{出|で}る{子|こ}どもも{多|おお}かった。
vocab.exampleEn: In the Edo period, many children went into service with merchant houses at about ten.

vocab.note: Also 〜する: {党|とう}が{分裂|ぶんれつ}する, {細胞分裂|さいぼうぶんれつ}.
vocab.example: {方針|ほうしん}をめぐる{対立|たいりつ}で、{党|とう}は{二|ふた}つに{分裂|ぶんれつ}した。
vocab.exampleEn: The dispute over policy split the party in two.

meanings: to rip (split apart, of cloth or wood)
vocab.note: Group 2. ます form: {裂|さ}けます; て form: {裂|さ}けて. {口|くち}が{裂|さ}けても{言|い}わない: I'd never tell, not for anything. Sounds like carried {避|さ}ける (to avoid).
vocab.example: {強風|きょうふう}でテントが{裂|さ}けてしまった。
vocab.exampleEn: The strong wind ripped the tent.

vocab.note: Group 1. ます form: {裂|さ}きます; て form: {裂|さ}いて. {二人|ふたり}の{仲|なか}を{裂|さ}く (to come between two people), Not to be confused with {割|さ}く (to spare time: {時間|じかん}を{割|さ}く). Sounds like carried {咲|さ}く (to bloom).
vocab.example: {布|ぬの}を{細|ほそ}く{裂|さ}いて、{包帯|ほうたい}の{代|か}わりにした。
vocab.exampleEn: I tore the cloth into thin strips and used them as bandages.

vocab.note: Also 〜する: {交渉|こうしょう}が{決裂|けつれつ}する.
vocab.example: {賃上|ちんあ}げをめぐる{交渉|こうしょう}は{決裂|けつれつ}した。
vocab.exampleEn: The negotiations over a pay rise broke down.

meanings: fissure (a crack in a wall or road)
vocab.note: 亀 is lesson 2's kanji. Literal ({壁|かべ}に{亀裂|きれつ}が{入|はい}る) and figurative ({関係|かんけい}に{亀裂|きれつ}が{生|しょう}じる).
vocab.example: {地震|じしん}で、{道路|どうろ}に{大|おお}きな{亀裂|きれつ}が{入|はい}った。
vocab.exampleEn: The earthquake left a large crack in the road.

meanings: to fall into (a bad state, written)
vocab.note: Group 1. ます form: {陥|おちい}ります; て form: {陥|おちい}って. A group 1 verb that looks like group 2: {陥|おちい}らない, {陥|おちい}って. {危機|きき}に{陥|おちい}る, {混乱|こんらん}に{陥|おちい}る. Transitive: {陥|おとしい}れる.
vocab.example: {資金|しきん}が{尽|つ}き、{会社|かいしゃ}は{経営|けいえい}{危機|きき}に{陥|おちい}った。
vocab.exampleEn: With its funds exhausted, the company fell into a management crisis.

meanings: defect (a flaw in design or a product)
vocab.note: {欠陥|けっかん}{住宅|じゅうたく} (a badly built house). Sounds like carried {血管|けっかん} (blood vessel).
vocab.example: {製品|せいひん}に{欠陥|けっかん}が{見|み}つかり、メーカーは{回収|かいしゅう}を{始|はじ}めた。
vocab.exampleEn: A defect was found in the product, and the maker started a recall.

meanings: cave-in (subsidence of the ground or a road)
vocab.note: Also 〜する: {道路|どうろ}が{陥没|かんぼつ}する. 没 is lesson 22's kanji.
vocab.example: {水道管|すいどうかん}の{破裂|はれつ}で、{交差点|こうさてん}が{陥没|かんぼつ}した。
vocab.exampleEn: A burst water main made the crossroads cave in.

meanings: food supplies (staple food, as a national resource)
vocab.note: {食糧|しょくりょう} is food as a supply (rice, wheat: {食糧問題|しょくりょうもんだい}, {食糧危機|しょくりょうきき}); {食料|しょくりょう} is food in general. Same reading.
vocab.example: {世界|せかい}の{人口|じんこう}が{増|ふ}え{続|つづ}ければ、{食糧|しょくりょう}{不足|ぶそく}は{避|さ}けられない。
vocab.exampleEn: If the world's population keeps growing, food shortages are unavoidable.

meanings: sustenance (food for body or mind, figurative)
